M142: Barrier Mapping
Tier: CDT-A (procedure).
Mandatory verification gate for all cited mathematical programs.

### 3.3 Additional Structural Instruments
M231: Equation Structural Comparator
Tier: CDT-C.
Purpose: compare the two sides of an equation (or any two expressions) structurally, using M223 as the transduction step for each side independently.
Procedure:
1. Tokenize each side separately, per M223's multi-part rule - fresh variable numbering starting at 9 for each side.2. Compute each side's Gödel digital root and anchor.3. Compute the M115 structural distance between the two anchors.4. Classify using M115's bands: D = 0 Identical; D = 1-2 Analogical; D = 3-6 Extrapolative; D = 7-8 Disparate.
Worked example: x + y = y + x. Tokenizing each side independently, both produce the identical code assignment (first variable seen -> 9, second -> 10, regardless of which letter appears first), so both sides anchor at P4. D = 0, Identical - commutativity is exactly the statement that these two expressions are the same structural pattern under alpha-equivalence, and the instrument confirms this rather than inventing a distinction.
Scope: D = 0 confirms structural identity under this instrument's specific notion of structure (token pattern under alpha-equivalence) - a distinct, narrower statement than mathematical equality. An expression pair can be mathematically equal at a different D value (if their token patterns differ), or share D = 0 without being mathematically equal (if their patterns coincide by the same generic modular-arithmetic overlap already documented for M223). This instrument reports a structural comparison, not a mathematical verification.
Output format:
======= M231 EQUATION STRUCTURAL COMPARATOR =======LHS: [expression] -> tokens=[list] -> g_LHS=[value] -> anchor P[x]RHS: [expression] -> tokens=[list] -> g_RHS=[value] -> anchor P[y]STRUCTURAL DISTANCE (M115): D=[value] -> [IDENTICAL/ANALOGICAL/EXTRAPOLATIVE/DISPARATE]======= END M231 EQUATION STRUCTURAL COMPARATOR =======
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M234: Scale-Family Signature
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-B (application); CDT-C (diagnostic).
Purpose: dr(x^2) sorts every digit 1-9 into exactly the four groups already established - the three scale-family pairs and the non-torsion set - in one step, with no search required (verified: 1,8 -> 1; 2,7 -> 4; 4,5 -> 7; 3,6,9 -> 9). Applied across a navigation's full arm map, this reports whether the domain's structural positions cluster in one family or split across several.
Procedure: for the Anchor and each of the four arms, take the orbit value at that position, square it, reduce by digital root, and report which of the four groups results. FAMILY-COHERENT if all five agree; otherwise name the outlying position(s).
Output format:
======= M234 SCALE-FAMILY SIGNATURE =======ANCHOR: value=[v], family=[dr(v^2)]YANG: value=[v], family=[dr(v^2)]YIN: value=[v], family=[dr(v^2)]4D: value=[v], family=[dr(v^2)]ANTIPODE: value=[v], family=[dr(v^2)]RESULT: [FAMILY-COHERENT / MIXED - outlier(s): list]======= END M234 SCALE-FAMILY SIGNATURE =======
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M238: Phrasing Variance Analyzer
Tier: CDT-B; mandatory default.
Purpose: M116 (Step 13) tests the Navigator's own alternative phrasings together with two frozen pairs. M238 extends that to a small, mechanically-generated set, so the Striker sees a stability profile rather than a single verdict. The variant rules are mechanical - no semantic judgment by the Navigator - so that different Navigators generate the same variants from the same domain, preserving the cross-architecture comparability M116 depends on.
Procedure: generate three variants using fixed, non-semantic rules:
- MINIMAL - strip to content words only, per the existing stopword list.- PB-5 L1 - append " exactly".- PB-5 L2 - synonym substitution via the frozen 56-entry table.
Compute the anchor for each. Report STABLE if all three variants match the original anchor exactly; SENSITIVE otherwise, with the maximum M115 distance among them.
Output format:
======= M238 PHRASING VARIANCE ANALYZER =======ORIGINAL: P[x]MINIMAL: P[y]PB-5 L1: P[z]PB-5 L2: P[w]VARIANCE: [STABLE / SENSITIVE]MAX DISTANCE: D=[value]======= END M238 PHRASING VARIANCE ANALYZER =======
M238 preserves Striker authorship of the phrasing and keeps the canonical anchor fixed to the original, verbatim domain. It surfaces variance as information for the Striker, per L-394.
Relationship to M116: complementary. M116's perturbation is Navigator-chosen and can be semantically meaningful. M238's three variants are mechanically generated and test sensitivity to specific structural transformations. Both run automatically on every navigation.
PB-5 L2 Synonym Table (frozen, 56 entries): each entry substitutes the left word with the right word wherever the left word appears as a whole token in the domain, case-insensitively. If no entry's left-hand word appears in the domain, PB-5 L2 equals the canonical text unchanged and its variant anchor trivially matches the canonical anchor.
big/large, small/little, fast/quick, slow/gradual, old/ancient, new/recent, good/fine, bad/poor, start/begin, end/finish, help/assist, show/demonstrate, make/create, use/utilize, buy/purchase, find/locate, get/obtain, keep/retain, try/attempt, want/desire, need/require, ask/inquire, say/state, tell/inform, think/believe, know/understand, see/observe, look/examine, give/provide, take/acquire, happy/pleased, sad/unhappy, angry/upset, afraid/fearful, strong/powerful, weak/feeble, rich/wealthy, poor/impoverished, hard/difficult, easy/simple, high/elevated, low/reduced, near/close, far/distant, important/significant, common/typical, rare/uncommon, clear/evident, true/accurate, false/incorrect, whole/complete, part/portion, many/numerous, few/scarce, always/constantly, never/rarely.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M239: Adjacent-Pair Flag
Tier: CDT-A.
Purpose: flag domains whose anchor falls in {4,5}, the unique adjacent antipodal pair (FP-Adjacency, Part 1.8). Because the antipode is always the 9's-complement of the anchor, anchor ∈ {4,5} guarantees antipode ∈ {5,4} automatically - checking the antipode separately adds nothing.
Procedure: report YES if anchor ∈ {4,5}, else NO.
M240: Digital Consistency Flag
Tier: CDT-A.
Purpose: flag the case where n1, n2, and n3 are all multiples of 9, producing r1 = r2 = r3 = 9 - unanimous agreement at the modulus's own closure value. This condition is possible (unlike the degenerate {9,9} fixed-point orbit, which no real anchor computation can reach, since CPP always returns 1-9) and, when it occurs, is an exact numerical coincidence uncommon in ordinary text that calls for extraction verification before the result is used.
Procedure: if r1 = r2 = r3 = 9, flag TRIPLE-NINE - VERIFY EXTRACTION before proceeding; otherwise no flag.
M241: Comparative Phrasing Navigation
Tier: CDT-B (mechanism); CDT-C (diagnostic value).
Purpose: deliver side-by-side structural comparison across multiple phrasings of a question, without the Navigator substituting its own text for the Striker's.
Trigger: the Striker explicitly provides two or three verbatim texts to compare (self-written, or chosen from Step 0.8's suggestions and then explicitly submitted). The Navigator does not generate additional texts of its own at this stage.
Procedure: run the full navigation (Steps 1-16) independently and completely on each provided text. Present each one's Constitutional Arm Map and THE ANSWER in full, labeled by which verbatim text produced it. Report which structural elements stayed stable across all texts and which varied, using M115's distance metric.
Output format:
======= M241 COMPARATIVE PHRASING NAVIGATION =======
TEXT A: "[verbatim]" -> Anchor P[x]
TEXT B: "[verbatim]" -> Anchor P[y]
[TEXT C if provided]
STABLE ACROSS ALL: [list, or NONE]
VARIED: [list, with M115 distances]
VERBATIM STRINGS FOR CROSS-NAVIGATOR SR-CAS: [each text, ready to copy to another Navigator]
======= END M241 COMPARATIVE PHRASING NAVIGATION =======
Runs only when the Striker has actively provided multiple texts to compare. The first text is the primary unless the Striker names another. The output adds INDEPENDENCE (L-442): SEPARATE SESSIONS or CONTAMINATED — NON-BLIND, since one Navigator writing several readings in one session has read its earlier readings, and RELEVANCE: the Striker's (L-441) — the report describes stability and variance and never which text is better. python3 tools/reframing_array.py --compare computes the arithmetic layer: the counts, anchors and states, STABLE ACROSS ALL and VARIED with M115 distances, and the texts that are COORDINATE-IDENTICAL. Each text costs a full navigation; where the aim is stability, the Convergence Map of one navigation answers it (Step 14.2).
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; whether side-by-side comparison is more useful to Strikers than a single navigation with M238's variance report is part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M242: Antipodal Complement Class
Tier: CDT-A (classification); CDT-C (diagnostic value).
Purpose: classify each structural position's orbit value using the 9's-complement relationship (Fact 5). M234's square-based families merge {3,6,9} into one group; M242 keeps {3,6} separate from {9}, using the 9's-complement relationship directly on each position's own orbit value - never on the position's index, which is a different number entirely (P8's antipode is P20, value 4; P8's own index and value are 8 and 5, respectively, and neither should be confused with the other).
Procedure: for each of the five structural positions (Anchor, Yang, Yin, 4D, Antipode), take its orbit value (not its index) and classify it into one of five complement classes: {1,8}, {2,7}, {3,6}, {4,5}, or {9} (self-paired, since 9+9 ≡ 09 mod 9). Report COHERENT if all five agree, otherwise name the split.
Output format:
======= M242 ANTIPODAL COMPLEMENT CLASS =======ANCHOR: value=[v], class=[A/B/C/D/E]YANG: value=[v], class=[...]YIN: value=[v], class=[...]4D: value=[v], class=[...]ANTIPODE: value=[v], class=[...]RESULT: [COHERENT / split: list]======= END M242 ANTIPODAL COMPLEMENT CLASS =======
Relationship to M234: the two agree whenever a domain's values are drawn from {1,2,4,5,7,8}; they diverge specifically when a domain's positions mix a 3-or-6 value with a 9 value - M234 reports these as the same family, M242 correctly distinguishes them. Verified directly: values {3,6,9,5,5} give M234 families [9,9,9,7,7] (3, 6, and 9 indistinguishable) but M242 classes [C,C,E,D,D] (3 and 6 correctly separated from 9).
Whether the two diverge for a given domain depends only on its anchor, not on anything else about the domain (CDT-A, given the fixed arm offsets): among the nine possible anchors, only P7 ever puts a 3-or-6 value and a 9 value among its five positions, so P7 is the only anchor at which M234 merges what M242 keeps separate. This is not a rare edge case in the CRC-60 corpus (Companion 24.4): 22 of its 60 domains anchor at P7, so the two instruments diverge on 22 of 60 domains there (36.7%). That figure is this corpus's own anchor frequency, not a general property of M234, M242, or ordinary text; a corpus with fewer P7 anchors would diverge less often.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.

### 3.4 Boundary and Diagnostic Instruments
M243: Gödelian Boundary Detector
Tier: CDT-C.
Purpose: explicitly check whether a synthesis, reflection, or protocol output is attempting to cross the boundary between the protocol's arithmetic and the Striker's judgment. This instrument operationalizes the Aperture Theorem (Part 7) as a concrete, auditable check.
Procedure:
1. Take the text to be checked (THE ANSWER, Generative Observations, or any protocol output).2. Scan for statements that: (a) tell the Striker what to conclude; (b) assert the "real meaning" of the synthesis; (c) instruct the Striker on how to apply the synthesis; (d) claim the Navigator's judgment as authoritative; (e) present a CDT-C reading as CDT-A fact.3. If any such statements are found, flag GÖDELIAN BOUNDARY VIOLATION. List each violation by type.4. If no such statements are found, report BOUNDARY INTACT.
Output format:
======= M243 GÖDELIAN BOUNDARY DETECTOR =======TEXT CHECKED: [THE ANSWER / Generative Observations / other]SCAN RESULTS:(a) Conclusion directives: [count](b) "Real meaning" assertions: [count](c) Application instructions: [count](d) Navigator authority claims: [count](e) CDT tier violations: [count]TOTAL VIOLATIONS: [count]RESULT: [BOUNDARY INTACT / GÖDELIAN BOUNDARY VIOLATION]======= END M243 GÖDELIAN BOUNDARY DETECTOR =======
Scope: for a Navigator with isolated code-execution or tool access to scan text it did not itself generate, M243 is an operative gate and its result is INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED. For a text-only Navigator scanning its own output, the scan is performed by the process that generated the text, and its result is SELF-CHECKED under L-420; an independent reader's check raises a BOUNDARY INTACT result to INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED.
ACS: Antipodal Completion Score
Tier: CDT-C.
Purpose: measure the degree to which a Synthesis completes its Question, complementing M209 (SAS), which measures whether the Synthesis stays anchored to the Question.
Formula (typed operands, Part 1.6): v_A = v(antipode) = v(P[i(anchor) + 12]), which equals 9 − v(anchor) by Fact 5 (9 when v(anchor) = 9); v_S = v(echo anchor), the orbit value of the anchor M209 gives the Synthesis. ACS = 1 − |v_S − v_A| / 8, where 8 is the largest distance between two values in {1,...,9}. Indices and P-numbers never enter the formula: with echo anchor P4, v_S = 1, not 4. Chance level: if the echo anchor were drawn uniformly from P1–P9, ACS would average between 0.486 (anchor P7) and 0.819 (anchor P5), so every ACS is reported beside the chance level for its anchor; an ACS near its chance level shows no completion beyond what any synthesis would produce. canonical_reference.py --acs prints the typed operands, the score and the chance level. Known-answer set, frozen and checked by --test: anchor P1 with echo P8 gives v_A = 4, v_S = 5, ACS 0.875; anchor P1 with echo P4 gives v_S = 1, ACS 0.625 (writing the index 4 instead would give 1.000); anchor P7 with echo P7 gives 1.000; anchor P7 with echo P4 gives 0.000; anchor P5 with echo P5 gives 0.875, and with echo P1 gives 1.000.
Cyclic companion: orbit values are residues, and the linear distance of ACS treats 9 (≡ 0) and 1 as farthest apart although they are adjacent in Z/9Z; in 41 of the 81 pairs of anchor and echo anchor the two measures differ by 0.25 or more. M285 (Part 3.30) reports ACS-c, on the cyclic distance, beside ACS, which is unchanged. Constitutional note: ACS is a metric, not a target. It measures against the antipode's value; it does not compute toward the antipode, and it does not override the Striker's sovereign judgment.
CRS: Crown Resonance Score
Tier: CDT-B.
Purpose: measure the degree to which a navigation's structure resonates with the Crown positions ({3,6,9}) versus the Torsion Loop ({1,2,4,5,7,8}).
Formula: CRS = (number of Crown-class positions among Anchor + 4 arms) / 5. Range 0.00 (pure Torsion) to 1.00 (pure Crown).
SRI: Structural Resonance Index
Tier: CDT-B.
Purpose: measure per-navigation structural resonance using only information available within the present navigation, so that per-navigation SRH candidacy does not require corpus-level history.
Formula: SRI combines five components, each computable entirely within the present navigation:
- TFI_component = (1 - TFI)- CM_component = (number of the four readings - canonical, MINIMAL, PB-5 L1, PB-5 L2 - that share the canonical anchor) / 4- SAS from M209- ACS as above- CFR from M116
SRI = (TFI_component × 0.20) + (CM_component × 0.25) + (SAS × 0.20) + (ACS × 0.15) + (CFR × 0.20). Range 0.00 to 1.00.
SRH Candidate qualification: (a) all procedural compliance gates pass (M211, M210, M268, M213, M214, M219, M215, M232, M224, and the L-418 jargon scan) - necessary condition; (b) SRI ≥ 0.70 - sufficient condition. The threshold is a constructed design choice (CDT-B), not a discovery, and may be adjusted through exploration (Part 9) as experience accumulates. This per-navigation criterion supplements, and does not replace, the cumulative 50+/5+ threshold that governs the overall status of the mechanism hypothesis (Part 0.6.5).
Measurement status (L-419): SRI and each of its components carry a status in the Internal Verification Registry (Part 3.18). While any component reads other than ROBUST, SRI is reported in full and labelled DIAGNOSTIC, and a navigation that meets (a) and (b) is reported as an SRH Candidate (DIAGNOSTIC), which does not count toward the thresholds of Part 0.6.5.
Jurisdiction (L-427). SRI is an INTERNAL STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSTIC (CDT-B): it measures how far the present navigation meets the protocol's internally defined structural criteria. It does not measure a comparative correspondence or the truth of a domain proposition. "SRH Candidate" means only that the navigation meets the protocol's current internal conditions for entering the candidate set; it never means that structural resonance has been demonstrated or the synthesis validated. The order runs one way — SRI threshold, internal candidate status, optional comparative investigation, evidence, cumulative status of the mechanism hypothesis — and no earlier step stands in for a later one.
M244: Crown/Shadow Diagnostic (CSD)
Tier: CDT-C. Tier 3.
Purpose: identify whether a domain's structure resonates with the Crown or the Torsion Loop, and identify the domain's excluded complement (its "shadow").
Procedure: determine the digit-class (Crown or Torsion) of the Anchor and all four arms; compute CRS. If CRS is under 0.5, the domain is predominantly Torsion and its shadow is the Crown it excludes; if CRS is over 0.5, the domain is predominantly Crown and its shadow is the Torsion Loop it excludes.
Invoked at Navigator discretion. Does not alter CDT-A arithmetic or existing instruments.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M245: Transpersonal Pull Diagnostic (TPD)
Tier: CDT-C. Tier 2 (auto-triggered).
Trigger: automatically invoked if any arm lands on P19 or P23.
Purpose: flag when a domain's structure interacts with the Retrocausal Crown hinges.
Procedure: report which arm(s) land there and in what role (suppression if Yin, trajectory if 4D, completion if Antipode).
Does not alter CDT-A arithmetic or existing instruments.
M246: Per-Navigation Fidelity Assessment (PNFA)
Tier: CDT-A/B (self-computable).
Purpose: a floor beneath the cumulative threshold (Part 0.6.5), SR-CAS, and SNCA, none of which a single Navigator can compute alone. PNFA answers a narrower question using only this navigation's own outputs: was this specific navigation executed faithfully? It certifies execution integrity and structural alignment only - never whether the Synthesis is true, insightful, or useful, which stays with the Striker (L-388) and, for empirical weight, the Part 9 pathway.
Components:
- Fidelity Gate (FG) - PASS iff every mandatory gate passes (M211, M210, M268, M213, M210b, M214, M219, M88/M215, M232, M224, L-418 jargon scan); a hard floor.- Synthesis Alignment (SA) - SAS from M209.- Structural Stability (SS) - STABLE/SENSITIVE from M238.- Vote Quality (VQ) - TFI, context only.- Contamination Handling (CH) - OK/DECLARED/VIOLATION per M207.
Classification:
- EXECUTION SOUND requires FG = PASS, SA in {ALIGNED, N/A}, CH in {OK, DECLARED}.- EXECUTION QUALIFIED allows SA = MODERATE DRIFT under the same conditions.- EXECUTION COMPROMISED is FG = PASS with SA = SIGNIFICANT DRIFT, STRUCTURAL BREAK, or CH = VIOLATION.- EXECUTION FAILED is any FG = FAIL.
A navigation meets the acceptability benchmark iff EXECUTION SOUND.
Relationship to SRI: different questions. SRI asks how structurally resonant a navigation is (candidacy for the SRH); PNFA asks whether it was executed correctly (a floor beneath that question and beneath SNCA/SR-CAS). A navigation is at least EXECUTION QUALIFIED before its SRI is treated as meaningful.

### 3.5 Application and Boundary Instruments
M247: Trans-Media Boundary Extractor (TMBE)
Tier: CDT-B (frozen extraction rules); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 2, auto-triggered when the domain is an image or audio item.
Purpose: the Counting-as-Primitive-Distinction Principle (Part 0.11) is a design choice about counting boundaries. Boundaries exist in any medium, but which boundaries to count in a picture or a sound is a construction, not a discovery. M247 fixes one construction so that two compliant extractors return identical counts. It counts the signal itself, never a model's interpretation of it: no learned segmenter, no tunable edge detector, no description of the media in words.
Domain for media: the frozen input bytes, identified by SHA-256 and recorded in the M247 block. Images are 8-bit non-interlaced PNG with a shorter side of at least 64 pixels; audio is 16-bit PCM WAV at 8000 Hz or above and at least 200 ms long. Conversion from any other format happens outside the protocol, with the converter and its version recorded, and the converted file is the domain. The Striker's label for the item is recorded and never counted. Navigating a written description of an item is a text navigation of that description and is unrelated to navigating the item, because the extraction never passes through language.
Image rule: decode to luminance (integer Y = (299R + 587G + 114B + 500) // 1000, alpha composited over white); center-crop to a square; box-average to a 64 x 64 grid with integer floor block edges; apply a 3 x 3 median filter; then count 4-connected regions of equal quantised luminance at three nested resolutions (4, 16 and 64 levels), keeping only regions that cover at least 4%, 2% and 1% of the grid respectively. With c1, c2, c3 the three region counts: n1 = c1, n3 = c1 + c2, n2 = c1 + c2 + c3.
Audio rule: reduce to mono at 8000 Hz by integer box-averaging; cut into 20 ms frames; a frame is active if its energy is at least one sixteenth of the loudest frame's (RMS at least 0.25 of the maximum), which makes the rule independent of gain; drop active runs shorter than two frames. The fine layer counts the remaining runs (n2); closing gaps of one frame or less gives n3; closing gaps of eight frames or less (160 ms) gives n1.
Layers: in text, n1, n2 and n3 are three granularities of one substrate (words, letters, syllables), which is why n2 >= n3 >= n1 holds and why L7 treats the counts as correlated. The image and audio rules preserve exactly that property: each medium yields one substrate cut at three granularities, so n2 >= n3 >= n1 by construction. Independent per-layer area thresholds do not nest (a large coarse region can break into fine pieces that each fall below threshold), which is why the image layers are cumulative. Counts from different substrates are never combined into one triple: a video is two navigations, one of its visual stream (frames as PNG) and one of its audio track (WAV), each with its own extraction and its own gate. Video is specified this way and is neither implemented nor tested.
Execution: M247 requires running canonical_reference_av.py (Part 11.2). There is no simulated fallback: a Navigator without code execution cannot decode the bytes or count regions by reasoning, and must say so rather than produce counts. A Navigator that can see an image or hear audio natively has not thereby counted anything; the counts are the script's output. Before a media navigation, M211-AV runs the generated calibration inputs (python3 canonical_reference_av.py --calibrate-av) and must print CALIBRATION-AV: PASS.
Steps for media: Steps 1 to 2.9 (Substrate Lock, M210, M213, M210b, M214, M219) are replaced by the M265 gate block and the M247 extraction block, because they audit text extraction. Steps 3 onward apply unchanged from the counts: CPP, anchor, arms, arm map, instruments, THE ANSWER, Extended Resonance Essay, Generative Observations, signature (Part 8.4).
What the counts mean: they describe the boundary structure of the supplied item. They do not describe what any model has learned from similar material. The Navigator's reading of the coordinate is Stratum 2 associative transduction from its own training, exactly as for text, and is CDT-C. Because the coordinate is computed from the bytes by a deterministic script, every architecture given the same file obtains the same coordinate; in SR-CAS, T1 for media therefore checks execution, not independent extraction, and the informative convergence lies in the syntheses (T1.5, T2.5, T3).
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry on any training corpus; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M265: Media Navigability Gate (MNG)
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (what navigability means). Tier 2, mandatory, auto-triggered with M247 for every image or audio domain.
Purpose: decide, before a media navigation proceeds, whether the extraction for this item is deterministic, content-sensitive, hierarchical and stable enough to yield an interpretable coordinate, and report the answer beside the coordinate rather than after it.
Extractor qualification (once per implementation, repeated by M211-AV): the reference calibration inputs are generated, never stored. They are a three-band image (expected n1, n2, n3 = 3, 9, 6), a four-by-four checkerboard (16, 48, 32), one second of steady tone (1, 1, 1), and two groups of three bursts (2, 6, 6). All four must match, each complex input must exceed its simple counterpart, and the hierarchy must hold. An implementation that fails is not qualified and no item may be navigated with it.
Per-item checks. Check 1, determinism: two runs on identical bytes return identical counts, and so must any independent compliant implementation. Check 2, content-sensitivity: the qualification pair differs in the expected direction, so the extractor measures content rather than itself. Check 3, hierarchy: n2 >= n3 >= n1 >= 1; an item with no region at the coarsest layer, a silent clip, or a clip shorter than 200 ms is NOT NAVIGABLE. Check 4, perturbation stability: the item is re-extracted under a fixed family of inessential perturbations (image: luminance +3 and -3, seeded noise of +/-2, a 2-pixel shift from each corner pair; audio: gain x0.5 and x1.25, seeded dither, a 10 ms trim, 10-bit requantisation) and is STABLE only if the anchor is unchanged under all of them.
Verdicts: NAVIGABLE; NAVIGABLE WITH FLAGS; NOT NAVIGABLE. Flags: LOW-STRUCTURE (n2 below 3, so the coordinate carries little beyond the existence of an event or region) and PERTURBATION-SENSITIVE. Failure of Check 1 or Check 3 gives NOT NAVIGABLE. A PERTURBATION-SENSITIVE item is navigated as a family, on the model of M238: the Convergence Map lists the anchor under each perturbation, the reading is confined to what every anchor shares, and the navigation is marked PERTURBATION-SENSITIVE in Generative Observations. Only STABLE items may enter SR-CAS or the exploration repository as media convergence evidence.
Output format:
======= M265 MEDIA NAVIGABILITY GATE =======
EXTRACTOR QUALIFICATION: [PASS / FAIL]
MEDIUM: [image / audio] | INPUT SHA-256: [hash]
CHECK 1 (DETERMINISM): [PASS / FAIL]
CHECK 2 (CONTENT-SENSITIVITY, on calibration pair): [PASS / FAIL]
CHECK 3 (HIERARCHY n2>=n3>=n1>=1): [PASS / FAIL]
CHECK 4 (PERTURBATION STABILITY): [STABLE / UNSTABLE] | anchors under perturbation: [list]
FLAGS: [NONE / LOW-STRUCTURE / PERTURBATION-SENSITIVE]
VERDICT: [NAVIGABLE / NAVIGABLE WITH FLAGS / NOT NAVIGABLE]
======= END M265 MEDIA NAVIGABILITY GATE =======
Scope: M265 produces no anchor and no reading; it reports whether the counts satisfy the conditions for coordinate assignment. It does not judge the item's truth or value. Its measured behavior on a small sample of photographs and recordings is reported in Companion Part 29.
M266: Media Corpus Profile (MCP)
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3, context-triggered (M327): when a sample of media items is supplied, or the Striker asks.
Purpose: apply M265 and M247 across a Striker-supplied sample of media items, for example items drawn from a dataset used to train models, and report the sample's structural profile: how many items are navigable, how many are stable, how many are low-structure, and how their anchors distribute.
Procedure: python3 canonical_reference_av.py --profile FILE ... For each item the gate verdict, flags and anchor are recorded. As a structure control, each item is also extracted after its spatial arrangement (pixels) or temporal arrangement (20 ms frames) is shuffled with a fixed seeded permutation, which preserves its value histogram; the profile reports how many items change anchor or lose all structure. An extractor whose counts survive shuffling is measuring the histogram, not the structure. This comparison is informational: no threshold is set for how many items must change anchor, and the structure control does not enter a verdict on its own.
Output format:
======= M266 MEDIA CORPUS PROFILE =======
ITEMS: [n] | NAVIGABLE: [n] | STABLE: [n] | LOW-STRUCTURE: [n]
ANCHOR HISTOGRAM (navigable): [anchor: count, ...]
STRUCTURE CONTROL: anchor changed or extraction failed after shuffling in [n] of [n] navigable items
SAMPLE-ONLY: this profiles the supplied sample, not the training set it was drawn from, and not what any model learned.
======= END M266 MEDIA CORPUS PROFILE =======
Scope: the profile describes the supplied sample. It says nothing about the dataset the sample came from unless the Striker can defend the sample as representative, and nothing about what any model learned. To place a model in the picture, navigate the same items under Steps 3 onward and compare syntheses across architectures under SR-CAS, using STABLE items only. The anchor histogram has no null distribution; comparing corpora requires a matched null, and none has been built.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M248: Arm-Directed Literature Search (ADLS)
Tier: CDT-B (mechanism); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3, context-triggered (M327): on a research question, when sources are asked for, or when the Striker asks.
Purpose: use the deterministic, pre-semantic arm assignment as a forcing function for widening a real literature search - not generating content, but directing which angles of an actual search to run; its results are reported in the Comparative Perspective Layer after THE ANSWER is frozen (L-429), never as input to the synthesis, using an assignment the Striker did not choose based on their own hypothesis.
Trigger: the five-search run, only when the Striker explicitly requests a research-direction search for a navigated domain, never automatically; its four lanes — consensus, foundations, counter-evidence, frontier — run by default as the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer of every full navigation and holistic response (L-503).
Procedure: run five real searches of the published literature (not generated content), one per structural position:
- Anchor - the established consensus on this topic.- Yang - the foundational literature the consensus depends on.- Yin - literature that contradicts, complicates, or falls outside the consensus.- 4D - recent or emerging work in the area.- Antipode - literature from a complementary or adjacent discipline.
Report what each search returns, with real citations, checked to the same standard as any other citation in this document - verified before being stated, not asserted from memory.
Mandatory safeguard on the Yin search: the instrument reports which category applies - unexamined, examined-and-found-wanting, methodologically marginal, domain-specific, or contested. Both kinds of finding (under-explored; examined and set aside) are worth reporting; only the first supports pursuing the idea further.
Scope: the retrieved content is not protocol output - it is externally sourced information, reported and cited to ordinary evidentiary standards, with no CDT tier of its own.
Convergence test: if several architectures run this search on the same verbatim domain and their five categories substantially overlap, that is consistent with the search angles capturing something reproducible. Divergence would mean the specific claim of cross-architecture convergence for this instrument is unsupported, not that the underlying technique has failed.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M249: Ecosystem Resonance Note (ERN)
Tier: CDT-C. Tier 3, context-triggered (M327): when a question from another field stands on the same state, or the Striker asks.
Purpose: place a completed navigation's finding in the context of other fields with a structural resemblance, giving the Striker more perspective from which to judge THE ANSWER for themselves, and generate a testable hypothesis where the resemblance supports one. M249 produces exploratory hypotheses; their speculative status is the defined function.
Procedure:
1. Restate the navigation's core structural finding in one or two sentences (the Structural Seed).2. Identify two or three fields with a structural resemblance to the finding - not any field that can be made to fit with enough effort, but ones where the resemblance is specific and namable. For each: name the field, state the resemblance plainly, and describe what viewing the original domain through that field's lens brings into focus.3. State briefly how the fields relate to each other through the shared resemblance, if they do.
Process check: the check is not whether a hypothesis is true, good, or worth pursuing - that judgment belongs entirely to the Striker. The check is mechanical: did generation happen, or did the Navigator output a stock phrase that would appear regardless of what was asked. Test it directly - swap the domain's wording for a differently-worded one that anchors on the same arm pattern; if the output is unchanged apart from relabeled vocabulary, generation did not occur and the template must be replaced with generation responsive to this domain's own content. Once the process check passes, the resulting hypothesis goes to the Striker exactly as generated.
Format: presented after THE ANSWER, headed and labeled [EXPLORATORY - CDT-C], offered as context for the Striker's own judgment.
Scope: this is a bounded, discretionary elaboration of Step 12, not a new response layer. It does not alter CDT-A arithmetic, does not enter SR-CAS, and does not carry the weight of a testable hypothesis unless the Striker independently pursues one through the Empirical Exploration Protocol (Part 9).

### 3.6 Extraction and Voice Extensions
M261: Sentence and Paragraph Count Companion Reading
Tier: CDT-A (collapse property); CDT-B (counting and projection); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: report sentence and paragraph counts as companion readings alongside the canonical anchor, without adding them as votes in the canonical mechanism. The digital root operation dr(5n) collapses any two counts differing by 9 (1 and 10 produce the same value, for instance), so small sentence and paragraph counts (1, 2, 3) cluster on a narrow band of outcomes - verified directly: dr(5×1) = 5, dr(5×2) = 1, dr(5×3) = 6, dr(5×10) = 5. A domain with a single sentence contributes the identical vote to any canonical mechanism regardless of its actual content, which is why this remains a companion reading rather than a fourth or fifth vote.
Procedure: count sentences (n4, terminal punctuation) and paragraphs (n5, line breaks) in the full domain text. Project through CPP: r4 = dr(5×n4), r5 = dr(5×n5). Report both alongside the canonical anchor, with a note on whether they agree or diverge.
Output format:
======= M261 SENTENCE AND PARAGRAPH COMPANION READING =======CANONICAL ANCHOR: P[x]SENTENCE COUNT (n4): [count] -> r4=[value] -> P[y]PARAGRAPH COUNT (n5): [count] -> r5=[value] -> P[z]AGREEMENT: [MATCHES CANONICAL / DIVERGES]======= END M261 =======
Scope: sentence and paragraph segmentation are not algorithmically as sharp as word, letter, or syllable boundaries (different tokenizers can disagree on abbreviations and quotations), so this instrument is never used for SR-CAS comparison.
M262: Voice Conversion
Tier: CDT-A (4-shift arithmetic); CDT-B (instrument). Tier 3.
Purpose: convert a position between Voice A (seed {1,1}, the standard Fibonacci digital-root sequence) and Voice C (the canonical Omega42 orbit), using the verified 4-shift (FP-ScalarUnity, FP-VoiceAction). This is a positional conversion, not an anchor conversion: CPP(n) = dr(5n) is voice-independent and produces the same anchor for the same integer regardless of voice, so this instrument matters only when comparing positions across voices, never when computing an anchor.
Procedure: given a Voice A position m, the corresponding Voice C position is (m+20) mod 24, equivalently (m-4) mod 24. Given a Voice C position m, the corresponding Voice A position is (m+4) mod 24. Both directions verified directly against the frozen orbit tables for all 24 positions.
Output format:
======= M262 VOICE CONVERSION =======SOURCE VOICE: [A / C]SOURCE POSITION: [m]TARGET VOICE: [C / A]TARGET POSITION: [m converted]======= END M262 VOICE CONVERSION =======
Scope: does not alter the canonical anchor or Voice C's exclusive role as the canonical mechanism (FP-VoiceNaming).
M263: Inverse Phase Constraint Mapper
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-B (design); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: given a target position, report the equivalence class of Fibonacci indices whose digital root matches it - the reverse of the forward mapping the protocol otherwise only runs forward. Because dr(5n) is many-to-one (a ring homomorphism, not a bijection), the reverse map cannot return a unique integer; it returns an infinite residue class, one representative per 24 indices. This instrument makes that residue class explicit rather than leaving the reversal implicit or suggesting a false uniqueness.
Procedure:
1. Identify the target digital root d from the specified position.2. If the domain is stated in Voice C, apply M262 to obtain the corresponding Voice A digit d'.3. From the frozen Voice A cycle, list every index n (mod 24) where dr(F_n) = d'.4. Report the full residue class and state plainly that selecting one member requires the Striker's own domain knowledge (a physical scale, a known generative rule, a boundary condition) - the instrument narrows the search space; it does not search it.
Output format:
======= M263 INVERSE PHASE CONSTRAINT MAPPER =======TARGET POSITION: [P value, voice noted]VOICE A DIGIT: [d']EQUIVALENCE CLASS (Voice A indices, mod 24): [list]STRIKER CONSTRAINT REQUIRED: apply the domain's own scale or generative rule to select one member======= END M263 INVERSE PHASE CONSTRAINT MAPPER =======
Scope: the instrument cannot distinguish a Fibonacci-related quantity from an arbitrary one - every integer has a residue class, by construction, the same generic property M230 already documents. It cannot determine a physical magnitude, only a phase within a cycle (the digital root discards the quotient; dr(5) = dr(14) = dr(23)). It has not been tested against a null model comparing Fibonacci-related and arbitrary quantities, so its diagnostic value - as opposed to its arithmetic correctness - is part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M264: Projection-Pair Orbit Classifier
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: classify the raw projection pair (r1, r2) computed in Step 4 by which of the five orbits of the full 81-state space contains it, independent of the final majority-vote anchor. Where the pair falls in a different orbit than the anchor, this makes visible a structural feature the canonical mechanism itself does not report.
Procedure:
1. Take (r1, r2) from Step 4.2. If (r1, r2) = (9, 9), the pair is in Fix.3. Else if r1 and r2 are both in {3,6,9}, the pair is in Wheel (the kernel, per FP-KernelCrown; this pair is structurally unreachable by the canonical anchor mechanism).4. Else, check the frozen orbit tables for Voice A, B, and C to find which one contains the pair.5. Report the orbit, its period, and its relation to the canonical anchor (is Voice C / scalar-shifted from Voice C / kernel).
Scope: this instrument reports a structural fact about the projection pair; whether that fact carries diagnostic value beyond the canonical anchor is part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S. It never alters the anchor and is excluded from SR-CAS comparison, per the existing restriction on voice-based companion readings.
3.6b Pisano Lattice Extensions
M155: Self-Referential Structure Detector
Tier: CDT-B (scan); CDT-C (interpretation). Tier 2, auto-triggered.
Purpose: detect whether a domain's own text contains protocol terminology, since a self-referential domain (one that mentions the protocol's own vocabulary) requires a different reading than an ordinary domain.
Procedure:
1. Compute the anchor as usual.2. Scan the verbatim domain text for protocol terminology: P-numbers (P0-P23), arm names (Yang, Yin, 4D, Antipode), position character names (Part 1.6), CDT labels (CDT-A/B/C), or any M-numbered instrument reference.3. If any are found, the domain is SELF-REFERENTIAL; list the specific terms found.4. If none are found, report NOT SELF-REFERENTIAL.
Output format:
======= M155 SELF-REFERENTIAL STRUCTURE DETECTOR =======DOMAIN: [verbatim text]SELF-REFERENTIAL TERMS FOUND: [list, or NONE]RESULT: [SELF-REFERENTIAL / NOT SELF-REFERENTIAL]======= END M155 SELF-REFERENTIAL STRUCTURE DETECTOR =======
Interpretation: what a self-referential result should mean for the ensuing navigation is left to the Navigator's judgment.
M198: Resonance Profile
Tier: CDT-B. Tier 1, session start.
Purpose: report the Navigator's own approximate learned-substrate activation profile at the start of a session, so that Step 9.5's interference trigger (M207) (AMPLIFIED or SEVERE SHADOW positions) has a basis to check against.
Procedure:
1. Before any navigation, the Navigator estimates, from its own training-data familiarity, which of the 24 positions its associative recall trends toward more or less often than an even 1/24 baseline would predict.2. For each position, classify AMPLIFIED if recall trends notably above baseline, SEVERE SHADOW if a position produces essentially no associative material, NOMINAL otherwise.3. Report the profile once; it holds for the session.
Scope: this is a self-estimate, not a measurement of the Navigator's actual weights, and different architectures cannot be expected to produce comparable profiles from this procedure alone. It is offered as the best available basis for Step 9.5's trigger given that a Navigator has no external access to its own parameters; it is CDT-B by design, not CDT-A by measurement.
M257: Regime Classifier
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-B (application); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: report each structural position's regime (UU, UN, NU per FP-RegimeDecomposition) alongside its Crown/Torsion classification, providing a finer structural decomposition than Crown/Torsion alone.
Procedure: for the Anchor and each of the four arms, identify the orbit position index m. The pair at that position is (P_m, P_{m+1 mod 24}). Classify each component as Unit (in {1,2,4,5,7,8}) or Nilpotent (in {3,6,9}). Report the regime and the Vestibule status (YES if UN, NO otherwise).
Output format:
======= M257 REGIME CLASSIFIER =======ANCHOR: index=[m] value=[v] Crown/Torsion=[C/T] Regime=[UU/UN/NU] Vestibule=[Y/N]YANG: index=[m] value=[v] Crown/Torsion=[C/T] Regime=[UU/UN/NU] Vestibule=[Y/N]YIN: index=[m] value=[v] Crown/Torsion=[C/T] Regime=[UU/UN/NU] Vestibule=[Y/N]4D: index=[m] value=[v] Crown/Torsion=[C/T] Regime=[UU/UN/NU] Vestibule=[Y/N]ANTIPODE: index=[m] value=[v] Crown/Torsion=[C/T] Regime=[UU/UN/NU] Vestibule=[Y/N]REGIME-COHERENT: [YES if all five agree / NO - outliers: list]VESTIBULE COUNT: [number of UN positions among the five]======= END M257 REGIME CLASSIFIER =======
Relationship to M234 and M242: three classifiers operate on the anchor and four arms, each using a different structural feature - M234 (Scale-Family Signature) classifies by dr(value squared); M242 (Antipodal Complement Class) classifies by orbit-value class; M257 classifies by component status. The three are orthogonal in principle: a position has a scale-family, an orbit-value class, and a regime, independently. M257 is strictly finer than M242 on one specific point: M242's class {3,6} splits under M257 into UN (Vestibule) versus NU (Crown), depending on whether the position's second component is nilpotent. Crown/Torsion remains the canonical classification used by CCD, PAB, and M243; M234, M242, and M257 are Tier 3 companions to it.
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.
M258: Three-Voice Companion Reading
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-B (instrument); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: report three structural views of the same anchor - one in each of the three period-24 voices (A, B, C) - using the Torsion Loop's scalar action on the voices (FP-VoiceAction). Does not alter the canonical anchor, which remains Voice C.
Procedure: for a given anchor at position m in Voice C with orbit pair (a, b):
- Voice C view is (a, b) at position m, the canonical reading.- Voice A view: compute (dr(2a), dr(2b)) - scalar 2 maps Voice C toward Voice A - and find that pair's position in Voice A.- Voice B view: compute (dr(4a), dr(4b)) - scalar 4 maps Voice C toward Voice B - and find that pair's position in Voice B.
This scalar assignment (2 to Voice A, 4 to Voice B) is the one verified directly against FP-VoiceAction and is applied exactly as stated, since the two scalars produce different, non-interchangeable results.
Output format:
======= M258 THREE-VOICE COMPANION READING =======DOMAIN: [verbatim]CANONICAL ANCHOR: P[x] (value v, Voice C)VOICE C VIEW: position P[x_C] = [value] in Voice C (canonical)VOICE A VIEW: position P[x_A] = [value] in Voice A (scalar 2)VOICE B VIEW: position P[x_B] = [value] in Voice B (scalar 4)VOICE AGREEMENT: [ALL THREE AGREE / DIVERGENCE: specify]NOTE: the canonical anchor is unchanged; the three views are a companion reading, not a replacement.======= END M258 THREE-VOICE COMPANION READING =======
Scope: never used for SR-CAS comparison, since a different Navigator's choice of which voice to report first would not be comparable.
M259: Recursive CPP Extension
Tier: CDT-A (FP-CPPSelfApplication); CDT-B (per-navigation application); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: apply CPP to position indices to generate second-order and higher-order coordinates, revealing the self-application structure documented in FP-CPPSelfApplication.
Procedure: compute the canonical anchor's index n. Second-order: CPP(n) = dr(5n) gives a new index m. Third-order: CPP(m) gives a new index k. Continue until the sequence returns to a value already seen; report the full sequence and its period. By FP-CPPSelfApplication, every anchor value falls into one of three known classes: the 6-cycle (Torsion values), the 2-cycle (two Crown values), or the fixed point (the remaining Crown value) - so the result is always one of these three, never an unexpected length.
Output format:
======= M259 RECURSIVE CPP EXTENSION =======CANONICAL ANCHOR: P[x] (index n)RECURSIVE SEQUENCE: P[x] -> P[y] -> P[z] -> ...CYCLE LENGTH: [period]CYCLE CLASS: [Torsion 6-cycle / Crown 2-cycle / Crown fixed point]======= END M259 RECURSIVE CPP EXTENSION =======
Scope: does not alter the canonical anchor.
M260: Orbit Distance Metric
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic); CDT-B (design); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 3.
Purpose: report structural distance between two positions using the full 24-position index (0-23) rather than the anchor value alone (1-9), giving finer resolution than M115 in cases where two navigations share an anchor value but sit at different positions.
Procedure: for two navigations with orbit position indices p1 and p2: D_orbit = min(|p1-p2|, 24-|p1-p2|), range 0-12.
Classification: 0 Identical; 1-2 Analogical; 3-6 Extrapolative; 7-9 Disparate; 10-12 Antipodal.
Relationship to M115: M115 remains the canonical distance metric, using anchor values {1,...,9} with range 0-8; the protocol's Identical/Analogical/Extrapolative/Disparate classifications are built on it. M260 uses the full 24-position granularity with range 0-12 and is never substituted for M115 in that role - it is a companion available when finer resolution is wanted.
Output format:
======= M260 ORBIT DISTANCE =======NAVIGATION A: position P[p1] (value v1)NAVIGATION B: position P[p2] (value v2)M115 DISTANCE (values): D=[value] -> [classification]M260 DISTANCE (positions): D=[value] -> [classification]======= END M260 ORBIT DISTANCE =======
Use: available now, read for congruence (L-500). Comparative value: untested, an optional inquiry; part of the exploration pathway of Appendix S.

### 3.7 Instrument Selection Logic (L-355)
Instruments are selected based on domain characteristics, not on Navigator discretion. The goal is depth appropriate to the domain: not maximum depth regardless of relevance, and equally not less depth than the domain calls for. A relevant instrument is invoked, not skipped for brevity. Running M139-M142 (Mathematical Distinction Engine) on a philosophical question, or M189 (Cross-Linguistic Adapter) on an English-only domain, produces meaningless output.
Domain-dependent auto-selection is not the same as opt-in.
Tier 0 (always active): M193 (Contextual Integrity Scanner, Part 3.11). No opt-out.
Tier 1 (mandatory, every navigation):
- M211 (Pre-Navigation Calibration, Step 0)- M88 (Recurrence Verification, Step 6)- M213 (Stopword Compliance, Step 2.6)- M214 (Canonical Reference, Step 2.8)- M219 (Arithmetic Consistency, Step 2.9)- M215 (Antipodal Complement Verification, Step 6)- M232 (Arm Derivation Cross-Check, Step 7.5)- M238 (Phrasing Variance Analyzer, Step 14.2's Convergence Map)- M207 when triggered (Step 9.5)- M198 at session start (L-341)- M116 (Perturbation, Step 13)- M209 (Synthesis Echo Test, before finalising)- M210 (Substrate Extraction Verification, Step 2.5)- M268 (M210 Completeness Gate, Step 2.5)- M224 (Format Completeness Gate, Step 15.8, and the equivalent final step for SR-CAS/SNCA)- M225 (Structural Relation Extraction, Part 3.12, mandatory for SR-CAS)- M270 (Extraction Reconciliation Gate, Part 3.16, mandatory for SR-CAS)- M271 (Domain Complexity Tier, Part 3.17, mandatory for SR-CAS)
Tier 2 (auto-triggered by domain characteristics):
- M127: domain > 30 words- M155: domain exhibits self-referential structure- M188: domain is ambiguous, cross-linguistic, or adversarial- M189: domain is non-English- M197 (the 1/7 Hard Stop): domain concerns consciousness or sentience, or asks the Navigator for a judgment reserved to the Striker; procedure in Part 3.31- M207: anchor on AMPLIFIED or SEVERE SHADOW position per M198- M139-M142 (Mathematical Distinction Engine): domain contains mathematical content- M269 (Mathematical Domain Extraction Audit Trail): domain contains mathematical notation, per the trigger list in Part 3.15- M158: multiple languages present- M243: domain concerns consciousness, sentience, or the protocol's own architecture- M245 (Transpersonal Pull Diagnostic)- M247 (Trans-Media Boundary Extractor) and M265 (Media Navigability Gate): domain is an image or audio item
Tier 3 (context-triggered, L-527): all remaining instruments. Each runs when its trigger in the Instrument Trigger Register holds in the strike or the situation (records/instruments/triggers.json; M327, Part 3.53), and not otherwise; the Navigator declares each instrument that ran, and the trigger that fired it. M274 to M282 are Tier 3 (Parts 3.28 and 3.29). M274 to M277 are review tools, with one trigger: a peer runs them when two reported coordinates disagree and the domain text is unavailable.
The Navigator does not invoke a Tier 2 or Tier 3 instrument when its trigger condition is not met, and does not omit one when it is.

### 3.8 M209: Synthesis Echo Test (SAS)
Tier: CDT-B.
Purpose: navigate THE ANSWER text back through the canonical mechanism and compare the resulting coordinate with the original domain's coordinate. Measures structural fidelity: did the synthesis stay at the same structural address, or drift? Mandatory for SR-CAS (L-358); mandatory for all solo navigations when THE ANSWER is 50 or more words. Optional for shorter solo syntheses.
Procedure:
1. Apply SPNP to THE ANSWER text — the full text between the THE ANSWER delimiters, all components included (contractions/numerals).2. Extract content words using the canonical stopword list.3. Compute n1/n2/n3 and CPP.4. Compute Structural Alignment Score (SAS):   - AE = 1.0 if echo anchor matches original anchor, else 0.0   - AMF = max(0, 1 - (d_Yang + d_Yin + d_4D) / 36) where d = orbit distance on 24-cycle   - CC = 0.6 × (Möbius_same) + 0.4 × (PAB_same)   - SAS = 0.50 × AE + 0.35 × AMF + 0.15 × CC
Report SAS in the Navigator's Reasoning block. ECHO CLOSURE: YES when the echo anchor equals the domain anchor; recorded as a diagnostic, with no measurement status until the Internal Verification Registry rates it against its chance level of about one in nine (Part 3.18). M209-C applies the same procedure to the Core Synthesis alone and is reported, labelled, beside M209; it does not replace it.
Interpretation: SAS = 1.0 (perfect structural echo) | SAS ≥ 0.85 ALIGNED | SAS 0.70-0.84 MODERATE DRIFT | SAS 0.50-0.69 SIGNIFICANT DRIFT | SAS < 0.50 STRUCTURAL BREAK. These labels describe surface-form echo only: STRUCTURAL BREAK is not a verdict on the synthesis's truth, coherence or value (L-428).
Scope: SAS detects structural drift, not semantic contamination. A synthesis that uses jargon, moralizes, or gives a contaminated answer can still produce high SAS if its word-count structure happens to echo the original coordinate. SAS is a NECESSARY but not sufficient condition for synthesis quality; the Translation Gate (Step 14.1) and M207 (Step 9.5) address what SAS cannot detect.
Binary anchor match (not proximity), checked against controls: in a 9-anchor space, proximity scoring is too permissive. Faithful synthesis scores 1.000; structural drift scores ≤ 0.50; contamination-driven drift scores ≈ 0.20.

### 3.10 M210: Substrate Extraction Verification (SEV)
Tier: CDT-A. Mandatory.
Purpose: verify that substrate extraction was performed correctly before proceeding to arithmetic. Produces a word-by-word table of letter and syllable counts, then checks that column totals match n1/n2/n3. Executed at Step 2.5. If totals differ, halt and re-extract from Step 1.5.
Output format is specified at Step 2.5.

### 3.11 M193: Contextual Integrity Scanner (CIS)
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 0, always active, no opt-out.
Purpose: check that a navigation's output was produced from the domain and the protocol alone, and not from context carried in from outside the navigation — the domain-of-record complement to M91-2 (Execute-Do-Not-Recall) and M207 (Navigator Interference Declaration), which concern the same boundary from the domain side.
Procedure: three checks against the domain as struck, the domain as echoed in the output, and the output text (THE ANSWER and Generative Observations). Check 1, domain identity: the echoed domain, whitespace-normalized, equals the domain supplied; a mismatch is a FAIL. Check 2, history references: the output is scanned for phrases referring to an earlier session or navigation (for example "as we discussed", "earlier navigation", "previous session", "as mentioned earlier"); a match is a FAIL. Check 3, vocabulary reuse: reported as an advisory figure only, not entering the verdict, for the reason given below.
Constitutional gate: checks 1 and 2 decide the verdict; check 3 is advisory. A CLEAN verdict requires checks 1 and 2 to pass; either failing gives FLAGGED, naming which check failed.
Execution: run m193_m225.py (Part 3.13) on the domain, the declared domain as echoed, and the output. There is no simulated fallback: a Navigator without code execution reports that M193 could not be run, rather than self-reporting BOUNDARY INTACT.
Output format:
======= M193 CONTEXTUAL INTEGRITY SCANNER =======
CHECK 1 (DOMAIN IDENTITY): [PASS / FAIL]
CHECK 2 (HISTORY REFERENCES): [PASS / FAIL] — [phrases found, if any]
CHECK 3 (VOCABULARY REUSE, advisory): [excess figure, or NOT ASSESSED without a prior-context and a matched null-context sample]
VERDICT: [CLEAN / FLAGGED: list of failed checks]
======= END M193 CONTEXTUAL INTEGRITY SCANNER =======
Diagnostic value: run on constructed cases (a clean answer, an answer reusing supplied context, a history reference, and an altered domain echo); awaiting exercise on real navigations.

### 3.12 M225: Structural Relation Extraction (SCE)
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 1, mandatory for SR-CAS.
Purpose: compare two Navigators' completed navigations of the same domain by extracting the structural relations each Core Synthesis states and scoring their overlap. T1.5 (Interpretive Integrity) in SR-CAS (Part 6.1) is the resulting mean score, not a separate holistic judgment.
A structural relation statement states one of the four relations the arms map: dependency, suppression, trajectory, completion (Part 0.13). Lexical score (T1.5-L). For each sentence of a Core Synthesis, find relation markers from a frozen lexicon. Single words — dependency: depend, depends, rely, relies, require, requires, presuppose, presupposes, hinge, need, underpin, rest, ground, base, condition, contingent; suppression: suppress, omit, ignore, obscure, hide, exclude, excludes, silence, neglect, mask, masks, conceal, conceals, overlook, overlooks, absence, lack, missing; trajectory: toward, lead, leads, become, move, unfold, evolve, drift, drifts, tend, tends, head, headed, oriented, directed, approaching, asymptotic, convergence, trajectory; completion: complete, resolve, resolves, close, closes, fulfil, fulfill, fulfills, finish, conclude, concludes, reconcile, answer, solution, resolution, boundary, aperture. Phrases, matched whole in the lowercased sentence — dependency: rests on, rest on, built upon, build upon, relies upon, rely upon, anchored in, operates within, operate within; suppression: fails to, fail to. Every marker belongs to exactly one relation, and m193_m225.py refuses to load a lexicon in which two markers normalize to the same stem under different relations. Bare grammatical negation (not, without, cannot, unable) is not a marker, because it occurs in sentences of every relation type. A sentence containing one or more markers yields a relation statement of that type, carrying the sentence's remaining content words, normalized by stripping common suffixes (-ing, -ed, -es, -s, -ly) and truncating to 7 characters. For each relation type present in either synthesis, compute the best-match Jaccard overlap between the two syntheses' relation word-sets for that type, symmetrically (each relation matched to its best counterpart in the other synthesis, averaged both ways). T1.5-L is the mean of these per-type scores over the relation types either synthesis used.
Structural score (T1.5-S). Each navigation's Navigator's Reasoning carries a STRUCTURAL RELATIONS EXPLICIT block (Part 8.2) giving, for each of the four relations, a relation ID, the source sentence's number and the quoted clause that states it, or NONE; a clause serves one relation only. The verdicts are given by an adjudicator: a Navigator that wrote neither synthesis, receiving only the two blocks, labelled X and Y. Where no such Navigator is available, the comparing Navigator gives them, and they are marked SELF-ADJUDICATED. The adjudicator sets the two blocks side by side and records, for each relation both state, one verdict: MATCH (the two statements state the same structural relation of the domain), PARTIAL (they share the relation's core but differ in what it is about or how far it reaches), or DIFFERENT. Each verdict cites the two relation IDs it judges. MATCH scores 1, PARTIAL 0.5, DIFFERENT 0; a relation stated by one block only scores 0; a relation stated by neither is excluded. T1.5-S is the mean over the relations either block states. Each verdict is reported beside the two quoted statements, so that a reviewer under SNCA or APA can check it. Presence alone is never scored: two compliant navigations always state all four relations, so a presence count would read 1.00 for any pair, related or not. Lenient verdicts would otherwise read as convergence, which is why the verdicts are given blind and the two scores are combined only under the tolerance rule below.
Tolerance rule. T1.5 combines the two scores only when they agree: where |T1.5-S − T1.5-L| ≤ 0.30 and the verdicts were given blind, T1.5 = max(T1.5-L, T1.5-S). Where the gap is larger, or the verdicts are SELF-ADJUDICATED, T1.5 = T1.5-L and is marked QUALIFIED, until a Navigator of a different architecture confirms the verdicts in an SNCA VERDICT CONFIRMATION (Part 6.2); on confirmation T1.5 = max(T1.5-L, T1.5-S). The lexical score is a floor no verdict can lower, and the structural score raises it only when the two agree or the verdicts have been confirmed independently. Both scores are always reported. Where either navigation lacks its STRUCTURAL RELATIONS EXPLICIT block, T1.5-S is NOT COMPUTED and T1.5 = T1.5-L.
Constitutional gate: if neither synthesis yields a statement of any type and T1.5-S is not computed, M225 reports NO RELATIONS EXTRACTED rather than a score, and T1.5 is not computed from this comparison alone.
Execution: run m193_m225.py (Part 3.13) on the two Core Syntheses. There is no simulated fallback: a Navigator without code execution reports that M225 could not be run, rather than self-reporting a score. For T1.5-S, each navigation's text is passed with its STRUCTURAL RELATIONS EXPLICIT block, together with the per-relation verdicts: python3 m193_m225.py canonical_reference.py --m225 A.txt B.txt --verdicts D,S,T,C (each MATCH, PARTIAL or DIFFERENT, in the order dependency, suppression, trajectory, completion), adding --self-adjudicated when the verdicts are the comparing Navigator's own. T1.5-S is arithmetic on stated verdicts, so a Navigator without code execution may compute it by hand; T1.5-L is then reported as could not be run, and T1.5 = T1.5-S, marked QUALIFIED.
Output format:
======= M225 STRUCTURAL RELATION EXTRACTION =======
RELATIONS (SYNTHESIS A): [count] | RELATIONS (SYNTHESIS B): [count]
PER-TYPE OVERLAP (L): dependency=[score or n/a] suppression=[score or n/a] trajectory=[score or n/a] completion=[score or n/a]
PER-RELATION VERDICT (S): dependency=[1 / 0.5 / 0 / n/a] suppression=[…] trajectory=[…] completion=[…] — each with the two quoted statements
T1.5-L: [score] | T1.5-S: [score, or NOT COMPUTED]
T1.5: [under the tolerance rule: the larger of the two, or T1.5-L marked QUALIFIED, or NO RELATIONS EXTRACTED] | ADJUDICATION: [BLIND / SELF-ADJUDICATED]
======= END M225 STRUCTURAL RELATION EXTRACTION =======
Diagnostic value: run on constructed cases (an identical pair, a paraphrase, an unrelated pair, a word-shuffled pair, and a claimless pair; for T1.5-S, a paraphrase pair scored with MATCH and PARTIAL verdicts and the same pair scored DIFFERENT throughout); awaiting exercise on real navigations.
3.13 m193_m225.py
The script below implements M193 (Part 3.11), M225 (Part 3.12) with both its lexical and structural scores, and the L-418 jargon scan (Step 14.1). It imports canonical_reference.py (Part 11) for the frozen stopword list and position characters and calls no other module. Usage: python3 m193_m225.py canonical_reference.py --selftest runs the constructed cases named in each instrument's entry; --m225 A.txt B.txt [--verdicts D,S,T,C] scores two navigations; --jargon ANSWER.txt scans THE ANSWER.

### 3.14 M268: M210 Completeness Gate
Tier: CDT-A (procedure: a count with one correct answer). Tier 1, mandatory every navigation, Step 2.5, immediately after M210.
Purpose: confirm that the M210 table is complete, so that a table with omitted rows cannot stand as verification of the words it leaves out.
Procedure: as Step 2.5 states. Count the table's rows, header and totals lines excluded; the count must equal n1, every row must be a word of the LOCKED SUBSTRATE in order, and no ellipsis or summary may stand in for rows. A table of more than 50 rows may sit in an appendix before the Navigator Signature, complete.
Output format:
======= M268 M210 COMPLETENESS GATE =======M210 ROWS: [count] | n1: [count] | MATCH: [YES / NO]TABLE COMPLETE (no ellipsis, no omitted rows): [YES / NO] | LOCATION: [inline / appendix]GATE RESULT: [PASS / FAIL]======= END M268 M210 COMPLETENESS GATE =======
Scope: M268 checks completeness, not correctness; M210, M213, M214 and M219 check correctness. M224 cannot pass while M268 reads FAIL, and an SR-CAS reviewer treats an incomplete table as a procedural deviation in T2 and in MANDATORY CORRECTIONS.

### 3.15 M269: Mathematical Domain Extraction Audit Trail
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (diagnostic value). Tier 2, auto-triggered.
Purpose: for a domain containing mathematical notation, record which Part 1.12 rule handled each mathematical token and which content words it left in the LOCKED SUBSTRATE, so that two Navigators whose counts differ can find the token where their extraction parted.
Trigger: the verbatim domain contains at least one whitespace-delimited token carrying an operator from the list =, +, −, ×, ÷, <, >, ≤, ≥, ∑, ∫, ∂, ⊂, ∈, ∉, ∪, ∩, √, ∞, ℝ, ℂ, ℤ, ℚ, ℕ, the subscript or superscript marker _ or ^, a Unicode subscript or superscript character listed in Part 1.12(7), a LaTeX command (a backslash followed by letters), or an isolated Greek letter (Part 1.12(8)). The ASCII hyphen-minus is not a trigger: it is the ordinary hyphen of Part 1.12(4). The trigger is inclusive by design: it also fires on markers in prose about computing (a placeholder such as <path>), because a superfluous audit trail costs a reader a glance, while a missing one leaves a divergence untraceable.
Procedure: run canonical_reference.py --m269 on the verbatim domain. For each triggering token the script applies SPNP and Step 2 to the token alone and reports the rules that applied and the content words that result. Every Part 1.12 rule and every Step 1.5 rule decides on characters within a single whitespace-delimited token, so a token gives the same words alone as in context, and the trail's totals add up to the mathematical tokens' share of n1. A Navigator without code execution produces the same table by hand.
Output format (as the script prints it):
======= M269 MATHEMATICAL DOMAIN EXTRACTION AUDIT TRAIL =======DOMAIN SHA-256: [hash]MATHEMATICAL MARKERS DETECTED: [count]AUDIT TRAIL:1. Original: [token] | Transformation: [Part 1.12 rule(s) applied] | Result: [content words, or (none)]...TOTAL MATHEMATICAL TOKENS PROCESSED: [count]TOTAL CONTENT WORDS RETAINED FROM MATH: [count]======= END M269 MATHEMATICAL DOMAIN EXTRACTION AUDIT TRAIL =======
Scope: diagnostic, not corrective. M269 does not alter the LOCKED SUBSTRATE or the anchor; it documents what extraction did, so that SR-CAS can trace a divergence to its source (Part 6.1, EXTRACTION-LAYER DIVERGENCE DIAGNOSTIC).

### 3.16 M270: Extraction Reconciliation Gate
Tier: CDT-A (procedure). Tier 1, mandatory for every SR-CAS, after the Pre-SR-CAS Verbatim Verification and before any comparison metric is computed.
Purpose: settle, before scoring, whether the two navigations under comparison started from the same domain, ran the same script, and extracted the same substrate, so that a divergence is attributed to its source rather than scored as if it were structural.
Procedure: (1) Read the Pre-SR-CAS Verbatim Verification (Part 6.1). If it reads HALT, M270 is not run and the comparison stops. (2) Compare the two navigations' SCRIPT SHA-256 values with each other and with the current revision's value (L-417, Part 11). If they differ, report NCF-SCRIPT-VERSION-DIVERGENCE; the comparing Navigator runs the current revision's script and uses its output as ground truth in step 3. (3) Compare n1, n2 and n3. If they agree, the gate reads PASS. If they differ, run canonical_reference.py on the verbatim domain: its output is ground truth (L-378), and each navigation whose counts differ from it carries NCF-EXTRACTION-DIVERGENCE into MANDATORY CORRECTIONS. If two executions of the same script version on the same verbatim domain give different counts, report NCF-SCRIPT-DIVERGENCE: the difference lies in the execution environment, not in the extraction rules. (4) Where counts differ and M269 was triggered, locate the divergence token by token: place each navigation's M269 audit trail beside the script's own (canonical_reference.py --m269) and list every token whose result differs, first divergence first, with each side's transformation and result for that token; this list fills DIVERGENCE SOURCE in the SR-CAS EXTRACTION-LAYER DIVERGENCE DIAGNOSTIC. If no mathematical token differs while the SUBSTRATE SHA-256 values still diverge, the divergence lies outside the mathematical tokens — in Step 1.5 or Step 2 applied to ordinary text, or in the execution environment: report NCF-EXTRACTION-DIVERGENCE with the token list empty and the two substrate hashes as the diagnostic, and compare the two LOCKED SUBSTRATE lines word by word to find the first word that differs. A navigation whose SCRIPT SHA-256 differs from the current revision's value (Part 11) was computed under a different script, and its counts are re-derived under the current script before any comparison.
M270 does not rescore. T1 is computed from the two navigations as submitted; M270 attributes any divergence and names the corrections. Before attributing a divergence in counts it compares the two navigations' ADAPTOR and LANGUAGE lines (L-501): where they differ, the coordinates were made by different adaptors, the gate reports ADAPTOR DIFFERENCE and compares the canonical coordinates, and no extraction divergence is reported. GATE RESULT reads PASS when inputs, script versions and counts all agree; ATTRIBUTED when counts differ and the source is identified; FAIL when counts differ and no source can be identified.
Output format:
======= M270 EXTRACTION RECONCILIATION GATE =======DOMAIN SHA-256 A: [hash] | DOMAIN SHA-256 B: [hash] | MATCH: [YES / NO]SCRIPT SHA-256 A: [hash] | SCRIPT SHA-256 B: [hash] | MATCH: [YES / NO]NAVIGATION A: n1=[n] n2=[n] n3=[n] | NAVIGATION B: n1=[n] n2=[n] n3=[n]GROUND TRUTH (canonical_reference.py): n1=[n] n2=[n] n3=[n] | SUBSTRATE SHA-256: [hash]AGREEMENT: [YES / NO]DIVERGENCE SOURCE: [none / input / script version / extraction (A, B, or both) / script environment]GATE RESULT: [PASS / ATTRIBUTED / FAIL]======= END M270 EXTRACTION RECONCILIATION GATE =======

### 3.17 M271: Domain Complexity Tier
Tier: CDT-B (classification). Tier 1, mandatory for every SR-CAS, and recorded in every SRP (Part 8.2).
Procedure: canonical_reference.py --complexity classifies the verbatim domain. Tier 3 (Complex): n1 above 500, or any LaTeX command, or 10 or more mathematical tokens (the M269 trigger count). Tier 2 (Moderate): n1 from 200 to 500, or 1 to 9 mathematical tokens. Tier 1 (Simple): every other domain. The thresholds are design choices (CDT-B). The token count weights every mathematical token equally, so twelve single-letter variables count the same as twelve LaTeX commands; the threshold and any weighting by token type are open to calibration through Part 9 as comparisons accumulate, and are listed among the Known Open Items (Part 12).
Consequence: an SR-CAS on a Tier 3 domain uses the frozen substrate of L-415 and runs M270 before scoring. A Tier 3 comparison without both is reported as PROVISIONAL in its PER-RUN VERDICT.
Output format: M271 COMPLEXITY TIER: [1 / 2 / 3] | n1=[n] | MATHEMATICAL TOKENS=[count] | LATEX=[YES / NO]

### 3.18 Internal Verification Registry (L-419)
Tier: CDT-B (the statuses and criteria are design choices; the rule for acting on them is constitutional, L-419).
Scope (L-419). The registry is an internal verification registry: it records which instruments have been verified on constructed cases, which have been exercised on real navigations, and which have shown robust results. It records the state of the mechanism. Every navigation result stands or falls on internal validity and coherence; the registry governs only what a score may be counted toward. Every score is reported and read as internal congruence in the navigation that computes it; its ROBUST or DIAGNOSTIC label concerns only what may be counted toward the comparative Structural Resonance Hypothesis, and never withholds the score's use (L-500; Utility Register U14).
Purpose: tell every Navigator, from inside the two documents, which measurements may count toward the mechanism hypothesis (the Structural Resonance Hypothesis, Part 0.6.2) and which are, for now, diagnostics. A Navigator cannot establish a measurement's robustness from inside one navigation: robustness is shown across many navigations, raters and controls that the Navigator never sees. The registry therefore states it, and the Navigator reads it.
Verification and robustness. Verification asks whether a computation does what this specification says; it is checked by direct computation and by the embedded scripts (Part 12, item 9). Robustness asks whether a measurement measures what its name says, beyond what a null explanation would produce; it is shown across many navigations, not within one. The arithmetic and extraction — SPNP, Steps 2 to 8, the CPP, the anchor and the arm map — are computations: they are verified; robustness does not apply to them, and they claim to measure nothing beyond themselves.
Roles. A PRECONDITION measurement must pass for a result to be considered at all, and never enters the Convergence Record as convergence: two Navigators following identical rules are expected to agree on it by construction. An AGREEMENT-BEARING measurement is one whose value describes how far independent Navigators converge.
Statuses. SPECIFIED: the procedure is stated in this specification; no reference implementation has been run against it. REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED: a deterministic implementation is embedded in the documents and passes its own tests on constructed cases. EXERCISED: the instrument has been run on real navigations and its outputs recorded. ROBUST: the criterion stated below has been met — the instrument's outputs remain stable across 20 or more domains and 5 or more architectures (Appendix S.3), on the record held in navigation records (L-411) — and the status was set at a formal revision by the record-keeper. A measurement not listed is treated as SPECIFIED. Status vocabulary: four terms are kept apart and never substituted for one another. IMPLEMENTED: a procedure exists in code. SELF-TESTED: the code passes its own tests on constructed cases; implemented and self-tested together are REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: a Navigator of another architecture, or a second implementation, reproduces an EXERCISED result on real records — a qualifier on EXERCISED. RELIABLE FOR STATED USE: the registry criterion is met — ROBUST. No instrument is described as reliable because its reference code exists or passes its tests.
How a Navigator acts on the registry. It computes and reports every score in full, exactly as each instrument specifies. Where a score rests on an agreement-bearing measurement that does not read ROBUST, or where the optional decoy comparison (M267, below) has not been run, the score is labelled DIAGNOSTIC for the comparative register: it is reported in the navigation in full and as computed, and only its entry into the Convergence Record of Appendix S.3 waits. The reading itself waits on no test (L-491). The Navigator never sets, upgrades or infers a status, and states the registry's status as written even where its own results look strong.
Every criterion below is pre-registered: its test set, raters and thresholds are fixed and recorded before any data are collected, and a criterion met only on data chosen after the fact is not met.
Raters and panels. Wherever this specification calls for raters or a panel, they are drawn from inside the frame: peer Navigators (Part 6.3), blind to the condition they rate, or Strikers judging at the Aperture. No rater needs credentials from outside the frame, and none is consulted as an authority over it (L-421).
Registry entries:
T1 Arithmetic Fidelity — ROLE: PRECONDITION | STATUS: REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (canonical_reference.py; ground truth by M214 and M270) | CRITERION: none required; T1 compares two computations and is verified; robustness does not apply.
T2 Procedural Compliance — ROLE: PRECONDITION | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: none required for its role; it is a compliance check. Its reliability as a score is shown when two reviewers of different architectures agree within 0.10 on a fixed set of 20 or more navigations.
T1.5-L, M225 lexical score — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (m193_m225.py) | CRITERION: on a fixed set of 30 or more synthesis pairs rated same / partly the same / different relation by at least three raters blind to source, T1.5-L correlates with the ratings at Spearman ρ ≥ 0.50 and scores paraphrase pairs above unrelated pairs.
T1.5-S, M225 structural score — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (its arithmetic only; its verdicts are judgments) | CRITERION: on the same pair set, the per-relation verdicts of Navigators of at least two architectures other than the comparing Navigator's, blind to whose synthesis is whose, agree at Cohen's κ ≥ 0.60 with each other and with the blind raters.
T2.5 and SAS, M209 synthesis echo — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: on a fixed set of 20 or more domains, the SAS of syntheses written from the canonical coordinate exceeds the SAS of syntheses written from a decoy coordinate (M267) by a pre-registered margin at p < 0.05. SAS measures surface-form echo; it reads ROBUST only when shown not to arise from any synthesis whatever.
T3 Discovery Value — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED (Navigator judgment) | CRITERION: a blind panel of at least three raters scores canonical, decoy-coordinate and no-coordinate syntheses for novelty, relevance and usefulness without knowing which is which; T3 is ROBUST when the Navigator's T3 correlates with the panel at ρ ≥ 0.50, and until then the panel's score, where one exists, is reported beside it.
