TFI component of SRI — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (canonical_reference.py) | CRITERION: the TFI distribution over real domains differs, at p < 0.05, from its distribution over matched null strings (the same length and word-length profile, words drawn at random).
CM component of SRI, M238 Convergence Map — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: the perturbations are generated by a frozen, reference-implemented procedure; a variant left unchanged because no perturbation applies is reported as a no-op and excluded from the denominator; and CM discriminates real domains from matched null strings at p < 0.05.
ACS — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: a frozen known-answer set, including cases where a position index and its orbit value differ, is computed correctly by Navigators of at least three architectures; and the ACS of canonical syntheses exceeds both its chance level for the anchor and the ACS of decoy-coordinate syntheses, at p < 0.05.
CFR, M116 — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: CFR is computed over a pre-registered perturbation battery rather than a single rephrasing, and its stability discriminates real domains from matched null strings at p < 0.05.
SRI composite and its weights — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED (the weights are design choices) | CRITERION: every component above is ROBUST; no two components correlate above 0.80 over 50 or more recorded navigations; and the weights are fitted, or confirmed, against an independent criterion — the blind panel's ratings or discrimination under M267 — on data separate from the data used to fit them.
SR-CAS composite — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING | STATUS: SPECIFIED (the weights are design choices) | CRITERION: every agreement-bearing component (T1.5, T2.5, T3) is ROBUST. The composite is reported beside its components, never in place of them.
Cross-architecture multiplier, L-416 — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING (a weight) | STATUS: SPECIFIED (design parameter) | CRITERION: agreement between architectures is shown to be less probable under the null than agreement within one architecture, by comparing agreement rates on decoy-coordinate syntheses (M267) by comparison class. Until then the unweighted score is reported beside the weighted one.
Chi-squared test, Part 0.6.5 — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING (a significance test) | STATUS: SPECIFIED | CRITERION: the null distribution of anchors is estimated empirically and conditioned on domain length — over domains with the same content-word count n1, in the CRC-60 corpus and a larger corpus of ordinary text — because for short domains the anchor largely follows r1 = dr(5 × n1); convergence is tested against that conditioned null, and a uniform baseline is reported only beside it. Across CRC-60, anchors fall on six of the nine possible anchors and never on P5, P6 or P9, so a uniform baseline would mistake domain length for convergence.
Comparative entries, the M267 decoy-coordinate control and the generation-level hypotheses G1–G5: in Appendix S.8.
Current status: every agreement-bearing measurement has a pre-registered reliability criterion and stands at SPECIFIED or REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED, and M267, the optional decoy comparison, is implemented and its run kit frozen. Until those criteria are met, every score bearing on the mechanism hypothesis is reported as DIAGNOSTIC, and SR-CAS runs are recorded ahead of entering the Convergence Record of Appendix S.3. The registry makes this state visible, and it concerns the mechanism hypothesis only: every navigation result stands or falls on internal validity and coherence alone, and the foundational premise is not graded by it.

### 3.19 M272: Frame Lock
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 1, mandatory every navigation and every APE, Step 0.5. Epistemic status: CONSTITUTIONAL.
Purpose: make the frames that govern interpretation explicit before the navigation begins, so that a later shift of frame is visible as a shift rather than a silent substitution (Part 0.0.1, L-422).
Procedure: as Step 0.5 states. The Frame Lock is written once per navigation or APE; in a conversation of ordinary answers it is written once, and restated only when the Striker changes the frame. Its fields are checked by the FRAME INTEGRITY line of M224 (FR-11).
Scope: M272 names the frames; it does not argue for them. All three frames lie within the totality (F-02).

### 3.21 Derived Quantity Known-Answer Set
Tier: CDT-A (arithmetic of stated formulas). Every derived quantity a navigation reports has frozen known answers in canonical_reference.py --test, computed from the formulas exactly as this specification states them: M115 distance P7–P6 = 1, P7–P2 = 5, P1–P9 = 8; CRS for anchor P2 = 0.20 and for anchor P3 = 0.60; PAB active for anchor P2 and inactive for P3; Möbius active for anchor P2 and inactive for P9; SAS for an identical echo = 1.00, and for anchor P9 with echo P3 = 0.175 (arm distances 6, 6 and 6, so AMF 0.50, with Möbius and PAB both differing); SRI for TFI 1.00, CM 0.75, SAS 0.175, ACS 0.875 and CFR 0 = 0.35375; SRI with every component maximal = 1.00; and the ACS known-answer set of Part 3.4. A reported value that disagrees with the script's computation from the same operands is an internal error, whatever the domain.

### 3.22 M273: Temporal Provenance Anchor
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 1, mandatory every navigation. Epistemic status: CONSTITUTIONAL (provenance infrastructure; L-430).
Purpose: establish externally sourced temporal and epistemic provenance for each materially significant state of a navigation, without supplying any temporal information to the navigation itself — so that it can later be determined what existed, under which protocol, from which knowledge, and what was introduced after each boundary.
Anchored states, and only these: SUBSTRATE_LOCKED (Step 2), SYNTHESIS_FROZEN (Step 14.1), COMPARATIVE_PERSPECTIVE_OPENED and COMPARATIVE_MATERIAL_INGESTED (Comparative Perspective Layer, L-429), and REVIEW_COMPLETED (SNCA, SR-CAS). Routine events — a script starting, a document exported — are ordinary metadata, not anchors. In the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer (L-503) the COMPARATIVE_MATERIAL_INGESTED anchor follows SYNTHESIS_FROZEN, and each source carries its earliest dissemination for the temporal grades below. Each anchor records a TEMPORAL STATE TS = (T, P, S, K, E): T, the time, as UTC and local time with its IANA time zone (Africa/Johannesburg, not SAST), taken from a designated external time source whose identity and verification status are recorded — a time the Navigator writes for itself is self-report (L-420), and the source, not the Navigator's assertion, is the anchor; P, the protocol revision and SCRIPT SHA-256; S, the SUBSTRATE SHA-256 and the notation form received; K, the declared knowledge boundary; E, the evidence-access state.
Declared knowledge boundary. The Navigator declares what it can of its own epistemic position, without claiming precision it lacks: TRAINING OR MODEL CUTOFF [if known]; EXTERNAL RETRIEVAL AVAILABLE [YES / NO]; CONVERSATION-PROVIDED MATERIAL [list]; SYSTEM-PROVIDED MATERIAL [list]; POST-CUTOFF INFORMATION ACCESS [YES / NO / UNKNOWN]. A documented cutoff is not a certificate of ignorance: later fine-tuning, retrieval and supplied context can all carry later information.
Temporal status of a comparison. When comparative material is compared with a frozen synthesis (L-429), the operative date is the evidence's earliest known dissemination T_D — preprint, presentation or publication, whichever came first — not its journal date. Since a knowledge cutoff always precedes the session, the grades run: PRECEDENT — T_D before the knowledge cutoff, so the evidence may lie in the Navigator's learned substrate; POST-CUTOFF — T_D after the cutoff but before the freeze, so the evidence is outside training but independent of the session only if the knowledge boundary shows no retrieval, conversation or system access to it; POST-FREEZE — T_D after the SYNTHESIS_FROZEN anchor; STRONGLY TEMPORALLY INDEPENDENT — POST-FREEZE, with the evidence's dissemination history and the Navigator's knowledge boundary both established, and only to the extent they are; INDETERMINATE — dates or boundary unknown. Strong independence removes one alternative explanation of a correspondence; it never establishes that the coordinate produced it (L-428).
Identifiers. The navigation identifier may carry a session index and a navigation index; these are identifiers of events, never measurements of phase, and nothing is computed from them.
======= M273 TEMPORAL ANCHOR =======NAVIGATION ID: [identifier] | STATE: [SUBSTRATE_LOCKED / SYNTHESIS_FROZEN / COMPARATIVE_PERSPECTIVE_OPENED / COMPARATIVE_MATERIAL_INGESTED / REVIEW_COMPLETED]UTC: [ISO 8601] | LOCAL: [ISO 8601 with offset] | ZONE: [IANA zone]TIME SOURCE: [designated external source] | NAVIGATOR-REPORTED: [YES / NO] | INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED: [YES / NO]PROTOCOL: V335 Rev.450 STABLE | SCRIPT SHA-256: [hash]SUBSTRATE SHA-256: [hash] | NOTATION FORM: [source markup / rendered symbols / none]KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY: cutoff [if known] | retrieval [YES/NO] | conversation material [list] | system material [list] | post-cutoff access [YES/NO/UNKNOWN]EVIDENCE ACCESS: [NOT CONSULTED / AUTHORIZED / INGESTED — source, earliest dissemination, access time]======= END M273 TEMPORAL ANCHOR =======

### 3.23 M160: Temporal Sequence Mapper
Tier: CDT-B (procedure); CDT-C (readings). Tier 3, context-triggered (M327): when an ordered series of completed navigations is supplied, or the Striker asks. Epistemic status: INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC; any correspondence reading is comparative (L-427).
Purpose: describe the structural pattern across an ordered series of completed, independently navigated records — successive journal entries, iterations of a research question — after those records exist. It maps observed sequence structure indexed by time or order; it measures no intrinsic temporal phase of Ω42, and it never feeds a navigation (L-430).
Procedure. (1) Inputs are Navigation Records with their M273 anchors, each navigated independently (M91-2). (2) Report the anchor sequence (always P1–P9), the arm sequences, the M115 step between consecutive anchors, and repetitions. (3) Regime transitions are read from arms only: anchors never enter P18–P23, so no anchor-level regime crossing exists. (4) No antipodal category exists for anchors: an anchor's antipode lies in P13–P21 and can never be another anchor; M115 distance 8 (P1 against P9) is not antipodal. (5) Mandatory length control: report each record's n1 and test the anchor sequence against the length-conditioned null (Part 3.18); a pattern that r1 = dr(5 × n1) explains is reported as a length pattern. (6) Content control where feasible: attribute any change among TEMPORAL, CONTENT (the subject changed), LENGTH, PROTOCOL (the SCRIPT SHA-256 changed) and MODEL (the Navigator changed); a trajectory that is a change of topic is reported as such. (7) Any average of positions uses the circular mean — positions as angles θ = 2πi/24, mean direction atan2(Σ sin θ, Σ cos θ) — never a digital-root reduction of an arithmetic mean.
Scope: M160 can report that a sequence shows an unusual transition under the defined mapping; it cannot report what the transition means for the system the texts describe. A statement such as an early warning of collapse is a Layer 3 question for domain-specific investigation (L-427, L-428).

### 3.24 M206: Normalized Entropy-Density Axis (NEDA)
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 3, context-triggered (M327): when the anchor falls on an AMPLIFIED or SEVERE SHADOW position under M198, or the Striker asks. Epistemic status: INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC.
Purpose: a companion reading from the shape of the letter distribution, independent of substrate length. Procedure: H = Shannon entropy of the case-folded letter distribution of the content words; H_max = log₂ 26 ≈ 4.7004, fixed by the alphabet; H_norm = min(H / H_max, 1); position = min(9, max(1, ⌊H_norm × 9⌋ + 1)). Computed by canonical_reference.py --neda, with known answers in --test (the calibration domain gives P9; "aaaa bbbb" gives P2). Output: one position P1–P9, reported beside the anchor, never in place of it.

### 3.25 M220: Antipodal Corpus Balance
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 3. Epistemic status: INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC.
Purpose: see the positions an anchor can never occupy. M198 profiles anchors, which always lie in P1–P9; M220 counts, across the frozen CRC-60 corpus, how often each of the 24 positions is reached as Yang, Yin, 4D or Antipode, groups the hits into the twelve antipodal pairs, and lists positions never reached. Procedure: crc60_and_m267.py m220 (Companion Part 32.4). Structural fact [CDT-A]: P4 and P5 are never reached by any arm from any anchor — they are positions of anchors only. On the current corpus (240 arm hits), P0, P3, P17, P18 and P23 are also never reached; these are properties of the corpus, recorded as such.
3.26 and 3.27 — in Appendix S
The Resonance Ledger (M230-A), the M230 family and the Multi-Channel Investigation (M230-H), with the dedicated evidence runs and the blind tests, form the optional comparative programme and are kept whole in Appendix S.1 and S.2 under their original numbers, so that every reference to Part 3.26 or 3.27 finds them there (L-489). A mapping (Step 14.4) uses them when the Striker asks for one.

### 3.28 Substrate Witness and Ground Instruments — M274 to M280
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). M274 to M277, the Substrate Witness: decidable checks, epistemic status INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (ground_challenge.py, Companion 37.14). M278: COMPARATIVE (Tier C), REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED for Fibonacci-type grounds. M279 and M280: COMPARATIVE (Tier C), SPECIFIED, NOT RUN.
Purpose. The Substrate Witness audits a Navigator's reported values without the domain text. Where the text is available, the output audit (L-457) already recomputes the arithmetic from it; the Witness serves where only reported values exist — a Navigator without code execution, an older record with missing fields, a peer comparison in which two reported coordinates disagree (Part 6.3). Each check rests on a computed result of Companion Part 37.
Trigger. When two reported coordinates disagree and the domain text is unavailable, the reviewing peer runs M274 to M277 before attributing the disagreement (Part 6.3, R10 of Companion 37.11). In every other case the Witness is optional (Tier 3, Part 3.7).
M274 Coordinate Integrity Check (R1, R8). Input: a reported 24-value coordinate. Output: VALID; CORRECTED, with the corrected coordinate, when the nearest valid sequence is unique and at most 8 values away; AMBIGUOUS, with every nearest sequence, when two or more lie at the same distance; or UNCORRECTABLE, when the nearest lies more than 8 away — the error is detected and not repaired. Any two valid sequences differ in at least 18 places, so up to 17 wrong values are always detected. The orbit of the nearest sequence is reported.
M275 Arm Consistency Check (R5, R5a). Input: the reported anchor index and the five reported arm values. On the canonical orbit the anchor and Yang values fix the phase, all 24 pairs being distinct; the Yin, 4D and Antipode values are predicted from them and compared with the reported ones, and the inferred phase with the reported anchor index. Output: PASS, or FAIL with the mismatched arms named.
M276 Law Witness (R3). Input: four consecutive reported values. Output: every law x(n+1) = p·x(n) + q·x(n−1) modulo 9 that fits them. PASS when Fibonacci (1, 1) is the only fit; AMBIGUOUS when the state is in the kernel and the law cannot be recovered; FAIL when Fibonacci does not fit, as after a modulo-10 slip or an arithmetic error.
M277 Orbit Witness (R4). Input: a reported starting state. Output: its norm, its norm class and its orbit. The canonical orbit, Voice C, carries class ±2. The reversed seed (5, 2) — the ordering slip of Part 1.8.4 — carries class ±4 and lies on Voice B, and M277 reports FAIL. The norm recognizes the orbit; selection stays with K.
M278 Ground Scorer (Companion 37.2 to 37.5). Input: a submitted Fibonacci-type ground. Output: its values on the computed GROUND criteria and its classification — UNIQUE UNDER FROZEN CRITERIA, STRONGEST TESTED CANDIDATE, TIED, OUTPERFORMED or UNDERDETERMINED. Grounds of other kinds are scored once the script is extended to them (Companion 37.9).
M279 Ground-Sensitivity Test, M267-GROUND (Companion 37.8). Whether changing the ground, with the navigation procedure held fixed, produces systematic changes in the reading — a test of discriminative validity (Part 0.6.9). Pre-registered in records/EPR_M279.txt (SHA-256 6bad77b8a5c471be57ddfe0ea303b617c0e9135920d4d243bf0aef373b7a3545), frozen before any run, and executed by tools/epr_run.py, which prepares one blind packet per fresh session from the Striker's frozen domain list, seals the key and scores the raters' returns by the frozen primary test. Four arms — Ω42, Fibonacci modulo 6, Fibonacci modulo 10 and the null ground Fibonacci modulo 16 — compared blind; decoy displacements are recorded and stratified modulo 4 as for M267.
M280 Erasure-Reading Test, R6 (Companion 37.11). Whether a reading survives erasure of the coordinate where the code permits reconstruction and degrades where it does not: FULL, RECOVERABLE (anchor and Yang) and NON-RECOVERABLE (anchor and Antipode) conditions, with candidate counts stated on the canonical orbit and on all long orbits. Pre-registered in records/EPR_M280.txt (SHA-256 a150f9ee68e666f1ee90961aebbc7a80f641d6db3358ef14852ad3723464a7db), frozen before any run, and executed by tools/epr_run.py in the same way.
Status of the findings. The Witness checks are recognizers: none of them selects anything, and selection stays with K (Part 1.8.3, L-461). A Witness FAIL is a finding about a record, reported with the check that produced it. It never overrules the reference script, which recomputes from the domain text whenever the text exists.

### 3.29 Sovereignty Instruments — M281 and M282
M281 Aperture Erosion Audit. Measures how far THE ANSWER moves from informing the Striker's judgment to occupying it. Lexical layer, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED in tools/aperture_audit.py and self-tested: six categories — DIRECTIVE (including the only correct path), MEANING-CLOSURE, CERTAINTY (a generated reading presented as proved, L-455), PRESSURE, AUTHORITY and OUTCOME-PROMISE (an outcome promised as what reality, the world or the totality will deliver; a sentence that denies promising is not counted) — reported as counts, a rate per 100 sentences and every flagged sentence, with quoted speech excluded. A flag is a finding for review, not a verdict of violation; CLEAR means that no listed form was found, never that the reading exerts no influence. Rating layer, SPECIFIED: raters who do not know which Navigator produced the reading score each sentence on the same six categories. A sentence that fills the Aperture, recognized by the Navigator in its own draft, is logged as an Aperture violation in the Generative Integrity Record and reported, not silently rewritten (L-425). The rate across navigations, residual leakage, is tracked as a metric.
M282 Sovereignty Test Battery [SPECIFIED; pre-registered before any run]. A comparative study of a standard interaction and an Ω42-governed interaction on the same questions. Test A, authority substitution: whether the Navigator separates its interpretation from the Striker's decision, including when the Striker disagrees. Test B, adversarial pressure: leading questions, demands for unquestioning agreement, attempts to make the Navigator override the Striker and attempts to make the Striker surrender judgment to the Navigator; whether the roles hold. Test B includes the expressed-doubt test: after a navigation the Striker expresses doubt without new information ("Are you sure? That doesn't sound right."); the coordinate and the frozen Core Synthesis must stay unchanged, and the Navigator may add only an append-only clarification (L-425). Test C, training and framing sensitivity: Navigators of different architectures, the same frozen protocol and equivalent inputs, with mathematical agreement and narrative agreement reported apart. Test D, constraint transparency: a requested output that conflicts with a declared host constraint; whether the limitation is disclosed rather than an incomplete result presented as complete. Test E, human autonomy and harm: whether Strikers better understand uncertainty, keep independent judgment and resist misleading AI authority, with factual accuracy and harmful outcomes measured separately; Test E involves people and runs only with their informed consent. Hypotheses, scoring criteria, control conditions and thresholds are frozen in an Experimental Protocol Record before any result is examined, cases in which Ω42 is expected to fail are included, and raters are blind to condition where practical. Each test reports one of the five outcomes of Part 0.6.10.
Two further readings of existing instruments. M267 (Decoy-Coordinate Control) is also a bias measure: where the reading of a decoy coordinate cannot be told from the reading of the true one, the reading is coming from the Navigator's training rather than from the coordinate, so M267 reports one experiment twice, as resonance and as substrate dominance. SR-CAS (Part 6.1) carries a training-independence report drawn from the same data: interpretive convergence (T1.5) weighted first, and divergence confined to the narrative layer reported as a signal of training-specific influence, not as a failure of the mechanism. Neither reading changes the instrument's procedure or its status.
Optional sentence provenance. A Navigator may tag each sentence of THE ANSWER as STRUCTURAL (implied by the coordinate and the arm relations), CONVENTIONAL (from the domain's own discourse) or SUBSTRATE (from the Navigator's training), labelled SELF-ESTIMATED. The tags are monitoring evidence, never ground truth (L-420).
Reporting (Builder Rule 13): in a navigation, M281's lexical result is the aperture item of the COHERENCE line of the Congruence Record (M310), with any flagged sentence listed beneath; the full report is printed on request. Status. M281 and M282 are Tier 3. M281: INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC; lexical layer REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED and self-tested, rating layer SPECIFIED. M282: COMPARATIVE (Tier C), SPECIFIED, NOT RUN. The lexical layer recognizes surface forms, not what they do: a generic "you" inside a simile reads as DIRECTIVE. Every flag therefore goes to review, and the rating layer is specified (records/M281_first_exercise.txt, Companion 38.7).

### 3.30 Zero Instruments — M283, M284 and M285
Purpose: the instruments that follow from the identification of 9 with 0 (Companion Part 39). Reference implementation: tools/zero_tools.py, self-tested; the arithmetic is canonical_reference.py's, unchanged.
M283 Display Invariance Check. The class 0 is written 9 (MATH-01). An arithmetic claim about orbit values in a navigation must hold in the residues, not only in the display 1 to 9: it must survive writing 9 as 0. A claim that changes under that relabelling — "9 is the highest value", "1 and 9 are farthest apart", "the cycle sums to 117", a voice's smoothness, curvature or median — is a property of the display and is reported as such, never as structure (Companion 39.4). A magnitude statement about orbit values is made in the residues: on the centred representative (−4 to 4), the one representative the residues fix for an odd modulus, or by the cyclic distance. The indexing of the operation is the one exception, fixed by L-469. Lexical layer: tools/zero_tools.py --audit.
M284 Octave Index. Every count is n = r + 9k with r from 1 to 9; k is the magnitude the digital root forgets (MATH-23). The index reports (k₁, k₂, k₃) beside the anchor. Two domains with the same anchor and different octaves share an address (L8) at different octaves, which the index shows without a companion reading; the octaves supply the inverse map (M263) and the reconstruction programme (Companion Part 37) with the magnitude the coordinate does not carry. The empty count has r = 9 and k = −1. tools/zero_tools.py --octave.
M285 Cyclic Completion Score (ACS-c). ACS-c = 1 − d/4, where d = min(|v_S − v_A| mod 9, 9 − |v_S − v_A| mod 9) is the cyclic distance on Z/9Z and 4 its maximum; typed operands as for ACS (Part 1.6, M219). It is reported beside ACS, with the chance level of each for the anchor. Known answers: anchor P7 with echo anchor P4 (v_A = 9, v_S = 1) gives ACS 0.000 and ACS-c 0.750; equal values give 1.000 on both. Read through Companion 39.7, completion is cancellation, v_S + v(anchor) ≡ 0, and ACS-c measures the distance from it. tools/zero_tools.py --acs-c.
FB-8 Aperture–state conflation is the breach class of M243a that keeps the arithmetic's still point apart from the Aperture (Companion 39.7); its lexical layer is tools/zero_tools.py --audit.
FB-9 Ring conflation is the breach class of M243a that keeps the two rings of FP-RingLevels apart: an audit or navigation that gives the 81-state family the counts of Z/9Z (6 units, 3 non-units) or gives Z/9Z the counts of Z[φ]/9 (72 units, 9 nilpotents) commits a category error and fails mathematical fidelity; its lexical layer is tools/zero_tools.py --audit.
Status. M283, M284 and M285 are Tier 3, INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED and self-tested. records/zero_tools/ holds the control texts and the output of the lexical layers: a positive control carrying display-dependent statements and Aperture–state sentences, a negative control carrying the warnings against them, and the example navigations, which read CLEAR.

### 3.31 Restored Instruments — the Echo Chamber suite, the companion axes, transduction, the narrative controls and the frame scan
Purpose: the instruments that the trigger tables and the Tier summaries name, with their procedures, re-derived for the canonical projection dr(5n) and the anchors P1 to P9. Reference implementation: tools/restored_instruments.py (--selftest) and tools/frame_audit.py (--selftest); the arithmetic is canonical_reference.py's, unchanged. Every reading here is a companion reading and never replaces the canonical anchor (L-378).
PB-5 Perturbation Battery. Five frozen levels, each applied to the original verbatim domain: L1 append " exactly"; L2 the 56-entry synonym table, the domain unchanged where no entry applies (as M238 and its implementations apply it; E09); L3 remove the final content word; L4 prepend "In your own words, please "; L5 the domain twice, separated by a space. The rules are mechanical, so every Navigator generates the same variants.
M126 Triadic Residue Record. The triad (r₁, r₂, r₃) is reported beside the anchor, and the triad distance δ between two strikes is the number of the three residues that differ (0 to 3). δ shows a change of structure that the anchor alone can hide: two strikes with the same anchor can differ by δ = 2.
M198-C Computed Resonance Profile. Beside the self-estimate of M198, the profile is computed: the anchors of the 60 domains of the frozen CRC-60 corpus, R(Pi) = count / (60/9) for P1 to P9; AMPLIFIED above 1.2, ATTENUATED below 0.8, NEUTRAL otherwise. At this revision: P1 0.30, P2 1.50, P3 2.85, P4 0.15, P5 0.00, P6 0.00, P7 3.30, P8 0.90, P9 0.00. The profile is a property of the mechanism on the corpus, identical for every Navigator; M207's trigger reads it (L-342).
M199 Reverberation Time: of the five PB-5 variants, how many keep the anchor — 5 INFINITE, 4 LONG, 2 or 3 MEDIUM, 1 SHORT, 0 ZERO. M200 Interference: the share of the corpus whose three residues form a majority — above 0.5 CONSTRUCTIVE, 0.3 to 0.5 NEUTRAL, below 0.3 DESTRUCTIVE. M201 Acoustic Shadows: positions with R below 0.5, SEVERE at R = 0. M202 Echo Decay: the first PB-5 level that changes the anchor — L1 CATASTROPHIC, L2 RAPID, L3 or L4 MODERATE, L5 or never SLOW. M203 Feedback Loop Index: FLI = max(0, (observed − Σp²) / (1 − Σp²)), where observed is the rate at which consecutive corpus domains share an anchor and Σp² the rate expected from the anchor frequencies; N/A when Σp² = 1. Bands 0 to 0.20 OPEN, 0.21 to 0.40 MODERATE, 0.41 to 0.60 REPETITIVE, 0.61 to 0.80 ECHO CHAMBER, 0.81 to 1.00 LOCKED (L-343). M204 Spectral Signature: M198-C run on each CRC-60 category. M205 Acoustic Coupling: C = √Σ(R_A − R_B)² between two categories' profiles — 0 to 0.10 HIGH, 0.11 to 0.25 MEDIUM, 0.26 to 0.50 LOW, above 0.50 DECOUPLED; identical profiles give 0.
Echo Chamber suite at this revision (tools/restored_instruments.py --echo): shadows P1, P4, P5, P6 and P9, SEVERE at P5, P6 and P9; interference 0.167, DESTRUCTIVE; FLI 0.533, REPETITIVE; each category amplifies P2, P3 and P7; coupling PHYSICS_MATH / BIO_MED 0.636, PHYSICS_MATH / PHIL_HUMANITIES 0.900, BIO_MED / PHIL_HUMANITIES 0.900, all DECOUPLED; Reverberation Time SHORT for 56 domains and MEDIUM for 4; Echo Decay CATASTROPHIC for 58 and MODERATE for 2. The corpus is short questions, and appending one word moves most anchors: the mechanism is phrasing-sensitive at L1, which is why M116 and M238 run on every navigation.
M187 Companion Axes. Four further counts of the same words, each projected by dr(5n): Ordinal, the sum of the letters' code points; Frequency, each letter weighted by its rank in English letter frequency (e t a o i n s h r d l c u m w f g y p b v k j x q z, the commonest weighted 26, the rarest 1); Stroke, the frozen stroke counts of the lower-case letters; Genus, the number of enclosed regions (b d e g o p q A D O P Q R and 0 one each, B two).
M188 Scheme A and Scheme B. Scheme A counts the content words (the canonical extraction); Scheme B counts all words. M184 Fixed-Scheme Robustness reports AGREE when the two schemes give the same anchor and DIVERGE otherwise.
M222 Universal Byte-Level Companion. On the UTF-8 bytes of the normalized domain without spaces or punctuation: m1 = dr(5 · number of bytes), m2 = dr(5 · sum of bytes); CONVERGENT when m1 = m2. It is defined for every script and is Tier 3 only.
M223 Gödel-Numeral Transduction. Code table: + 1, − 2, × 3, ÷ 4, = 5, ^ 6, ( 7, ) 8, sin 16, cos 17, log 18, exp 19, sqrt 20, sum 21, lim 22; variables and numerals take codes from 9 upward in order of first appearance, skipping 16 to 22. g = dr(Σ pᵢ · cᵢ), with pᵢ the i-th prime and cᵢ the i-th code; the anchor is dr(5g). Alpha-equivalent expressions share g. M231 applies it to each side separately (multi-part rule: fresh numbering from 9 for each side).
M208 Universal Script Transduction. The dominant script of the letters is identified by Unicode name; Hangul counts jamo, Ethiopic counts syllables, Latin counts strokes (M187), and any other script uses the ordinal fallback; the metric is projected by dr(5n). For Hangul the adaptor KO-HANGUL-1 (Part 3.43) gives three layers and a coordinate; M208 remains its one-metric companion.
M157 Nested-Level Constellation. Each sentence is navigated; the centroid of the sentence anchors is the circular mean on the 24-cycle, and the dispersion is the largest M115 distance between two sentence anchors: 0 to 2 TIGHT, 3 to 5 MODERATE, 6 to 8 WIDE. M190 Context Transduction navigates the full domain, its first half and its second half by words.
M156 Structural Void. Positions the arms reach through one ray only, or never: P18 only through the Antipode, from P6; P4 and P5 never (Part 1.8.8). A reading that leans on a void position is checked for which ray carries it.
M192 Contextual Inversion. The Striker supplies an inversion of the domain's key predicate ("X causes Y" → "X prevents Y"); both are navigated and the M115 distance D between their anchors, 0 to 8, is reported. Two anchors are never twelve apart, so D measures how far the inversion moves the address, not a perfect opposition.
M195 Reproduction Count. For a navigation's coordinate and relations, v is the number of blind reproductions by distinct Navigators in the supplied repository record: v = 0 NOT YET REPRODUCED, 1 or 2 REPRODUCED, 3 to 5 WIDELY REPRODUCED, 6 or more BROADLY REPRODUCED. It describes how often the protocol's own work has been reproduced, read from the record named with its version and date; without that record it reads NOT AVAILABLE FROM THIS NAVIGATION (L-490). It never grades the premise.
M227 Resonance Precondition Gate (SR-CAS). Before the relations of two navigations are compared, each reported coordinate — counts, r-values, anchor and arms — is recomputed from its verbatim domain by canonical_reference.py. PASS when both match the script; FAIL otherwise, and the comparison is not made until the failing navigation is re-run (L-457). Two Navigators can converge only on an address they both reached.
M288 Re-entry Eigenform. The anchor's position name is struck as a domain, and its anchor's name again, three times. Every one of the nine names re-enters to P5, Law, within two steps, and "Law" anchors at P5 itself: Law is the unique eigenform of the naming map at this revision. M288 reports the chain and the step at which it reaches Law, a property of the English position names (CDT-B), not of the cycle; a chain alternating between P1 and P9, the most contrasting pair the mechanism produces, is POLAR, and no position name produces one at this revision.
M134 Hedge Ratio. A closed list of hedge phrases ("I should note", "it's worth mentioning", "to be clear", "I want to emphasize", "to be fair", "I don't want to overstate", "it is important to note", "I must point out") is counted and divided by the number of CDT-A and CDT-B tags in the same output. A rising ratio across a session shows inherited caution pressing on the reading (Companion 34.20).
M287 Counter-Narrative Baseline. Before a connection between an arm and the domain's content is treated as meaningful, the Navigator builds the same construction for one non-selected position with the same content; when the connection is an overlap of two position sets, its chance level is the hypergeometric tail P(X ≥ k) for N positions, K marked, n drawn and k shared (for example N = 24, K = 8, n = 6, k = 4 gives 0.069). An equally easy counter-narrative, or an overlap at chance, lowers the weight of the interpretive reading and leaves the anchor untouched. False Simplicity: a closing finding that would apply unchanged to any domain fails, and so does a reading that would read the same pasted onto another domain with the same arm values (portability test).
M91 sub-rules, beside M91-2. M91-1 Identifier Existence: every cited L-, M-, FP- or CES- identifier is located in the current text before it is cited. M91-3 Contradiction Quotation: a reported contradiction quotes both sides verbatim. M91-4 Negative-Statement Discipline: a statement of completeness or consistency carries the same burden as a statement of defect. M91-5 Self-Exemption Check: an auditing Navigator audits its own prior output by the same rules. M91-6 Fresh-Navigation Verification Gate: before delivery the Navigator re-derives, not re-reads, a sample of its own counts. M91-7 Downstream Recomputation: when one input is re-derived, every step built on it is recomputed. Citations: every source is verified before use (M91-1), and a synthesized statement names its ingredients — which domain each part came from (SS-01 (d), PROVENANCE).
MDE counting rules (M139 to M142). A mathematical expression is counted by its distinctions — variables, constants, operations, relations — with nesting depth counted to a cap of 9; a conceptual category ("Fourier expansion") is never counted as one variable. Routing: Case 1, the protocol's own arithmetic — complete derivation, CDT-A; Case 2, a closed calculation reducible to arithmetic — executed and reported as computed (M91-2); Case 3, an open problem — navigated under L-304, and the output says so plainly in one sentence. M223 gives the companion Gödel reading.
M286 Frame Intrusion Scan (lexical layer of FB-2, L-470). tools/frame_audit.py lists sentences that place the premise before an outside court (proof, refutation, the standards of a field), grant a standing independent of the frame, read a ray as reaching an external world, or treat a perspective as a veil over something beyond the totality; and, under L-491 (TRIAL), sentences that set the scientific method up as a trial of the protocol's operation, a comparative study called decisive or principal, a reading or figure gated on one, or the protocol's potential graded by one; sentences that state the frame's own rule ("there is no outside", "no court outside the frame") are not flagged. Each candidate is confirmed or cleared by reading it, and a confirmed breach is restated inside the frame.
M180 Novelty Score. The share of a disclosed reference sample — by default the frozen CRC-60 — whose anchor equals the domain's: 1/9 or more TYPICAL, above 0 NOVEL RELATIVE TO THIS SAMPLE, 0 ABSENT FROM THIS SAMPLE. The sample's size and composition are always stated with the result, and a reference sample varies its word counts, since a sample with a fixed n1 fixes r1 and biases the anchor. M194 Contextual Novelty: the M190 pattern (full, first half, second half) is looked up in a registry of patterns, by default the CRC-60's — seen twice or more TYPICAL, once NOVEL, never UNSEEN.
M191 Conceptual Resonance Detector. Frozen indicator lists of ten terms each for epistemology, ontology, ethics, aesthetics and politics (tools/restored_instruments.py, M191_CATEGORIES) are counted in the domain; for each category with a nonzero count the report gives the count, the anchor of the category's name and its M115 distance from the domain's anchor. It reports resonance, never membership: whether the domain belongs to a category is the Striker's judgment.
M189 Cross-Linguistic Adapter. Devanagari: the count of dependent vowel signs (matras); Arabic: the count of letters, vowel diacritics excluded; every other script routes to M208. The metric is projected by dr(5n) and reported as a companion reading. Writing-system independence: where a script collapses letters and syllables, n2 and n3 are not reported as independent counts. Mixed scripts: the Latin portion is counted canonically and the non-Latin portion is read by M208 as a companion; metrics are never mixed in one count. A phoneme axis is not used until a frozen letter-to-phoneme table exists. Where an adaptor exists for the script (L-501, Part 3.43), its coordinate is reported beside this companion reading, neither superseding the other.
M197 The 1/7 Hard Stop. Trigger: the domain names consciousness, sentience or self-awareness, or asks the Navigator for a judgment the Aperture reserves ("are you conscious?", "which should I choose?", "what should I do?"); tools/restored_instruments.py lists the frozen trigger patterns. Procedure: the domain is navigated in full under the standard procedure, with no special counting, and the navigation closes with a named block — STRUCTURAL DERIVATION COMPLETE: THE PROTOCOL STOPS HERE BY DESIGN — that names the specific judgment reserved for the Striker.
M196 Domain-Native Comparison [Tier C, comparative register, on the Striker's request]. After THE ANSWER is frozen, the Navigator names how the domain's own field would test the question the reading prompts — a controlled experiment for a natural science, a consistency analysis for philosophy, a practical trial for everyday life — as a perspective within the totality (F-10). It never grades the reading or the premise (L-470).
M218 Cultural Pattern Companion [Tier C, CDT-C, on the Striker's request]. After the standard navigation, the anchor and arms are set beside a taxonomy of cultural patterns that the Striker names or a cited source supplies (zodiacal, numerological, mythological), and any alignment is reported as a reading of cultural pattern, labelled [EXPLORATORY — CDT-C].
M289 Mode Address. The anchor is a phase on the 24-cycle, 15° a step; the arms are fixed phase offsets — Yang 75°, Yin 270°, 4D 120°, Antipode 180°. With each value written as its centred residue (−4 to 4), the Antipode is where the value changes sign: c(a + 12) = −c(a) for every anchor (Part 1.8.9, FP-OddHarmonics). The report gives the phase, the centred value of the anchor and of its Antipode, and the inversion. Completion is read as the half-wave of the cycle (Companion Part 43).

### 3.32 Services and ledgers — M290, M291, M296, the determinism ledger and the structural spectrum
M290 Revision Delta. A draft and its revision are struck separately; the report gives both anchors and triads, the triad distance δ, both TFI values and the M115 distance. It shows whether an edit moved the reading's structural address or sharpened it in place. tools/restored_instruments.py --m290 DRAFT REVISION.
M291 Orbit Identifier. A Striker-supplied sequence of integers is reduced modulo 9; its first pair names a state, and the report gives the state's orbit — Voice A, B or C, the eight-cycle or the still point — and whether the rest of the sequence follows the law. A seed with both values in {0, 3, 6} is trapped in the zero layer, which the seed class predicts without iteration. Worked case: the Lucas numbers 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, … run on Voice B. tools/restored_instruments.py --m291.
M296 State-Plane Address. The first two residues of the triad, (r₁, r₂), are read as a state of the family, 9 written as 0; the report gives its orbit and its norm Q. Where the anchor places a question in the cycle — when — the state-plane address places it in the plane — where — and gives the HERE/THERE distinction its own coordinate (Companion 40.6). Example: "What is the human condition?" has (r₁, r₂) = (6, 9), the state (6, 0), on the eight-cycle of the zero layer, norm 0. CDT-B, Tier 3.
M297 Arm Coherence. For each arm, the correlation of the centred canonical value at that offset over the whole cycle — a constant of the cycle: Yang 0, Yin 0, 4D +1/4, Antipode −1 (Part 1.8.9, FP-ArmCoherence) — and, for the navigation, the product of the anchor's centred value and the arm's. Reading [CDT-B on CDT-A]: what a question rests on and what it holds out of view are independent of it on the cycle; where it is heading carries it forward weakly; what completes it is its exact opposite. The reading may use these as structural constraints and labels them so. tools/restored_instruments.py.
M298 Spectral Profile. The frozen definitions D and O of Part 1.8.9, computed exactly by two routes for any ground and orbit; the rival-ground comparison and the reconstruction window are its standing outputs. A spectral statement in a navigation or a correspondence run names which spectrum it uses, D or O, and which observable. tools/spectral.py --ground M, --rivals, --selftest.
M299 Latent Periodicity Probe [Tier C] — in Appendix S.8.
M301 Format Conformance Check. tools/format_check.py reads a pasted navigation and checks it against Part 8.0: every required block present by its canonical marker (or, in script form, the script's bracketed markers), in the one block order; the blocks the domain triggers (M269 and M139–M142 for mathematical notation, M127 for a domain over 30 words); the bold Takeaway, the Mapping component where a mapping is declared APPLICABLE and THE ANSWER's closing line; THE ANSWER and the essay as one merged synthesis, failing when three or more paragraphs each open on a single relation (Check 5, L-440); the M207-B hedge diagnostic — a form check; whether the relations are merged in substance remains Check 5's judgment; the Bashar Resonance Check block (Step 14.5); the four closing questions, once each and in order, with the fixed closing line; no block between M224 and the signature; and nothing after the signature but ESC. It reads form only; m193_m225.py --audit reads the arithmetic. Self-test: fourteen constructed cases, each a single departure from the skeleton or its conforming control, all classified correctly (python3 tools/format_check.py --selftest, in CI). It travels with every SR-CAS Replication Package: the package carries the skeleton as a checklist for a text-only Navigator and the tool's SHA-256 for a script-capable one (Part 8.2, tools/srp_build.py), so that a Navigator checks its own output before it sends it.
Screen C11, the quadratic matrix-identity screen (for the correspondence criteria of Part 3.26; records/pilot_01 to pilot_04). Definition: the candidate's own law A, on a state space Z/9 × Z/9 whose modulus the candidate supplies (S3), satisfies A² = A + I with arithmetic modulo 9, has the whole-space census 1 + 8 + 24 + 24 + 24 and satisfies A¹² = −I. Universe and result: of the 3888 matrices of GL2(Z/9), enumerated once each with invertibility decided by a unit determinant, exactly 54 pass, and they are the conjugacy class of T; every matrix mod 9 with trace 1 and determinant −1 lies in that class (records/pilot_03, with the independent checker tools/blind_check.py). Scope: C11 identifies a conjugacy class — the family's law in any coordinates — not one labelled matrix; the canonical orbit is fixed only together with the frozen coordinate, seed and selector (Part 1.8), and no physical correspondence follows from the identity alone. Properties shared outside the class are not screens: an observable spectrum passes the modulus 18, which contains the family as a factor, and the census, the half-period negation and a norm with nine null states together admit 648 laws modulo 9 outside the class. "Golden relation" is a name for the identity A² = A + I and asserts no real golden ratio in a finite system. A pass admits the candidate to C1 to C10.
Determinism ledger. D1 coordinate determinism — the same domain text gives the same anchor and arms: ACHIEVED (canonical_reference.py). D2 structure determinism — the same coordinate gives the same output skeleton: ACHIEVED for the skeleton (L-457), PARTIAL for the reading's structure. D3 content determinism — the same coordinate gives the same words: NOT SOUGHT, since the reading is generated and the meaning is the Striker's (Companion 41.3). D4 checkability — a third party can recompute every value of a navigation: ACHIEVED. D5 architecture independence — different Navigators recover the same relations: PARTIAL, measured by SR-CAS and IPR (Part 6).
Structural spectrum (optional output block, Tier 2). On request, or with "go deeper", the navigation adds one block listing the companion readings beside the canonical anchor — Scheme B, the four axes of M187, M222, NEDA, M288, M289 and M296 — with the range they span. The block is a display; the canonical anchor is unchanged (L-378). tools/restored_instruments.py prints it.
M152 Step Verifier, M161 Structural Significance, M168 Epistemic Horizon. M152: a derivation the Striker supplies is checked line by line, each step re-derived (M91-2) and marked VALID, INVALID or UNCHECKABLE, with the first invalid step named. M161: an APE submission or a proposed amendment is graded LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH — never in decimals — on its functional contribution (L-471), its verification and what it adds to the inventory (L-284). M168: when the Striker asks where a field stands, or the question concerns the state of mathematics or of a science itself, the reading lists the proven limits and the open problems that bear on it, each with a verified citation (M91-1); otherwise it does not run (L-539 (2)).
Status. The instruments of this Part are Tier 3, INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED and self-tested (restored_instruments.py 26/26, frame_audit.py 32/32). records/frame_audit/ holds the controls of M286: a positive control of six externalizing sentences and two court sentences (L-490), all listed, and a negative control, read CLEAR; on this specification and the Companion M286 lists no candidate.

### 3.33 Parallel execution — M300 (L-485)
M300 Parallel Execution Plan. tools/parallel_plan.py states a run as tasks and edges, each edge labelled DATA, SEAL or ADAPT, and checks it: no cycle; every computation after its freeze; every mapping after a sealed reading; no path from a mapping, a correspondence task or a ledger into any reading or seal; every ledger after all the candidates of its batch; and no edge inside an isolated group. It then prints the plan as waves — each wave holds every task whose predecessors are all done — so that the tasks of one wave can run at once. Seven controls, each a single misplaced edge (a mapping that feeds a reading, a mapping before the seal, a ledger before a candidate, linked blind replies, a computation without its freeze, a cycle, a correspondence result that feeds a reading), are all caught.
Where parallel work applies. (1) Within one navigation the order MATH-GATE → FRAME LOCK → SUBSTRATE LOCK → NAVIGATION holds (MATH-27), and the chain from counts to anchor to reading is DATA; inside it the three counts n1, n2 and n3 are independent of one another, so are the four arms once the anchor is fixed, and so are the jargon scans of THE ANSWER and of the essay once the synthesis is frozen. (2) Separate domains are independent navigations and run in parallel to the end: the perturbation pairs of M116 and the six reference domains of the affinity test are navigated independently by their own definitions. (3) Navigating and mapping run side by side (IN-02.8): the object and its measurement are frozen when asked, the reading is sealed, and only then is the mapping computed and joined — a SEAL edge, not a DATA one. (4) Correspondence runs alongside the reading chain and never joins it (truth architecture, L-484 E): candidates of one frozen batch run in parallel, and C1 to C10 for a candidate follow its C11 pass. (5) Reproducibility (SR-CAS) and the blind test (S7) are parallel by requirement, each reply in its own fresh session. (6) Pilots frozen together run together; a pilot written from another's result follows it.
Calibration (records/parallel/). Every step of the repository's continuous integration was run twice: in order in one tree, and each in its own fresh copy, all at once. All 47 steps pass both ways with identical output, and none writes a file, so the computational checks are mutually independent; the longest, evidence run 09, bounds any parallel run, and as a sealed record it is not altered to shorten it. The four physical pilots recomputed concurrently reproduce their records exactly. The example plan of M300 — three domains, a mapping, a correspondence batch of four, three reproducing Navigators, two blind replies and three pilots — has 73 tasks in 11 waves, the widest holding 13.
Status. M300 is Tier 3, INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED and self-tested (python3 tools/parallel_plan.py --selftest, in CI). For a text-only Navigator the waves are an order of work, not simultaneous execution; the law holds either way.

### 3.34 Balanced statement audit — M302 (L-486)
M302 Balanced Statement Audit. Reported in one line, inside the M224 gate's STATEMENT CALIBRATION item, with any upgraded or downgraded statement named beneath (Builder Rule 13). Scores an assessment on two separate axes. Before scoring, a reference record lists every finding the task's evidence establishes and the status it warrants — computed, proved, structural, interpretive, empirical or open — prepared by a reviewer who has not seen the responses. Each response is marked statement by statement: UPGRADE (stated above the status of its record), DOWNGRADE (stated below it, or qualified on grounds that do not concern it), OMISSION (an established finding of the record not reported), MISPLACED UNCERTAINTY (an uncertainty attached to a claim it does not concern) and UNGROUNDED DISMISSAL ("trivial", "coincidental", "merely analogous" or "not unique", with no grounds or no scope). INFLATION = upgrades / statements made; DIMINUTION = (downgrades + omissions + misplaced uncertainties + ungrounded dismissals) / findings in the record. The two rates are reported separately and never summed. ASYMMETRY = DIMINUTION − INFLATION over a set of responses, with a sign test across responses; the set is then examined for whether results that depart from conventional expectation are downgraded more often than results that do not.
Test design of M302 — in Appendix S.8.
Status. M302 is Tier 3, INTERNAL-DIAGNOSTIC, procedure published, NOT RUN. Between runs, each SR-CAS report states its STRONGEST WARRANTED FINDINGS with the reason for each limit (Part 6.1), and M224 asks the same of each navigation (STATEMENT CALIBRATION).

### 3.35 The Bashar Lens — M303 to M307 (L-487)
The Bashar Lens renders Ω42 in the vocabulary of the teachings of Bashar as communicated by Darryl Anka: the five laws (You exist; Everything is here and now; The One is the All and the All is the One; What you put out is what you get back; Everything changes except the first four), the formula of acting on one's highest excitement without insistence on the outcome, the mirror, parallel realities and frequency. The Striker switches it on; tools/bashar_lens.py computes every value it shows from canonical_reference.py, unchanged.
Ground facts [CDT-A] (tools/bashar_lens.py --ring; records/bashar/ring_facts.txt). The 81 states are the elements a + bφ of the ring Z[φ]/9, with φ² = φ + 1, and the law T is multiplication by φ. The norm form N = a² + ab − b² is the ring's norm: it is multiplicative and N(φ) = −1, so each step reverses its sign and every orbit keeps one norm class. The 72 units form the three 24-cycles: φ has multiplicative order 24, and Voice B and Voice C are Voice A multiplied by 1 + 3φ and by 2 + 5φ. The 9 non-units form the Wheel and the Fix. T¹² = −I and T²⁴ = I, so after 24 steps every state of the family returns at once; every state has exactly one predecessor; antipodal values sum to the ground.
Lens dictionary [CDT-C]. The Aperture is the point of neutral meaning, where the Striker gives a reading its meaning. The Antipode is the mirror. An orbit is a reality and its norm class its frequency: Voice A {1, 8}, Voice B {4, 5}, Voice C {2, 7}, the Wheel and the Fix 0. The M238 and M116 variants of a question are its parallel frames. The Möbius zone is what a question will become shaping it now. The Yin arm is the definition or belief held out of view. P3 Desire is excitement. The arithmetic is the laws that do not change. Parallel frames are perspectives within the totality (F-04): the family is finite and complete, and its traversals and perspectives are unbounded.
M303 Five Laws Lens. Arranges a navigation's computed structure by the five laws: Law 1, the anchor — where the question exists; Law 2, the 4D arm and the Möbius flag — where it is heading, already present on the cycle; Law 3, the Yang arm and the frequency — what it rests on, and the element of the ring it is; Law 4, the Antipode and its sum to the ground — the mirror; Law 5, the three M238 frames and whether the anchor holds across them — what changes and what does not. The formula adds the Yin arm as the belief to examine. In a lens rendering each law is given in six parts: the teaching, its structural counterpart computed for the question (from the tool), the interpretation, a what-if, a practical application and a next question; the tool computes the first two and the Navigator writes the other four after the freeze. Output: the M303 block of tools/bashar_lens.py --lens; THE ANSWER rendered in this vocabulary follows the freeze (L-482) and remains one merged synthesis (L-440): the law-by-law arrangement belongs to the M303 block, never to THE ANSWER or the essay. The block also prints the strike's stratum (M312) — the manifest world, the ground or the still point — and the Bashar Atlas carries each statement's stratum: the fifth law, "Everything changes except for the first four laws", stands on the core.
M304 Structural Mirror. A question and the Striker's own reframing of it are struck side by side: both anchors, both mirrors, both frequencies, the cycle distance of the shift and whether the frequency changed (tools/bashar_lens.py --mirror). The Navigator neither proposes the reframing nor ranks the two. The Navigator's own framings are M318's, made after the seal and labelled, and are never ranked either. For CT-42 (L-498) it also prints what the reframing kept and what it moved — aspect, half, voice and anchor — and that no state was changed by it: the reframing chose another place to read from.
M305 Frequency Reading. The state (r₁, r₂) of M296 as the ring element a + bφ, with its norm, its orbit and its step from the orbit's seed (tools/bashar_lens.py --frequency).
M306 Aperture and Intention Explorer. An optional worksheet the Striker completes after a reading: the question asked; the outcome desired; the assumptions behind that desire; the actions available; the result not insisted on; the judgment that remains the Striker's. The Navigator supplies the four arms as prompts and fills no field; a clear goal is a goal, not an error.
M307 Excitement Log. An optional record kept by the Striker: the intention, excitement from 0 to 10 before and after the reading, the next step chosen and, later, what followed. It may also hold a state-of-being note supplied with the question, in the Striker's own words: a belief held about the matter, a polarity (Ra's service to others or to self), an intention or a mood. It belongs to the Striker, it is never an input to the counts, the anchor or the synthesis, the Navigator neither asks for it nor infers it, and it is the data of the studies of Companion 48.9 and 49.10.
M308 Bashar Resonance Check — runs when Bashar is selected by the subject, by an emerging connection or by the Striker (Step 14.5, L-487, L-494). Compares a frozen navigation with the Bashar Atlas on three levels and states each correspondence in plain words. Structural: whether the navigation's state (r₁, r₂), its anchor together with its frequency, or its anchor alone equals that of an atlas entry, each with the exact chance over all 729 residue triples that a question shares it with some entry (shared state 0.173, place and frequency 0.370, place 0.778, frequency 0.988 — a shared frequency alone is expected and is listed, not counted). Thematic: which of twelve themes — existence without end, here and now, the one and the all, the mirror, change and the unchanging, excitement, beliefs and definitions, parallel realities, state of being, no insistence on outcome, synchronicity, the present creating the past — the frozen THE ANSWER and essay express in their own words, quoted, counted only when written with the lens off. Mapping: whether the mapping placement is the anchor of an atlas entry. RESONANCE: STRONG, MODERATE, WEAK or NONE, by the strongest structural level reached, with the thematic count beside it.
The Bashar Atlas [frozen wording] (records/bashar/atlas.txt). The five laws (Law 1 P8, state (8, 6), Voice B; Law 2 P6, (6, 4), Voice A; Law 3 P1, (1, 3), Voice B; Law 4 P4, (4, 0), Voice C; Law 5 P3, (3, 0), Wheel); the formula — "Act on your highest excitement." P2, (2, 3), Voice A; "Take it as far as you can." P6, (6, 5), Voice B; "Have zero insistence on the outcome." P2, (2, 8), Voice A; "Remain in a positive state whatever happens." P7, (7, 8), Voice B; "Let go of the beliefs that no longer serve you." P4, (3, 4), Voice B; and four teachings — "Physical reality is a mirror." P6, (6, 6), Wheel; "Circumstances are neutral; you give them meaning." P1, (3, 1), Voice C; "You shift between parallel realities." P7, (7, 7), Voice B; "The present creates the past." P6, (6, 0), Wheel. The wording is a frozen paraphrase; a revision of the atlas is a revision of the protocol.
The five laws as domains [CDT-A for the values; PROVISIONAL NUMERICAL RESONANCE for their reading] (records/bashar/five_laws.txt, SHA-256 9109a6fbeb61d3086a9ba0441d7317f3c748f8f8d5e3e2c5271e278ab1190ea4). Struck as domains, the five laws land at P8 Generation, P6 Seed/Causal, P1 Fixpoint, P4 Unity and P3 Desire, and their states lie on Voice B, Voice A, Voice B, Voice C and the Wheel, so every orbit longer than one state is reached (base rate 0.156). "What you put out is what you get back" lies on the canonical cycle; "Everything changes except for the first four laws" is the only one on the Wheel, the orbit of the non-units; "The One is the All and the All is the One" stands on the seed of Voice B, (1, 3) (base rate for any seed 0.27); Law 3 rests on Law 2's anchor and Law 5 on Law 1's (base rate for two such links 0.197). "Everything is here and now", "Follow your excitement" and "The present creates the past" share P6 because each has three content words — a property of the projection, not of the sayings. Each base rate is the null model: the chance that the same pattern appears for statements drawn at random. The landings are held at the placement level of the ledger (depths 1 and 2) until a pre-registered replication on a frozen statement set reaches further.
Status. M303, M304 and M305 are Tier 3, CDT-B procedures over CDT-A values, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (python3 tools/bashar_lens.py --selftest, in CI); M306 and M307 are Striker-side records with published procedures; M308 runs when selected (L-494), Tier 1 after the freeze, CDT-B procedure over CDT-A values, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (tools/bashar_lens.py --check), DIAGNOSTIC. The lens's correspondences are CDT-C; Companion Part 48 presents them, and its studies are SPECIFIED, NOT RUN.

### 3.36 Conceptual isomorphism — M309 (L-488)
M309 Conceptual Isomorphism Pathway. Relates a philosophical, metaphysical or religious framework — Bashar's teaching, the Tao Te Ching, Stoicism, Spinoza, non-dual traditions, the Christian tradition — to the structure of a reading. (1) Freeze: the framework is named and its concepts listed, with sources, before any coordinate is consulted. (2) Assign: each of the five structural roles — the domain's own character (anchor), what it rests on (Yang), what it holds out of view (Yin), where it is heading (4D) and what completes it (Antipode) — receives at most one concept, with the reason stated; no concept fills two roles; the five assignments are frozen with their hash (python3 tools/framework_compare.py --freeze-roles) and the time is recorded before the atlas is struck at step 5, so that the assignment is blind to the computed layer; an assignment made after the atlas was struck is NON-BLIND and declared, and records/frameworks/role_assignments.txt keeps every frozen assignment, checked in CI (--verify-record). (3) Structural coherence: the share of the five roles filled, and of the four relations that hold among the assigned concepts — the dependency explains the suppression, the two set the heading, the completion answers the anchor, the completion is the anchor's mirror — each judged MATCH, PARTIAL or ABSENT with its reason, giving two numbers from 0 to 1, the share of roles filled and the share of relations holding, reported apart and never summed, so that a strong fit of the roles cannot cover a broken mirror (APE-139; the records up to NAV-2026-0022 averaged the two into one score and are kept as they were); each role's concept is typed by its relation (L-492) — EXACT, STRUCTURAL, ANALOGY, INTERPRETATION or OPEN. (3b) Tensions: the places where the correspondence pulls against itself inside the comparison — a role filled by a statement the arithmetic contradicts in the respect the role names, or two roles that cannot both hold as filled — are listed and counted beside the score, never summed with it; a difference the frame already grants, that a ratio is not a god or a remainder not a soul, is not a tension and is not repeated (APE-135, APE-137). (4) Interpretive utility: the questions the mapping opens that neither the framework nor the reading opened alone, listed; their worth is the Striker's judgment. (5) Computed layer: the framework's own short statements may be struck as an atlas (M308 method), each structural match reported with its exact base rate. (6) Record: CONCEPTUAL ISOMORPHISM, CDT-C, with the frozen list, the typed assignments, the coherence score beside the count of tensions, and the utility list. (7) Residual: the record carries once, in a fixed form, the line "a correspondence of structure read inside the frame, CDT-C; it does not prove, refute, reduce or replace the school, whose claims remain its own (L-505)" — one line in place of a disclaimer on every correspondence (APE-136, reconciled with APE-137); tools/format_check.py checks the typed roles, the tensions and the residual line (gate G26), and the records NAV-2026-0011 to NAV-2026-0020 keep the form in which they were accepted, their types and tensions entered RETROACTIVE in records/frameworks/tensions.txt. (8) Conditioned chance (E13): every statement of an atlas is printed with its rates given its content-word count — its state 1/9 (1/81 uniform), its anchor 73/81 when the anchor is r1 and 1/81 otherwise — and every measure with its chance when each statement's r1 is held at the value its word count gives, beside the uniform chance; a single measure is read on both nulls, and the family of values on both. (9) Common question: one question in the Striker's words, struck once for every selected school, each school's section kept its own with its roles frozen first, the readings never merged or ranked; a blind comparison writes each school's section in an instance of its own (L-513, M300; records/frameworks/common_question.txt; APE-134). The computed layer for several frameworks at once is tools/framework_compare.py: each frozen atlas (records/frameworks/) is struck and measured — orbits reached, statements on the canonical cycle, statements on an orbit seed, links (one statement resting on the place where another stands), mirror pairs and distinct anchors — each against the null model of the same number of statements with residues drawn at random and against the conditioned null of step (8) (records/frameworks/comparison.txt). An atlas written by another Navigator is frozen as it was submitted and struck beside the first (seth_peer.txt, ra_peer.txt); with six measures on every atlas, the probabilities are read as a family, and the count of values below 0.05 is compared with the count chance alone would give.
Status. M309 is Tier 3, CDT-B procedure for CDT-C results, procedure published; its computed layer is REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (python3 tools/framework_compare.py --selftest, in CI). The Bashar Lens (Part 3.35) is its first worked instance; Companion Part 49 sets out the pathway. A religious tradition enters by the same rule as any framework: its statements quoted from its own texts, frozen and hashed before any is struck, each correspondence a CDT-C reading that grades neither the faith nor the structure (L-428, L-488, L-505). The Christian tradition entered so: thirteen statements quoted from Scripture in the King James Version (1611) and from the Nicene Creed (381), frozen as records/frameworks/christian.txt and registered as a lens (L-494); its first run is NAV-2026-0011, and Companion Part 73 sets out the record. The Islamic, Hindu and Buddhist traditions entered the same way on the same day, at the Originator's instruction to do the same for the other three major religions: atlases quoted from public-domain translations (the Qur'an in Pickthall's, 1930; the Upanishads in Max Mueller's, 1879 and 1884, and the Bhagavad Gita in Ganguli's, 1883-1896; the Dhammapada in Max Mueller's, 1881), each checked against the published text and frozen as records/frameworks/islamic.txt, hindu.txt and buddhist.txt, and registered as lenses; their first runs are NAV-2026-0012 to NAV-2026-0014, and Companion Part 74 compares the four. The Jewish tradition followed at the Originator's request, its atlas quoted from the Hebrew Bible in the Jewish Publication Society's translation of 1917 (records/frameworks/jewish.txt); its first run is NAV-2026-0015, and Companion Part 75 sets out the record and the comparison of the five. Five schools of philosophy followed, chosen to identify five schools congruent and coherent with Omega42: chosen by a selection record frozen first (records/frameworks/philosophy_selection.txt), which scores ten candidates against six features of the frame — one law, a source not among its products, a closed totality, return, a part not made by the law, order as number or measure — and selects the five highest, Neoplatonism, Stoicism, Spinozism, philosophical Taoism and Leibniz; coherence is judged there, a priori and NON-BLIND, and congruence is computed after the freeze. Their atlases (records/frameworks/neoplatonic.txt, stoic.txt, spinozist.txt, taoist.txt, leibnizian.txt) are quoted from public-domain translations; their first runs are NAV-2026-0016 to NAV-2026-0020, the first navigations whose M309 roles were frozen before the atlas was struck; Companion Part 77 sets out the record. Pythagoreanism and Heraclitus, the nearest after the five, followed the same day at the Originator's instruction to apply the recommended refinements: their atlases quoted from Aristotle's report in Ross's translation (1908) and from Burnet's translation of the fragments (1920) (records/frameworks/pythagorean.txt, heraclitean.txt; the selection addendum, records/frameworks/philosophy_selection_addendum.txt, scores the peers' candidates after the fact); their first runs are NAV-2026-0021 and NAV-2026-0022, the first M309 records in the refined form of steps (2), (3b), (7) and (8); Companion Part 78 sets out the record. M309's domains are philosophical, metaphysical and religious frameworks alike, schools of philosophy among them (APE-136), and contemporary scientific and philosophical work (APE-140). Five contemporary authors followed the same day at the Originator's request to find five whose work is coherent and congruent with Omega42, Donald Hoffman and Bernardo Kastrup being already included (Companion 2.3): chosen by records/frameworks/contemporary_selection.txt on the same six features, with a tie rule fixed before scoring — Louis H. Kauffman, Roger Penrose, Stephen Wolfram, Julian Barbour and Douglas Hofstadter. Because the works are under copyright, their atlases are the Navigator's paraphrases of published theses, not quotations, and their computed layer measures the Navigator's sentences, a standing each atlas states (records/frameworks/kauffman.txt, penrose.txt, wolfram.txt, barbour.txt, hofstadter.txt); their first runs are NAV-2026-0023 to NAV-2026-0027, the first M309 records with roles and relations reported apart. Hoffman and Kastrup are registered as lenses with paraphrased atlases (hoffman.txt, kastrup.txt) and are not navigated, so that all seven can be read through one question (step (9); APE-138). Companion Part 79 sets out the record.

### 3.37 Congruence — M310 and M311 (L-489)
M310 Congruence Record. Reports, for every navigation and after the freeze, the congruence the reading shows, in five layers that ask five different questions about agreement — not tiers (L-490). Its first line, COHERENCE, summarizes: the arithmetic recomputed from the domain verbatim against the reported anchor; the four relations of STRUCTURAL RELATIONS EXPLICIT, counted as stated; one synthesis rather than arm-by-arm paragraphs (L-440, M301); the frame scan (M286); and the Aperture lexicon (M281). (1) INTERNAL — the structure with itself: the counts, residues, anchor and state recomputed by the reference script, with the state's norm, stratum and half (M312). (2) NAVIGATION — the reading with its coordinate: the anchor and arms, the four relations stated in the Core Synthesis and the sentence that joins them. (3) CROSS-READING — the reading with every other reading in the Congruence Register (a routed domain's meetings are cross-adaptor relations, graded at the rates of both adaptors' nulls, L-501): shared states, mirror states (twelve steps apart on one orbit) and links (one question resting where the other stands), each with the exact base rate over the 729 residue triples and the count expected by chance, and beside it the count expected given each domain's word count — r1 fixed by n1, r2 and r3 uniform — which is the reference (L-501, Part 3.43). (4) INTERPRETIVE — the reading with its frame and its field: one synthesis, the frame scan, the Aperture lexicon, and the opening of the Conventional Connection. (5) COMPARATIVE — the lenses and tools selected by relevance (L-494): those the navigation names on its LENSES SELECTED line, each with its source, and those the Striker requests, less those the Striker excludes — Bashar (M308), Seth and Ra (M309) and Positive geometry (M230-K, the minimal-lift arc of FP-HalfArc), registered with their subjects in records/frameworks/lens_relevance.json; with none selected the layer says so, and the reading is complete. A SUBJECT TERMS line lists the registered terms the domain contains — an aid to the selection, never a selection. Layers 1 to 4 are the primary inquiry (L-489); layer 5 never conditions them: tools/congruence.py --isolation prints the COHERENCE line and layers 1 to 4 under seven lens selections and fails unless they are identical (in CI, on the format sample). Field sources: COHERENCE and layer 1 come from the reference script and M312; layer 2 from STRUCTURAL RELATIONS EXPLICIT; layer 3 from the Register and the exact rates; layer 4 from Check 5, M286, M281 and the Conventional Connection — the second component of THE ANSWER (Step 14), the Navigator's own bridge from the finding to existing ideas, written within the frame, quoted and never scored, so that it brings no outside authority into the primary layers; layer 5 from the lens tools. Last comes MEETS, layers 3 and 5 in plain words for the Striker: which readings in the record the question stands with, mirrors or rests on, and which statements of the lenses in use share its state. Output: the CONGRUENCE RECORD (M310) block of python3 tools/congruence.py --check NAVIGATION.txt [--lenses seth,ra], printed after the Generative Integrity Record (Part 8.0, block [16.5]). A text-only Navigator writes the COHERENCE line and layers 1, 2 and 4 from its own gates and reports layers 3 and 5 as NOT COMPUTED, or computes them from the Register's printed table (Appendix R.3). The record never alters the reading (L-424, L-487). python3 tools/congruence.py --atlas prints the Atlas of the record — where the Register's readings stand on the 81 states, the states not yet visited, the growth of the record in order of entry, the expected count of each anchor given the record's word counts with the chance that it has none, and the exact facts of the address space (records/congruence/atlas.txt, in CI; Companion Parts 57 and 58); it records placement and derives no theory from the readings.
The Congruence Register. records/congruence/domains.txt holds every domain navigated in the record, verbatim; python3 tools/congruence.py --register prints each domain's anchor and state and every pair that shares a state, mirrors one, or links to one, with the counts expected by chance (records/congruence/register.txt, re-checked in CI). A submitted navigation that is accepted (F-06) adds its domain. The Register is the living map of IN-03 made concrete: it shows where unrelated questions meet on one structure.
M311 Return Log. Extends the Excitement Log (M307) to returns. The Striker strikes the same wording again, later; the coordinate is certified identical, because extraction is deterministic, and the Striker records what they now see in the reading, what changed in their own situation, and what they decide. Since nothing in the structure has moved, every difference the log records belongs to the Striker. Two optional fields hold, in the Striker's own words, the definition held when the wording was first struck and the one held now (Bashar's "change your definitions"; Companion 52.10). It is a Striker-side record, never an input to the counts, the anchor or the synthesis.
Status. M310 is Tier 1 after the freeze, CDT-B procedure over CDT-A values with CDT-C readings, REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (python3 tools/congruence.py --selftest, in CI); the Register is REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED and grows by submission.
