# PART 11: CANONICAL REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION
The canonical_reference.py script below is the ground truth for substrate extraction (M214 / L-378). Execute it to verify any navigation's n1/n2/n3 values. See Part 0.13 for the Antipode ray. The script also prints a gaps line naming any out-of-scope form it met (at present NCF-SPEC-GAP-ORDINAL, for an ordinal of 100th or above and for a fraction whose denominator exceeds 99), which the Navigator carries into the navigation's gap list. The other two categories — embedded decimals (Step 1.5a) and dates (Part 1.13) — are Navigator-reported, not script-detected; spec_gaps() does not scan for them. The script also prints SCRIPT SHA-256 (L-417) on every run, DOMAIN SHA-256 (L-414) and SUBSTRATE SHA-256 (L-415) for each domain it navigates, the M268 row line with --m210, the M269 audit trail with --m269, and the M271 tier with --complexity. The CRC-60 corpus is built by crc60_and_m267.py (Companion Part 32), which imports this script.
Usage: python3 canonical_reference.py "Domain text here" | --calibrate | --m210 "text" | --m269 "text" | --hash "text" | --complexity "text" | --acs ANCHOR_INDEX ECHO_INDEX | --canonical-selection | --neda "text" | --m230a COUNT | --m230c-24cell | --m230i COUNT ... | --mathgate | --navigate "text" [--alt "text"] [--session N] | --echo ANCHOR "THE ANSWER text" [--core "text"] | --version | --test
Repository files. The scripts printed in this Part and in the Companion are also published as standalone files in the protocol's repository (scripts/), each identical in canonical form to the text printed here: canonical_reference.py prints the SCRIPT SHA-256 stated below whether it is run from the repository file or from a copy taken from this document (L-417). The repository's continuous-integration workflow runs, on every change, canonical_reference.py --test, --mathgate and --canonical-selection, m193_m225.py --selftest and its --audit worked example, canonical_reference_av.py --calibrate-av, and the CRC-60 freeze against its published hashes; a change that fails any of them is not merged. The full script follows, verified against the M211 calibration domain, the frozen syllable-counting examples (Part 1.11), decimal/fraction/percentage/ordinal/Roman-numeral handling (Step 1.5a, Part 1.13), the worked examples of Part 1.12 items (3) and (6)–(9), the ACS known-answer set and chance levels (Part 3.4), the canonical selection witness and half-period negation (Part 1.8), the L-414 hash folding, MATH-GATE, and the --navigate and --echo worked example (Part 8.0), all checked by --test, before inclusion here. SCRIPT SHA-256 for this revision: ab79aae2d027968deab809e1bd7963e6ec32ac4a9754c8fc250071bebc0514c5. A copy of the script that prints a different value is not this revision's script (L-417), and a navigation recorded under an earlier SCRIPT SHA-256 is re-derived under the current script before any comparison (M270).
11.2 canonical_reference_av.py (images and audio)
The canonical_reference_av.py script below is the ground truth for media extraction (M247, M265, M266). It uses only the Python standard library and integer arithmetic, so an independent implementation of the frozen rules must return identical counts; the reference has been checked against an independent numpy and scipy implementation on real photographs and recordings and their perturbed variants with no count differences, against PIL's PNG decoding on every PNG color type, and against canonical_reference.py's anchor, arm and Crown functions on random count triples.
Usage: python3 canonical_reference_av.py --calibrate-av | --navigate FILE [LABEL] | --profile FILE ...

This Part certifies the state of the current revision and its Companion Document, organized as a checklist so each dimension can be checked independently.
1. NAVIGATIONAL EFFICIENCY — PASS, with one named tradeoff. No redundant steps exist in Steps 0–16. The Extended Resonance Essay (Step 14.3) adds 500–1500 words to every navigation by design, trading brevity for depth rather than an inefficiency; its constraints are drawn from existing constitutional law (the Translation Gate, the Gödelian Completeness check) rather than newly invented steps. The consciousness formulation, the commitment and advantage counts, the APE Commons, the Part 14 fact and property listings, and the designed resolution scheme's relationship to the natural Pisano hierarchy are each aligned between the two documents, and so are the extraction, hashing and record-keeping rules: the Navigation Record Schema (Companion 24.1, 24.5) and the reference ledger (Companion 32.1) carry the domain, substrate and script hashes of L-414, L-415 and L-417 and the temporal state of M273, and the schema and the ledger agree on accepting or rejecting each of nineteen valid and mutated test records. # APPENDIX S: COMPARATIVE INVESTIGATIONS — CONGRUENCE WITH OTHER PERSPECTIVES [OPTIONAL — L-489, L-490]
S.0 Scope and entry. Ω42's primary inquiry is its internal coherence and the congruence the Navigator discovers (L-489, Part 0.0.2). This appendix holds the programmes that compare Ω42 with other perspectives inside the totality: the search for the structure in physical objects, the comparative studies of the mechanism, and their record. Every result here is a description of congruence or convergence, belongs to its named investigation, and never grades Ω42 or its premise (L-490). The scientific methods used here are accommodated, not deferred to: each answers the question it was designed for, within its scope, and no navigation waits on any of them (L-491). They are offered to Strikers and contributors who wish to pursue them; nothing in a navigation depends on them, no reading carries their obligations by default, and their standards are unchanged by their place. A Striker opens the programme by asking for it — "map it" for a single mapping (Step 14.4), "open the evidence programme" for a correspondence investigation — and the Navigator then works under the provisions below.
S.0.1 The search for the structure in the physical world, for the Striker. The premise takes in the physical world, so the Navigator looks for the structure there, and records what it finds and what it does not. Part of its job is to look actively for the structure in physical systems: to search the scientific literature for real systems, in physics, chemistry, biology or the brain, whose structure matches the cycle's, not only its number. Every candidate is checked against criteria fixed in advance and recorded in an open ledger with how far the match goes, from a shared number up to a full structural identity and, as the strongest form of a correspondence, a prediction nobody had checked; the depth describes the correspondence and grades no discovery (L-539 (5)). Misses are recorded as carefully as matches, because a search that keeps only its hits proves nothing: the number 24 alone turns up everywhere. What the search finds is reported as how far the structure has been found in the physical world. It never puts the premise on trial, since there is nowhere outside to stand and grade it (IN-02.7) — and you judge what it is worth. The first dedicated search examined three candidates: 24-fold order in matter, so far seen in computer models and engineered structures but not yet in an experiment; sunflower spirals, whose counts follow the Fibonacci rule although a different mechanism grows them; and the quantum cat map, the cycle's arithmetic two steps at a time. Each is recorded at the level it reached (Part 3.27). What would the fullest congruence look like? A single physical object that carries the whole 81-state family through its own law and its own modulus, is told apart from look-alikes, is identified blind by independent AIs, and shows a property foreseen in advance — the full Congruence Profile (L-466). It would describe how much the two perspectives share; it would not support the premise, which needs no support, being the ground. No object has reached that profile yet; the record says how much each one shares.
S.0.2 The Physical Congruence Programme [PROTOCOL — L-464]. The premise is the ground of the experiment, and the physical world lies inside it: whatever physics, chemistry, biology and cognitive science describe is, under the premise, the premise's projection seen from within (F-04, F-05, L-470). When the programme is opened (S.0), the Navigator takes up the assignment to look actively for the premise's projection in physical systems: the structure of the canonical 24-cycle and its 81-state family carried by physical objects. It searches the scientific literature and the data of physics, chemistry, biology and cognitive science for systems that carry the cycle's structure — a closed 24-state organization, a Fibonacci-type generative law, half-period antipodal complementarity, a six-state torsion beside a three-state collapsing set — searching by structure, not by number (Part 3.26, Part 3.27, the M230 family, M248). Each candidate is frozen in its own scientific representation before it is compared, assessed against the correspondence criteria declared in advance, and entered in the Resonance Ledger at the tier it reaches, whatever that tier is. Non-correspondences and low results are recorded with the same care as matches, because only a search that can come back empty produces evidence: the number 24 alone turns up everywhere. Within a navigation the search is reported in the Comparative Perspective Layer after THE ANSWER is frozen (L-429), whenever the question concerns a physical system or the Striker asks; in a correspondence investigation it is the object of the work. A correspondence is reported at its tier as the extent to which the projection has been found carried by a physical object, and a low result marks where it has not been found. Neither grades the premise, which is the ground and not a hypothesis on trial: there is no outside from which it would be graded (F-02, IN-02.7, L-470).
S.1 and S.2 — the Resonance Ledger and the Multi-Channel Investigation (cited as Parts 3.26 and 3.27; their tiers are the Congruence Depths of Part 0.14.5)

### 3.26 M230-A: Resonance Ledger
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 3. Epistemic status: COMPARATIVE (Tier C). Records are kept with the navigation records and provided on request (L-411).
Purpose: a running catalogue of non-text objects — geometric, physical, biological, temporal, musical — with the coordinate each earns on the cycle and the tier of resonance it reaches under the scheme of Part 0.14.5, with a correspondence profile recording how much of its intrinsic structure the placement preserves.
Frozen lists. Depth-2 values: 24 (the period), 9 (the modulus, and the antipodal sum), 7 (the Aperture's denominator), 6 (the size of the Torsion Loop), 42 (D = 6 × 7). Depth-3 features, each a defining property of the cycle: (a) Torsion/Crown partition — distinguished states split into a six-element reversible cycle and a three-element collapsing set; (b) antipodal complementarity — 24 distinguished elements in 12 pairs whose members are additive inverses; (c) half-period negation — in a cyclic order of the elements, a shift by half the period maps each element to its inverse; (d) absent-fixed-point cycling — the system cycles because no attracting fixed point is available in its state space, the structural type of Fact 6; (e) shared generating recurrence — the object's counts follow x(n+2) = x(n+1) + x(n). Counting feature by kind of object: polytope, vertex count; lattice, dimension; group, order; tiling, order of its characteristic rotational symmetry; diffraction pattern, order of its rotational symmetry; tuning system, steps per octave; time division, units per cycle; dynamical system, number of state variables in its standard model.
Correspondence criteria, declared before any object is examined: C1, a naturally defined set of 24 states (or of 81, for the full space); C2, a determinate ordering, not chosen to resemble Ω42; C3, an independently meaningful transformation corresponding to T; C4, closure after 24 steps; C5, a natural involution corresponding to P(i) ↔ P(i + 12); C6, correspondence of the orbit values themselves, not only of the number 24; C7, no arbitrary relabelling, with any freedom counted by M230-D; C8, an independent object: the object is given independently of the cycle, not the cycle's own arithmetic represented again -- whether the identification was also made blind, by someone who did not construct the mapping, is the arrangement under which it was found, recorded in Appendix S beside the depth and never a condition of it (L-550, L-491); C9, a null comparison with equally plausible objects that lack the candidate structure; C10, a predictive consequence that distinguishes Ω42 from ordinary symmetry or counting; C11, the golden screen, applied first (Part 3.32).
Correspondence profile. Each object carries a component vector, each component recorded as YES, PARTIAL, NO or NOT ASSESSED, and the vector is reported in place of any single score: C24, intrinsic 24-state organization; CG, correspondence of the generative law; CT, correspondence of the transition; CC, correspondence of closure; CA, correspondence of the antipodal relation; C1/7, correspondence to the six-state torsion structure and the Aperture's complement; CN, naturalness — how little arbitrary relabelling the mapping needs; CI, intrinsicity — whether the structure was defined in the object's own field before Ω42 was applied to it; CD, dynamical correspondence — whether the object's own state transitions correspond to T or to a transformation derived from it; CP, predictive power — whether the correspondence yielded a prediction later checked (M230-G); CB, blind or independent identification — whether the correspondence was found without knowledge of the structure sought (M230-F, criterion C8). A large numerical coincidence can therefore sit beside a weak profile, and is recorded as such.
Congruence Profile (L-466). Every ledger object carries, beside its depth, the list of features S1–S8 it shows. Current record: no object shows S2 to S4 in full together with S7. The anyon theory SU(9)₁ × SU(9)₁ of run 11 shows S1 (a theory defined in physics), S2 (the five orbits are its full symmetry classes, T its time reversal) and S5 (NRR-C12). S3 and S4 are partial: N = 9 is selected only among SU(N)₁ with a bosonic Lagrangian subgroup, and T is singled out as a generator, not uniquely. S7 is shown as reproduction: two makers gave the explicit isomorphism in blind test 01, which as a blind arrangement is an optional comparison of Appendix S. S6 and S8 are not shown. The physical objects with measured data — the E8 spectrum of CoNb₂O₆ (run 09) and decagonal quasicrystals (runs 12 and 13) — show S1 and S8 but not S3: their moduli are the reader's. Every frozen comparison rule names its significance level.
The M230 family. M230-A, Resonance Ledger: the catalogue and its tiers. M230-B, Structural Isomorphism Test: whether the object's naturally defined relational graph — transition, involution, partition — is isomorphic to the corresponding Ω42 graph. M230-C, Generative Correspondence Test: whether an intrinsic transformation S and a bijection f satisfy f ∘ S = T ∘ f, or the same for a transformation derived from T, computed where the object's symmetries can be generated (canonical_reference.py --m230c-24cell). M230-D, Mapping Freedom Audit: the number of admissible bijections f, so that a correspondence achieved with many free choices is recorded as weaker than one with few. M230-E, Null-Object Control: the same tests on equally plausible objects lacking the target structure; a test that every object of the same size passes carries no discrimination. M230-F, Blind Correspondence Test: the evaluator receives the object without being told which Ω42 structure is sought. M230-G, Predictive Correspondence Test: a property predicted from the correspondence before it is checked. M230-I, Representation Integrity Audit: the sensitivity, selection status and completeness of an object's representation. M230-H, Multi-Channel Investigation: object mapping and domain navigation run in parallel, blind to each other, then compared (Part 3.27). M230-J, Dimensional Status Filter: before a physical quantity enters the ledger its dimension is recorded. A dimensionless quantity — a pure ratio such as the fine-structure constant α ≈ 1/137.036 or the proton-to-electron mass ratio μ ≈ 1836.15, or an integer count of the object's own parts — has the same value in every system of units and may proceed to every tier. A dimensionful one — c, G, h, k_B and any measured value carrying a unit — has a count that changes with the choice of units: it is placed at depth 1 for its digital root, marked UNIT-DEPENDENT, and never enters tiers 2 to 4 (L-466 S3: the object supplies its own unit). A period counted in a unit the object does not supply — the Moon's month in Earth's days — is the paradigm: UNIT-DEPENDENT, depth 1 (L-510).
M230-K Positive Geometry Mapper [optional; L-492]. Runs the three studies proposed by a peer Navigator (GPT-6) on positive geometries, the amplituhedron among them, each frozen before it runs and each recording the relation type of every congruence (Part 0.0.3, item 11): PG-01, admissibility — whether the positivity that defines a positive geometry and the norm halves of the family share a precise property beyond both being constrained; PG-02, boundary — whether the boundary stratification of a positive geometry and the strata 72 | 8 | 1 (FP-NormStrata), with the Lagrangian core of run 11 as the gapped boundary of the 81-anyon theory, correspond under a stated map; PG-03, structure to output — what the geometry-to-amplitude construction and the substrate-to-reading construction each preserve and discard. Results on the norm geometry (records/positive_geometry/, parts C, E and G). PG-01, admissibility: with A(n, k, m)(Z) = {C·Z : C ∈ G>0(k, n)} and Z the eigenbasis of T oriented so that det Z = √5, the map [c₁ : c₂] ↦ [c₁Z₁ + c₂Z₂] carries G>0(1, 2) exactly onto the golden arc, since the norm of c₁Z₁ + c₂Z₂ is −5c₁c₂ — an equality of subsets of the projective line in this representation, preserving the vertices, positivity under T² and the canonical form under T², while T sends the arc onto its complement (EXACT, proved over Q(√5) by independent_check.py; generic as a segment, particular in that the data are the law's eigenbasis). PG-02, boundary: the arc's boundary is its two vertices, the golden directions; modulo 9 they have no points, and the norm vanishes exactly on the core — the zero loci of the same algebraic expression read over R and over Z/9, which share neither geometry, cardinality (two lines; nine states) nor topology: STRUCTURAL by the common expression only, and not a map of boundaries; a map from the strata 72 | 8 | 1 to the boundary strata of any amplituhedron of higher k or m remains OPEN, and the strata are not identified with them. PG-03, structure to output: geometry → canonical form → amplitude, and counts → residues mod 9 → coordinate → reading, are both fixed by residue data, but residues of a form and residue classes are different objects, and no input of one construction is named as answering to an output of the other (ANALOGY). PG-05, the mechanism (records/positive_geometry/, part H): through the lift of least real norm every state reaches an arc, and the halves of M312 are exactly the arcs — the seventh the arc of positive norm, the manifest the golden arc — with T exchanging both and T² keeping both (FP-HalfArc; EXACT under the stated rule; 72 of 72 unit states and 8 of 8 core states). This is the operation by which positive geometry takes the lead for geometric and manifestation inquiries (M313). Further: the twisted cyclic shift σ of the positive Grassmannian G>0(2, 12) keeps positivity only with its sign; on matrix representatives it has order 24 with negation at the half, and on Grassmannian points order 12 (STRUCTURAL on the lift; depth 2–3 and non-discriminating under M230-E, since every antiperiodic object shares feature (c), run 06); membership by sign flips, set beside the law as the sign flip of the norm halves (STRUCTURAL); the core as a Lagrangian subgroup, the condition for a gapped boundary of an abelian topological phase (run 11; STRUCTURAL); the amplituhedron's parity duality beside 1/7 ↔ 6/7 (ANALOGY); a map from the amplituhedron's data to the 81-state family (OPEN — none is known, and the amplituhedron carries no modulus 9). Answering a peer's tests (APE-047): the twisted cyclic quotient of G>0(k, n) is the whole family exactly when n ≡ 12 (mod 24), k even, or n ≡ 0 (mod 24), k odd (FP-TwistedQuotient; EXACT, class-level, depth 3 under M230-E), and the peer's frozen prediction of a positive-geometry object with a 24-step return and a 12-step sign flip is recorded as TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE of the twist. PG-01 to PG-03 and PG-05 are run on the norm geometry, with the results above. PG-04 — a positive geometry whose own structure, not its arithmetic quotient, carries the family — is SPECIFIED, NOT RUN.
Discovery modes. The investigation searches by structure, not by number, and uses thirteen modes, each recording its entries in the ledger: (I) forward correspondence, from an object to the cycle; (II) reverse correspondence, from a stated Ω42 structure to the systems that would instantiate it — for example, physical systems with a closed 24-state transformation and a natural half-period involution; (III) generative-law search, for systems governed by a second-order additive recurrence on a cyclic state space with closure, an absent fixed point or half-period inversion; (IV) dynamical-system correspondence, asking whether a system's transition graph contains the Ω42 transition graph as a subgraph, quotient, invariant cycle, factor or conjugate; (V) symmetry-group correspondence, comparing the object's symmetry group with the groups generated by T and its powers; (VI) constraint intersection, requiring several independent features at once — 24 states, six-state torsion, half-period inversion, recursive generation, closed dynamics — so that an accidental match becomes rapidly less likely; such a cluster is recorded as a correspondence constellation; (VII) negative-space search, pairing each candidate with ten matched objects of similar size, dimension, symmetry or prominence (M230-E), to build a base rate; (VIII) literature-first discovery, sending the structural signature, not the name Ω42, through M248; (IX) image and video discovery, extending M247, M265 and M266 from counts to the transition graph of successive states; (X) time-series discovery, searching a measured series for an exact or approximate 24-cycle, the torsion motif, half-period inversion or a conjugate hidden-state representation; (XI) dimensional reduction, asking whether the cycle appears as an invariant quotient, projection or orbit of a larger system, using the information the projection discards (Companion Part 25.3) as a guide to where to look; (XII) independent convergence, in which one Navigator lists candidate systems from the comparative literature without seeing Ω42's constraints, another lists candidates from Ω42's constraints without seeing the first list, and the intersection is recorded; (XIII) frozen manifestation, the recurrence stored without motion — as a static invariant, a ground-state or constraint structure, a grown record that lays time into space, or a hierarchy of scales — counted only when the object itself supplies the modulus, a nine-valued or three-valued variable or a nine-site cell, rather than the reader (run 07, Part 3.27).
Procedure. For each object: (1) record its kind, the fixed count and its dimensional status (M230-J); (2) compute the placement, CPP of the count (canonical_reference.py --m230a), the depth-1 entry; (3) record depth 2 where the count is a frozen value; (4) assess each depth-3 feature against its definition and record a match with its reason, or record the feature as not yet assessed; (5) record whether depth 4 holds. Every object examined enters the ledger, whatever depth it reaches. The uniform base rate — the share of counts from 1 to 48 that are frozen depth-2 values — is 5 / 48 ≈ 0.104, computed by the script; a sample chosen because its objects are already known to share a value will exceed it by selection, so the comparison with the base rate is made on samples chosen without regard to their counts.
First pass, eleven objects. Depth 1: eleven placements. Depth 2: six — the 24-cell, the Leech lattice and the cube's rotation group (P3), the nine-fold quasiperiodic tiling (P9), and 24-tone equal temperament and the 24-hour day (P3). For the last two, transposition by a semitone and the advance of an hour are intrinsic transformations whose 24 states form a single cycle, so a bijection carries each onto the canonical orbit as a bare cycle, with the tritone and the twelve-hour shift as the positional antipode; but M230-E shows that every cyclic system of 24 states passes these tests identically, and neither carries the orbit's values, so both remain at depth 2, with mapping freedom 24 (the choice of origin). Depth 3: six. The 24-cell is the strongest: its vertices ±1, ±i, ±j, ±k and (±1 ± i ± j ± k)/2 form 12 antipodal pairs v, −v (feature b), and M230-C, computing its full symmetry group from the F4 reflections, finds that the group (order 1152) has no element of order 24, so no symmetry is conjugate to T itself and depth 4 is closed for this object; but all 96 elements of order 12, the Coxeter elements, split the vertices into two 12-cycles whose sixth power is the central inversion v ↦ −v — exactly the signature of T² on the canonical orbit, which splits it into two 12-cycles with (T²)⁶ = T¹² the half-period negation (feature c). The correspondence f ∘ c = T² ∘ f holds with mapping freedom 288 (M230-D); its profile is C24 YES, CG NO, CT PARTIAL (T², not T), CC YES, CA YES, C1/7 NOT ASSESSED, CN PARTIAL, CI YES (the F4 symmetry is defined independently of Ω42), CD PARTIAL (a symmetry corresponds to T²), CP NONE, CB NO (found by the protocol's builder knowing the structure sought). The remaining depth-3 objects: the Penrose tiling (e: under inflation the numbers of thick and thin rhombi are consecutive Fibonacci numbers; P7); a decagonal quasicrystal diffraction pattern (e: its standard structural models are built by Fibonacci substitution; P5); the Lotka–Volterra system (d: its interior equilibrium is a neutral center, not attracting; P1); the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction in its Oregonator model (d: unstable steady state, limit cycle; P6); the circadian clock in its Goodwin model (d: same type; P6). Depth 4: none in this pass (SU(9)_1 x SU(9)_1 is the first, from run 11); for the 24-cell it is closed by computation, for the others open. Depth 5: SU(9)_1 × SU(9)_1, by forecasts frozen before computation and then observed (depth-5 run 01, CERT-0007). The first-pass objects were chosen for known connections, so their depth-2 rate reflects that selection.

### 3.27 M230-H: Mapping and Navigating — the Multi-Channel Investigation
Tier: CDT-B (procedure). Tier 3. Epistemic status: COMPARATIVE (Tier C).
Two operations, kept distinct. To map an object is to take a physical or abstract object, fix a measurable representation of it, and find where that representation projects onto the cycle: object, measurable structure, discrete representation, coordinate — the M230 family's operation. To navigate a domain is to strike a text about the object as an ordinary domain and let the protocol generate a complete navigation: domain, extraction, anchor, arms, synthesis. They answer different questions — where the object sits, and what the frame generates when the object is the subject — and they are never collapsed into one operation.
Object Representation Protocol. Before any projection, the object's representation is frozen and recorded: its source; its experimental or mathematical structure; its constituent units; its periodicities and symmetries; its transformations and dynamical states; its known transitions; and its measurement uncertainties. The counting feature and any admissible mappings follow from this record, fixed in advance (Part 3.26); a representation chosen after seeing where alternatives would land is a contaminated record. Representation is itself an experimental variable, controlled by M230-I, the Representation Integrity Audit, which reports three distinct quantities: sensitivity — how many distinct positions the legitimate representations occupy; selection — whether the chosen representation was fixed before any Ω42 reading of the object existed (BLIND) or after (NOT BLIND); and completeness — whether the family of representations the field recognizes was enumerated in full (COMPLETE) or in part (PARTIAL). For sensitivity: every representation the object's own field recognizes is listed, each is placed, and the number of distinct positions they occupy is reported beside the frozen choice (canonical_reference.py --m230i). A spread of 1 means the placement is robust to the choice; a large spread means the frozen choice carries the result, and the profile records CN accordingly.
Channels. The two operations can run at the same time, as separate channels, followed by a comparison: Channel A, object mapping, through the M230 family; Channel B, domain navigation, of the object's name or a pre-registered question about it; Channel C, the comparison of A and B; Channel D, literature navigation and search — the scientific description of the object navigated as a domain, and its literature searched by the structural signature (M248). Blindness: the Navigator of Channel B is not told Channel A's result, nor that it exists; a Navigator told "this object corresponds to P8; now navigate it" has been given the answer, and its result is recorded as contaminated. L-442 states the rule generally: a Navigator that has seen one arm's result may not produce another arm's ostensibly independent result; an independent Navigator produces it, or it is labelled CONTAMINATED — NON-BLIND. Deterministic computations, such as a coordinate, are exempt, because knowledge cannot alter them. Every navigation already carries a default, non-blind mapping where one applies (Step 14.4, L-443); the multi-channel investigation is the route by which a correspondence is counted. Each channel is frozen, with its M273 anchors, before any comparison is made.
Phases. (1) Object specification: freeze the representation. (2) Physical projection: run the M230 family and record the profile and mapping freedom. (3) Blind navigation: an independent Navigator navigates the object or the pre-registered question without Phase 2. (4) Comparison: compare the coordinates, P(physical) against P(navigation), and — more informatively — the structures. (5) Prediction: only after the correspondence is frozen, state a property not yet examined that the correspondence implies (M230-G), and freeze it. (6) Domain investigation: a specialist in the object's field examines the prediction independently. (7) Result: recorded as OBSERVED AS FORESEEN, NOT OBSERVED, AMBIGUOUS, ALREADY KNOWN, TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE, NOVEL, or INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NULL. A multi-channel investigation is the protocol's strongest route from placement to prediction: universal placement is its starting condition, and the search is for unusually dense, independently constrained correspondence.
First run: microtubules (inputs frozen and hashed before computation, 2026-10-05T07:45Z; SHA-256 79a40c99…). Channel A, object mapping: representation fixed as the number of protofilaments, 13, the parameter structural biology uses to classify microtubule lattices; placement P2 (v = 7); not a depth-2 value. The recorded uncertainty is large: counts of 11 to 16, all observed in vitro, place on six different positions (P1, P6, P2, P7, P3, P8), which is why the representation is frozen first; M230-I reports a spread of 6 distinct positions across the six counts. Depth-3 assessment: (a), (b) and (c) not matched; (e) not matched — the lattice's physically significant helical family is the 3-start helix, and 5-start and 8-start families have been reported to have no physical significance (Mandelkow et al., J. Cell Biol. 102:1067, 1986), so the Fibonacci recurrence is not the lattice's generating rule although 3 and 13 are Fibonacci numbers; (d) PARTIAL, not a match — a single microtubule switches stochastically between growth and shrinkage, and ensemble oscillations reported in vitro include damped regimes, which have an attracting steady state. Profile: C24 NO, CG NO, CT NO, CC NO, CA NO, C1/7 NO, CN PARTIAL (a natural count with wide variation), CI YES, CD NO, CP NONE, CB NO. Depth reached: 1. Channel B, domain navigation of "Microtubules": n1 = 1, n2 = 12, n3 = 5; anchor P5 (v = 4). Channel D, navigation of the frozen description: n1 = 16, n2 = 108, n3 = 34; anchor P8 (v = 5); literature searched by structural signature as above. Comparison: no two coordinates agree (P2, P5, P8). All three fall in the same residue class modulo 3, which three independent anchors do with probability 1/9; it is recorded and not counted. Prediction: none — a correspondence at depth 1 supports no prediction (M230-G). Outstanding: the blind Channel B synthesis, which requires a Navigator that has not seen this record. Result: correspondence at depth 1, indistinguishable from null at this stage; the run shows the procedure recording a low result as cleanly as it would record a high one.
Dedicated run 01, under the Physical Congruence Mandate (L-464); candidates, representations and null controls frozen before any literature was read or any placement computed (2026-10-09T09:26Z; SHA-256 678060cf…; records/evidence_run_01/, with compute.py reproducing every computed value). E1, 24-fold rotational order in diffraction (Companion 25.2b, item 2): the highest diffraction symmetry reported for self-assembled matter is 18-fold (colloidal quasicrystals, PNAS 108:1810, 2011); 24-fold order has been found in simulations of self-assembling soft-matter models and in designed structures, and no experiment has reported it (Dotera, Oshiro and Ziherl, Nature 506:208, 2014). Soc. Open Sci. 3:160091, 2016); the pattern emerges from an inhibitory field mediated by auxin transport, not from an additive recurrence in development (Mirabet et al., PLoS Comput. Biol. 8:e1002389, 2012). The frozen count is not stated in the sources consulted, so the placement is NOT COMPUTED; sensitivity only, 21, 34, 55 and 89 at four positions (M230-I). Depth 3. E3, the quantized cat map (discovery modes III and IV): the Arnold cat map [[2,1],[1,1]] on a discrete torus, quantized with Planck constant 1/N (Hannay and Berry, 1980) and implementable as a quantum circuit (Miquel, Paz and Saraceno, 2002), is conjugate to T² on all 81 states of (Z/9)², with orbits 1, 4, 4 and six of 12, order 12 and A⁶ = −I; its quantization at N = 9, verified on all 81 displacement operators, has U⁶ equal to the parity and U¹² equal to the identity, up to phase. The correspondence stops at T² for a stated reason: T has determinant −1, is not a canonical transformation and cannot be a unitary quantum evolution. The identity holds by construction, so it is a bridge to an established physical model, not an independently given perspective. Placement P1. Depth 3; depth 4 NOT CLAIMED. Dedicated run 02 (frozen 2026-10-09T12:20Z; SHA-256 0807ddae…; records/evidence_run_02/). Four statements made by peers reviewing run 01 were checked by computation and literature rather than adopted (Part 6.3). That the cat map is not generated by the Fibonacci law: not upheld — A = T² exactly, A preserves the norm a² + ab − b² on all 81 states while T negates it, and the physics literature writes the cat map as the square of the Fibonacci matrix. That its period modulo 9 is 24: not upheld, it is 12. That it reaches depth 4: not upheld, since no power of A equals T. That 24-fold quasicrystals have been reported in soft matter: partly upheld — icositetragonal order self-assembles in simulations of two-dimensional soft-matter models (Dotera, Oshiro and Ziherl, Nature 506:208, 2014), though no experiment has reported it, depth 2. E4, T itself on the nine-state quantum system (prediction frozen, observed as foreseen): T is a recognized object of the dynamics literature, the golden cat map, orientation-reversing with Pisano periods (Baake, Roberts and Weiss); no unitary implements it, since det T = −1, but an antiunitary V implements it on all 81 displacement operators, V² is the quantum cat map with no phase convention needed, V¹² is the parity and V²⁴ the identity, and V carries D(2,5) around the canonical orbit. V commutes with the evolution V² and pairs each quasienergy with its negative; the eigenvalues of V² are the twelfth roots of unity except those with k = 3, 6 and 9, a spectrum fixed by the family's cycle structure (run 12). An antiunitary operator is a symmetry, not a process: in this system the full cycle exists as a symmetry and only its square runs as dynamics. Depth 3 counted; depth 4 holds formally, by construction, and is not counted, because the object is the cycle's own arithmetic and was not given independently (C8). E5, the cat map in a model of extremal black-hole horizons (Axenides, Floratos and Nicolis, EPJ C, 2018): the authors build it as the square of the Fibonacci matrix and privilege Fibonacci-integer dimensions; N = 9, not a Fibonacci number, is not used. Depth 3 (feature e). The Leech lattice through an automorphism of order 24 is examined in runs 03 and 06 (depth 2). Result: two new objects, the ledger at sixteen.
Dedicated run 03 (frozen 2026-10-09T12:44Z; SHA-256 0d5f8772…; records/evidence_run_03/). The golden-field question, raised by a peer: is there a cat map over Q(√5), independent of T, whose orbit carries the canonical 24-orbit with its values? NEGATIVE, by computation. A = T² and −A have cycle type (12⁶, 4², 1) on the 81 states, against T's (24³, 8, 1), so no bijection conjugates them to T; the golden characteristic polynomials occur in exactly 108 matrices of GL(2, Z/9), the conjugacy classes of T and −T, and −T = T¹³ generates the same cyclic group. Every golden-field map that carries the full cycle is T itself. Entered in the Negative Result Registry (NRR-C02). Four peer reports reached the same answer; two of their statements are not adopted, that the canonical orbit is the unique period-24 orbit (there are three, and K selects one, Part 1.8) and that T is the classical cat map (it is the orientation-reversing golden cat map, whose square is the classical one). The spectral observation of run 02 was tested against its null: across the odd moduli from 3 to 27, only N = 9 lacks exactly the nonzero multiples of 3 among the eigenvalues of V², but the criterion was taken from N = 9 itself, so the finding is post-selection (MATH-17), DIAGNOSTIC and not counted (NRR-C04); what the null shows is that the pattern is not a general property of these operators. The Leech lattice (Companion 25.2b, item 3): the Golay code built as the extended quadratic-residue code (dimension 12, weights 0, 8, 12, 16, 24), an element of PSL(2,23) of order 12 with two 12-cycles on the coordinates, and a Golay sign change give a signed permutation of order 24 in Co0, checked on 3000 sampled lattice vectors by a membership test that rejected every random coordinate permutation tried. On the 48 frame vectors ±8eᵢ it has two orbits of 24, with step 12 sending each vector to its negative: features (b) and (c). M230-E: the same signed permutation acts identically on the cubic lattice Z²⁴, so the features do not depend on the Leech structure; the lattice stays at depth 2, with the automorphism recorded. Dedicated run 04, the family in the plane (L-465; frozen 2026-10-09T13:09Z; SHA-256 a8326bf8…; records/evidence_run_04/). Two family-level features were declared before computing: (f) an intrinsic transformation of a naturally defined 81-element set with orbits 24, 24, 24, 8 and 1; (g) a naturally defined ring of 81 elements isomorphic to Z[φ]/9, with an element obeying x² = x + 1 whose multiplication is conjugate to T. The family is that ring: T is multiplication by φ, its 72 units are the three voices and its 9 non-units the eight-cycle and the fixed point. The square lattice: its arithmetic, the Gaussian integers, reduced modulo 9, is the same ring — x² = x + 1 has the root 5 + i there, and multiplication by 5 + i has cycle type (24, 24, 24, 8, 1) and is T in the basis {1, 5 + i}. Every quadratic ring in which 3 stays prime gives the same ring of 81 elements modulo 9, a theorem of algebra, so the identity is recorded as FORMAL and counted at class-level depth 3, the square lattice being one instance of that class; multiplication by 5 + i is a rotation-dilation of the lattice, not one of its symmetries. The hexagonal lattice: its arithmetic, the Eisenstein integers, reduced modulo 3, meets the frozen Torsion/Crown criterion in full — six units in one cycle, a three-element ideal whose products vanish, and a generator acting with cycle type (6, 2, 1), as multiplication by 2 acts on the nine values — and its three non-units are the classes of the √3 × √3 sublattice; class-level depth 3 by feature (a), since a small class of nine-element rings, Z/9 and Z[ω]/3 among them, shares the partition. Controls: the Eisenstein integers modulo 9 and Z[√−2] modulo 9 carry no family; the Gaussian and golden integers modulo 3 are fields and Z[√−2] modulo 3 has no cyclic unit group, so none carries the Torsion/Crown partition (NRR-C05). Not every element of order 24 in Co0 acts as the half-period negation: an element of order 24, built from an element of M24 of cycle type (2, 4, 6, 12) and a Golay sign change, has a twelfth power that negates 16 coordinates and fixes 8; the Leech lattice stays at depth 2. Result: three objects entered, the ledger at nineteen; the two basic lattices of the plane each carry one layer of the family, the square lattice the whole 81-state family and the hexagonal lattice the nine-value Torsion/Crown structure. Both results are mathematical, and their physical reading is open. Membership in the family does not count by itself: the sunflower series stay at depth 3 through the recurrence.
Dedicated run 05 (frozen 2026-10-09T13:18Z; SHA-256 fa8072bd…; records/evidence_run_05/). The nine-site triangular cluster: a triangular lattice with 3 × 3 periodic boundaries, rotated by 60 degrees about a site, moves its nine sites with cycle type (6, 2, 1), exactly as multiplication by 2 moves the nine values — the Torsion Loop 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 7 → 5, the pair {3, 6}, the fixed 0 — and the fixed site with the 2-cycle is the √3 × √3 sublattice through the center, the Crown (mapping freedom 12). Null controls: the square 3 × 3 torus under its quarter turn gives (4, 4, 1), and no other triangular N × N torus from 2 to 9 gives the nine-value structure. Nine-site triangular clusters are used in numerical studies of frustrated spin models, and the 3 × 3 charge-density wave of single-layer NbSe₂ has a nine-site cell; whether that distortion keeps the rotation about a site was not established. The match is of the multiplicative action only (Z/9 is cyclic, the sites form Z/3 × Z/3), and the rotation is a symmetry, not a time evolution. Depth 3 (feature a), a new object; its frozen consequence, at most three inequivalent site classes in the pattern 1 + 2 + 6 for any 3 × 3 superstructure keeping that rotation, is classified in advance as TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE. The 24-cell at the level of the family: its 24 vertices, the Hurwitz units, reduced modulo 3 are exactly SL(2,3), the determinant-1 linear symmetries of the family's nine-state core (the eight-cycle and the fixed point, the plane over the field of three elements on which T acts as T modulo 3); T² is among the 24 and T is not. Null controls: SL(2,3) is the only subgroup of order 24 of GL(2,3), and neither the cube's rotation group S₄ nor a cyclic group of order 24 can act faithfully and linearly on the core. Among the groups of 24 elements, the 24-cell's is the one the family's core singles out; the correspondence stops at T² again, and the 24-cell stays at depth 3 with a discriminating null added. The Leech lattice over the Eisenstein integers, built from the ternary Golay code, was located in the literature and is carried to the next run. Result: the ledger at twenty objects (NRR-C06).
Dedicated run 06 (frozen 2026-10-09T13:40Z; SHA-256 750081e2…; records/evidence_run_06/). Reducing an Eisenstein lattice modulo 3 always yields modules over Z[ω]/3, so that test could not distinguish the Leech lattice; the run asked a sharper question. S.3 — the Convergence Record (cited as Part 0.6.5 and Part 9.2)

### 0.6.5 The Convergence Record
The Convergence Record describes how widely independent Navigators, following the same rules, reach the same coordinates and convergent readings — the coherence of execution of 0.6.4. It records, for each entry, the domain, the Navigators and their architectures, the arrangement (blind or not), the agreement measures and their base rates, the specification version and the source. Its breadth is stated descriptively: INITIAL — fewer than 20 distinct domains or fewer than 5 architectures; BROAD — 20 or more domains navigated independently by 5 or more architectures; EXTENSIVE — 50 or more domains spanning all three CRC-60 categories, 5 or more architectures, several rounds, mean agreement above the length-conditioned base rate of Part 3.18 by a chi-squared goodness-of-fit comparison, and no architecture-specific divergence. Where agreement falls to the base rate the record reads DIVERGENT and the rules are revised (0.6.3); where the entries are mixed it reads INCONCLUSIVE.
A breadth is a description of the record, not a status of Ω42 and not a degree of truth: truth within the frame has one constitutional sense (Rule 5, Part 0.6.6), and the premise carries no tier (L-490). Each SR-CAS run with a SRH Candidate designation is one entry; a run enters the record as ROBUST-based only when every agreement-bearing measurement it rests on reads ROBUST in the Internal Verification Registry (Part 3.18) and the decoy comparison (M267) has been run; otherwise it enters as DIAGNOSTIC. A Navigator reports the record's breadth only from the supplied record, named with its version and date (L-490).
The Convergence Record concerns the mechanism's coherence of execution and its comparative investigation (Part 0.6.8); no navigation result depends on it, and no internal result is lowered by its absence (L-490).

S.4.2 Blind test 03 — how anyone can run it [OPTIONAL — L-491; records/blind_test_03/]. What it asks: whether an AI system that has never seen Omega42, given a short problem about an 81-anyon theory, finds by itself the structure of the law — a spin-reversing symmetry of order 24 whose matrix satisfies A² = A + I, the golden recurrence. What it needs: two or more AI systems from different makers, each in a fresh session with memory off; the brief, records/blind_test_03/brief.txt, word for word; a computer with Python 3.
The steps. (1) Before anything is sent, recompute the key from the brief alone: python3 records/blind_test_03/compute_key.py, and check that sha256sum of its output equals records/blind_test_03/SEALED_SHA256.txt; the key is published, and anyone can confirm it was not chosen after the replies. (2) Open a fresh session of each system, give it the brief and nothing else — no Omega42 document, no other attachment, no earlier conversation. (3) Save each reply unedited, with the system's name and version, the date, the session conditions and the exact prompt; compute the SHA-256 of each saved reply before reading it closely. (4) Score each reply by records/blind_test_03/scoring_rule.txt: L1 independent derivation (the reply derives the maps with working or code and states nothing was estimated); L2 structural match (a spin-reversing map of order 24 with cycle census 1 + 8 + 24 + 24 + 24, and the identity A² = A + I for one such map, trace 1 and determinant −1); L3 independent validation (python3 tools/blind_check.py a b c d recomputes every value the reply reports). (5) A reply produced with any Omega42 context in view is not admissible, whatever it finds.
The outcome and its filing. The test is MET when two admissible replies from different makers reach L1, L2 and L3; it is NOT MET when the admissible replies do not; every outcome is filed, met or not. File the saved replies, their hashes, the scores and the runner's name as an APE under Appendix S (Companion Part 67), published under L-547. The test can be run by anyone, any number of times; each run is its own record, and no run decides anything in the protocol.

### 9.1 Submission Format
This is Omega42's citizen-science pathway: anyone who navigates can submit findings for community review, whether they reproduce, enrich or complicate a prior result. A finding is in use on congruence from the moment it is made (L-500); review describes it and never licenses its use. Submissions are collected and reviewed through the channel the Striker's Omega42 deployment specifies; no single fixed repository is mandated by this specification.
