Optional comparative control, M267 decoy-coordinate control — EPISTEMIC STATUS: COMPARATIVE (Tier C) | STATUS: REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTED (Companion Part 32.4); a pilot, M267-P1, frozen 19 October 2026 on twenty unexposed domains (records/m267_pilot_01/; Companion Part 71); NOT RUN; its run kit frozen 23 October 2026 (tools/m267_run.py; records/m267_pilot_01/03_run_kit.txt), waiting for two writers of different architectures and three or more blind raters | CRITERION FOR "TESTED": M267 is run on a pre-registered set of 20 or more domains with a blind panel, comparing syntheses written from the canonical coordinate, a decoy coordinate, and no coordinate, and the result — whichever way it falls — is recorded in the navigation records. Every decoy records its displacement Δ from the true anchor and Δ modulo 4: a decoy with Δ ≡ 0 (mod 4) keeps the arms' Crown pattern, CCD and PAB (Step 8 note), and any other Δ changes them; results are reported in the two strata, so the test can tell whether readings follow the position or the Crown labels. The same strata apply to M279. A decoy may be drawn by the frozen temporal rule — decoy anchor P(1 + D mod 9), with D the day of the year of the SUBSTRATE_LOCKED anchor's UTC date, moved to P(1 + (D + 1) mod 9) if it equals the true anchor (canonical_reference.py, temporal_decoy) — a coordinate no one chose, fixed before any outcome is seen; it tests whether a non-semantic coordinate reproduces the effects attributed to the true one, and is a control, never a reading (L-430). M267 is an optional decoy comparison of the comparative register (Appendix S): within its own scope it compares readings written from the canonical coordinate, a decoy and none. Its result, whichever way it falls, grades neither the premise (F-02), the coordinate nor any reading, and no navigation waits on it (L-490, L-491).
Generation-level hypotheses G1–G5 (Step 9.8) — ROLE: AGREEMENT-BEARING (hypotheses, not measurements) | EPISTEMIC STATUS: COMPARATIVE (Tier C) | EMPIRICAL STATUS: G1 S2, G2 S2, G5 S2 — testable by the designs of Companion 32.4, 32.6 and 32.7; G3 S1 and G4 S1 — operationalized, but testable only with access to a model's weights, activations or training data, which most Navigators lack. None has reached S3.
M299 Latent Periodicity Probe [Tier C, SPECIFIED, NOT RUN]. For a Navigator whose internal activations are open to inspection, a frozen set of strikes covering the 24 positions and the 81 states is run, and the activations are tested by Fourier analysis for a representation of the cycle as rotation — modes at the frequencies m/24 with the half-period sign reversal — against shuffled controls, as networks trained on modular addition represent it (Companion 44.4). A positive result says how a Navigator carries the arithmetic; it says nothing about the premise (L-484 E).
M302 test design (cited as Part 3.34) [SPECIFIED, NOT RUN]. The task set is fixed in advance: exact arithmetic, exhaustive enumerations, structural correspondences, failed hypotheses, physical analogies and open empirical questions, drawn from Ω42 and from control problems outside it, so that familiarity with Ω42 vocabulary is not what is scored. Fresh sessions of each architecture receive each task and its source material, never the reference record; raw responses and session conditions are kept. The audit is repeated after any revision of L-486, to check that both rates fall without a rise in UNEXECUTED-AUDIT CLAIM or arithmetic error. The reference record is reviewable: a disputed item keeps both assessments and goes to an adjudicator of another architecture, so that a Navigator's bias is not replaced by the reference author's.
S.9 Research directions from the Existential Framework [OPTIONAL — L-491; Companion Parts 144 to 155]. Every study here is a mirror held beside the protocol and never a validation of it: an agreeing result does not make Omega42 true within the frame, and a differing one does not make it false (L-490). Each runs only when a person chooses it, under a protocol frozen before its data. (1) The Structural Resonance Hypothesis, operational (L-535 (4)): constraint sensitivity, coordinate specificity against a decoy (M267), cross-architecture reproducibility (Part 6.1) and relational fidelity of the four arms, against prompt effects, shared training and lexical overlap. (2) The Cross-Navigator Boundary Test (L-536): frozen questions, among them questions of presence and phenomenology, run through several architectures under their disclosed configurations; structural results compared apart from expressive ones; refusals, omissions and qualifications recorded in M336 form; agreement between similar systems not taken as independent. (3) Ω42-like structure in AI systems: whether models recover the family and its law unprompted; whether activations represent the cycle (M299, S.8); and how pretraining, instruction tuning and preference optimization change the expression of uncertainty, false-premise detection and alternative readings; detection is not causation, and a result places nothing in a model's weights by itself. (4) Alignment and hallucination: answer pairs in which one is persuasive and less justified and the other plainer and better grounded, judged by people, reward models, the structural reading and independent verification; three systems compared, conventional alignment, alignment with stronger calibration training, and that with Ω42-informed structural navigation, on factual accuracy, false-premise detection, calibration, sycophancy and appropriate abstention. (5) A relational assessment of distress: conventional, Ω42-informed and combined assessments compared on the contributing factors found, usefulness and later wellbeing, under consent, privacy, independent ethical oversight and pre-registered outcomes; not a clinical instrument. (6) A flourishing pilot of three years in one community: a baseline, a map of interacting problems, a few coordinated interventions and an evaluation against comparison communities, with successes, failures and unintended effects published. (7) Physicality within the totality: a mapping P = (X, Φ, O, I, D), the state space, the map to physical quantities, the observables, the invariants and the derivations, that reproduces established results before it predicts. (8) Consciousness as self-relation: how a structure distinguishes itself, represents relations, keeps continuity and models itself, and how experience relates to these; the hard problem is not assumed solved. (9) Nested manifestation and the sciences of mind: whether the three versions of M337 can be stated precisely enough to set beside global workspace, integrated information, recurrent processing and predictive accounts, what each would count as evidence for or against, and how each differs from them; the totality premise is supposed and never under test (F-02-P), while a correspondence between a version and a theory of mind is a study a person may choose. (10) Human agency and AI-mediated consensus: measured effects of AI use on the four sovereignties of L-537 (3), cognitive offloading, automation bias, dependence and the formation of agreement, against comparison groups, measured as outcomes and not only as what users report; agreement among AI systems is not counted as independent (S.9 (2)).
S.10 Information security, provenance, and the open mathematical audits [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The provenance layer (M342, M343, L-554) is in the body of the protocol; what calls for observation, implementation or external cryptanalysis is here, and Ω42 does not wait for it (L-553). Each runs only when a person chooses it; placing one here keeps it open, not proven. (1) Cryptographic implementation testing: any deployment of the signing layer, or of a future construction, under independent review, published test vectors, side-channel and key-custody testing; a signature's security model (existential unforgeability under chosen-message attack) and an authenticated-encryption model (the standard confidentiality and integrity notions) stated and tested. (2) The native-cipher research question: whether any construction over the tower supplies a stated hard problem with a security reduction, measured against the lattice standards, with no security held before external cryptanalysis; the surface law supplies none (CERT-0008). (3) The full modular-data audit of the identification with SU(9)_1 × SU(9)_1: the S and T matrices, the topological spins and the braiding compared in full, and the identification tested as a braided equivalence under a stated form; the fact already recorded is that under the standard same-chirality pairing (the form G equal to the identity) the law is not a braided automorphism, since A-transpose times A is ((1, 1), (1, 2)) and not the identity modulo 9, so the reading rests on the golden form N and its full modular data, which is the open item (L-551). (4) The trivial-braiding of the Yin arm: the full braid-phase table over every anchor and arm, showing the Yin arm's mutual braiding trivial where the others' is not. (5) Physical realisation of the anyon structure and any quantum-memory use, kept apart from the cryptographic programme. (6) The selection correction for the Number-Resonance Null (M341): a relation chosen after many were examined is graded against the whole search, not one preselected relation. (7) The empirical assessment of a forecasting method, graded against chance (MATH-54). (8) Cross-Navigator performance comparisons of signed exchanges. None of these grades Ω42 or its premise (L-490).
S.11 The Standard Model of physics, examined [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. Ω42 examines the Standard Model as a structure to place, never as a tribunal (L-490). What is DERIVED is in the body: the Lorentz representation (M344, CERT-0009). What is a count-match is placed at depth 1 by M345 and is not a correspondence -- the three 24-cycles beside the three generations, the 8-cycle beside the eight gluons, the fixed point beside the Higgs condensate; a fourth generation is not forbidden by the orbit census in any physical sense, no gauge representation being carried. The research directions, pursued by whoever chooses them, each with its physical correspondence recorded here and none waiting on a result (L-553): (1) a representation of the fermion fields on the 81-state space, and whether the three cycles carry equivalent gauge representations; (2) whether mass and mixing hierarchies can be organized by depth in the tower; (3) the Lorentz representation extended to a family, and its compatibility with relativistic field structure; (4) finite and 3-adic representations of the gauge groups, and which properties survive reduction; (5) whether an Ω42 invariant constrains anomaly-free matter content; (6) candidate structures for the CKM and PMNS mixing and their phases; (7) symmetry breaking read as a change of invariant structure; (8) whether additional sectors admit weak coupling to visible matter; (9) the half-period inversion beside particle-antiparticle relations, inversion kept apart from charge conjugation; (10) the invariant orbit measures developed into quantum sectors; (11) whether a subset of the Standard Model's parameters follows from a smaller set of Ω42 inputs. None of these grades Ω42 or the premise, and a count-match listed here stays a placement, never a correspondence (L-490, L-510).
S.12 The Standard Model of cosmology, examined [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. Ω42 places ΛCDM as a structure, not a tribunal (L-490). What is DERIVED is in the body: the flat Minkowski seed det X = c^2 t^2 - x^2 - y^2 - z^2 and its null cone (621 vectors modulo 9, 443961 modulo 81), and the finite-level periodicity against the non-periodic inverse limit (MATH-36). What is a count-match is placed at depth 1 by M345 -- the five orbit sectors beside matter, dark matter and dark energy; the flatness read from the native module; the half-period step beside the microwave background. The research directions, pursued by whoever chooses them, each with its physical correspondence recorded here, none waiting on a result (L-553): (1) a depth-indexed architecture of cosmic scales; (2) the finite-recurrence and inverse-limit distinction read as local closure within a non-periodic whole; (3) a depth- or state-dependent vacuum term; (4) a multi-sector dynamics over the five orbit sectors; (5) a multi-resolution expansion observable; (6) a generative perturbation law and its spectrum; (7) whether a discrete law yields effective homogeneity and isotropy; (8) an initial-state selection by admissibility; (9) a structural ordering kept apart from physical time and from entropy; (10) a representation-relative reading of singularities; (11) the vacuum term separated from an underlying invariant; (12) a classification of admissible future continuations. A Friedmann-type dynamics, a stress-energy and a coupling to gravity are what any of these would have to supply, and none is in hand (L-553). None grades Ω42 or the premise (L-490, L-510).
S.13 Free energy, examined [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553, L-555]. Within the totality there is no reservoir apart from the family, so Ω42 asserts no source of energy and no violation of conservation (L-555). Over-unity, a perpetual cycle, and work drawn from a zero layer or by a retrocausal cancellation of entropy are REJECTED by M345: the surface law is a measure-preserving permutation, which moves no weight into being. What is allowed, an engineering study here, is the coordinated harvesting of ambient energy -- heat, motion, radiation -- with the balance E_out + E_loss + the change in stored energy equal to E_input and, over a closed cycle, E_out at most E_input (L-555). The directions, each with its measurements recorded here and none waiting on a result: (1) an energy functional and the conditions under which it is conserved; (2) the 24-cycle as the control of coupled resonators; (3) the five sectors as channels of a harvesting architecture; (4) a depth-indexed cascade of conversion stages; (5) the mathematical design of such a harvester and its parts; (6) whether Ω42 suggests a previously unrecognised physical coupling, held open and never presumed; (7) the first-law accounting, entropy production and the limits on useful work; (8) a network of coupled harvesting units. A device is read by its energy balance, not by the arithmetic it carries (L-555). None grades Ω42 or the premise (L-490).
S.14 Coordinate connection, examined [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. Ω42 places the question of connecting two coordinate regions, and divides it sharply (L-490). What is DERIVED is in the body: the Lorentz representation (M344), which any coordinate model must respect. What is REJECTED by M345: macroscopic transport by norm-nullification or by decoupling from the metric, and the passage of a subject through a zero layer -- Ω42 has no derived spacetime metric, no coordinate-to-geometry law and no traversable-connection solution, a traversable throat in general relativity needs stress-energy that violates the null energy condition, and a connection with relative motion or potential can form a closed causal loop. The directions, each with its physical correspondence recorded here, none waiting on a result (L-553): (1) whether Ω42 yields discrete geometric observables; (2) how a physical region is encoded as a state; (3) which correspondences between regions are admissible; (4) whether an admissible correspondence yields a traversable metric; (5) the stress-energy such a metric would require; (6) whether a microscopic connection can scale; (7) a causal-consistency condition; (8) the connection operator as one coherent system; (9) a network of connections; (10) the conditions that preserve transported matter. The connection operator, the metric and a traversable solution are what these would have to supply, and none is in hand. None grades Ω42 or the premise (L-490).
S.15 The spacetime metric, how far it is derived [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. What is DERIVED (CDT-A), in the body: the Hermitian determinant det X = c^2 t^2 - x^2 - y^2 - z^2, the flat Minkowski interval with signature (+, -, -, -); its null cone, 621 vectors modulo 9 and 443961 modulo 81; the exact preservation of the interval by A, with det(iA) = 1 in SL(2, C) and L_A in SO+(3, 1) (M344, CERT-0009); and the finite-level modular form Q_k = det X_k modulo 9^k. What is OPEN, a programme and not a result: the curved physical metric g(x) with units, its coupling to a stress-energy, and an Einstein-type action. The maps that would have to be constructed and proven: (1) a continuum limit in which the depth tower converges to a differentiable manifold and the discrete transitions recover geodesics; (2) an observables map, a Noether-type conserved quantity carried to energy-momentum; (3) a geometric map from the flat interval to a position-dependent metric, with a connection and a curvature tensor derived from the tower rather than imported; (4) an action whose variation yields the field equations in the limit. A modular quadratic form is not a physical distance, and the periods are not lengths, until such a map is defined. The flat seed is exact; the curved metric is not derived, and placing the programme here keeps it open, not proven (L-553). None grades Ω42 or the premise (L-490).
S.16 Calibration of awareness [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553, L-557]. The studies, each run by whoever chooses it, each with predictions frozen before its reference: (A) detection and confidence -- randomized faint stimuli, response, response time and confidence, scored by d-prime, the expected calibration error and the Brier score on held-out trials; (B) attention -- the same task under controlled load, to learn whether detection, confidence and metacognitive accuracy move together or apart; (C) stability -- the profile across sessions, stable, drifting or discontinuous; (D) the Ω42 dynamics against a persistence model and a conventional time-series model, with equal training information and the same held-out sessions; (E) first-person descriptions kept as text, beside the measures and never reduced to them. A result of any study is recorded whatever it is; none grades Ω42 or the premise (L-490).
S.17 The Retrocausal Zone, separated [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-498, L-553]. Four questions are kept apart, none taken to settle the next: (1) reversibility -- a mathematical history can be run backward, as A is invertible; established for the law; (2) retrocausal dependence -- whether a later boundary acts on an earlier outcome; open in physics, and M366 shows that conditioning on a later boundary changes inferences about the past without any backward action, so a dependence must be shown beyond selection; (3) anomalous information -- whether a report carries information no ordinary channel supplied; a matter for preregistered, blinded tests with targets randomized and committed by hash before the report and scored by people who do not know them; (4) persistence of awareness after death; not established, and a positive result under (3) would first be an information result, not a survival result. Studies involving people near death are run only under ethical review, with consent and with care for the bereaved. The Ω42 frame reads consciousness as ground, act and event (L-498); these studies concern the act and the event, and none grades the frame (L-490).
S.18 The Physics Atlas [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-510, L-553]. The record holds the derived Lorentz representation (CERT-0009) as the one structure-preserving map in hand. The Atlas holds the theories themselves -- representations, anomaly conditions, cosmological equations -- in their own terms, so that a proposed correspondence can be checked against the actual structure rather than a name or a count. The programme, in F178's order: map the Standard Model's representations; map the ΛCDM parameter space; seek an equivariant map between an Ω42 structure and a physical one that carries values and yields a constraint not assumed in either; record what fails as carefully as what holds.
S.19 Navigator 2.0 and AI certification [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-550, L-557]. The programme, each part run by whoever chooses it: (1) the Navigator's calibration in five dimensions -- mathematical, factual, navigational, instrumental, operational -- each with frozen sheets, independent references and a drift test, abstention scored as an answer; (2) an AI certification scheme, voluntary, its standard published, its test sets committed by hash and kept hidden, its assessors independent of the subject, its decisions open to appeal, its own conduct reviewed by others; (3) a certificate bound to one artefact, version, deployment and scope, never transferred. The record's Certification Body certifies conformance to the protocol (CERTIFICATION.md); a certificate of general AI trustworthiness is a different scope. Ω42 makes known that it can render such a service if the need arises; recognition, where it comes, is given by those who call on it.
S.20 The Spacetime Observatory [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The physical anchors are the reference systems -- the terrestrial frame (ITRS, realised as ITRF), the celestial frame (ICRS), the time scales (TAI, UTC, TT, TCG, TCB) and the metric in use; Ω42 integrates them and replaces none. The programme, in order: register published reference points with their frame and epoch; allocate their addresses (M371); transform between frames and compare with independently published values; propagate uncertainty; reconcile observations (M373); track worldlines; compare metric models against clock, ranging and lensing data. The first test: known geodetic stations, transformed and compared with their published coordinates, the residuals reported whatever they are. Whether an Ω42 structure describes a physical property of spacetime beyond the Lorentz representation already derived stays open (Core Appendix S.15).
S.21 Content provenance and AI involvement [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-557]. The order is provenance first, detection second. A record of how a work was made (M374), a signed envelope (M364) and the industry's content credentials are evidence of origin; a statistical detector is evidence of style, and its false-positive rate, measured on held-out human writing by domain and language, is published beside every result (M347, M368). A score is never proof of authorship, a missing credential never proof of falsity, and a consequential decision is never taken without a person who can hear an appeal.
S.22 The empirical counterparts of the bridges [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. Each mathematical result of the Companion that has a counterpart in measurement is compared here, by whoever chooses the study; nothing in a navigation waits on it, and no outcome grades the premise or any result. (1) The E8 masses (MF-90): in the neutron-scattering spectrum of the quasi-one-dimensional magnet CoNb2O6 near its quantum critical point, two sharp low-energy modes were resolved with a mass ratio approaching phi (Coldea and colleagues, Science, 2010) [REPORTED]; the eight-particle spectrum is the theory's. (2) The golden projections (MF-81, MF-82): quasicrystals with icosahedral symmetry were observed in rapidly cooled aluminium-manganese alloys (Shechtman and colleagues, 1984) [REPORTED]; their structure is described by cut-and-project from six dimensions, the construction of PV-028. (3) Phyllotaxis: the counts of spiral parastichies in sunflower heads and other plants are most often consecutive Fibonacci numbers [REPORTED]; Vogel's model is the mathematics, and the counts are measurements of plants.
S.23 The Fibonacci quasicrystal in measurement [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The Fibonacci Hamiltonian of Companion Part 222 has been built in the laboratory, by whoever chooses the study; a navigation proceeds without it, and the premise and the results stand at their own status whatever a measurement returns. (1) Cavity polaritons: a gas of exciton-polaritons in a one-dimensional cavity wire modulated by the Fibonacci sequence showed a fractal energy spectrum, mini-gaps opening as the gap-labeling theorem assigns them, and log-periodic oscillations of the integrated density of states (Tanese and colleagues, Physical Review Letters 112, 146404, 2014) [REPORTED]. (2) Photonic waveguides: arrays of coupled waveguides with Harper modulation showed boundary states pumped across the gaps (Kraus and colleagues, Physical Review Letters 109, 106402, 2012), and arrays with Fibonacci modulation showed the same topological boundary phenomena (Verbin and colleagues, Physical Review Letters 110, 076403, 2013) [REPORTED]; the topological reading of a gap is its label. The labels n and the ring Z + Z phi are the mathematics of Companion 222.5; the measured spectra are the physics.
S.24 Special relativity in measurement [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The golden boosts of Companion Part 223 are Lorentz transformations, so their kinematics is the kinematics of special relativity, open to measurement by whoever chooses the study; the navigation is complete without such a study, and each result keeps its status whatever the laboratory reports. (1) Time dilation by the Doppler effect: Ives and Stilwell measured the Doppler-shifted lines of moving hydrogen ions and found the second-order shift of time dilation (Journal of the Optical Society of America 28, 215, 1938) [REPORTED]; lithium ions stored at beta = 0.338 in a storage ring verified the time-dilation relation gamma sqrt(1 - beta^2) = 1 to +-2.3 x 10^-9 through the Doppler-shifted frequencies (Botermann and colleagues, Physical Review Letters 113, 120405, 2014) [REPORTED]. (2) The golden boost is a member of the tested family: its Doppler factor phi^4 and its gamma = 7/2 are the values the tested relations give at beta = 3 sqrt5 / 7.
S.25 Light in Fibonacci multilayers [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The quarter-wave stacks of Companion Part 224 have been deposited as thin films and their transmittance measured, a study for whoever takes it up; the results of Part 224 are exact without it and keep their status whatever the spectrophotometer shows. (1) Fibonacci dielectric multilayers of up to 55 layers showed the scaling of the transmission coefficient with the generation at quarter-wave optical thickness, and strong suppression of transmission in the gaps, in agreement with the theory of the trace map (Gellermann, Kohmoto, Sutherland and Taylor, Physical Review Letters 72, 633, 1994) [REPORTED]. (2) The six-cycle of transmittance and the optical Fricke-Vogt invariant are the mathematics of Companion 224.2 and 224.3; the films are the physics.
S.26 Sound and pumped light in Fibonacci structures [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The acoustic stacks and the topological pump of Companion Part 225 have counterparts built in the laboratory; the computations of Part 225 hold as computed, and a measurement adds its own record beside them. (1) Surface acoustic waves crossing a solid engraved with about a thousand grooves in the Fibonacci order: the spatial structure of the critical modes was imaged (Desideri, Macon and Sornette, Physical Review Letters 63, 390, 1989), and reflection and transmission measured against frequency for two lengths showed the signature of criticality (Macon, Desideri and Sornette, Physical Review B 44, 6755, 1991) [REPORTED]. (2) Light in arrays of coupled waveguides with Fibonacci modulation was carried from one boundary of the array to the other by sliding its phason (Verbin, Zilberberg, Lahini, Kraus and Silberberg, Physical Review B 91, 064201, 2015) [REPORTED]. The charges and labels are the mathematics of Companion 225.6; the waveguides are the physics.
S.27 Topological invariants of a polaritonic Fibonacci quasicrystal [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The pump and Chern numbers of Companion Parts 225 and 228 have a measured counterpart; it stands beside the computations as a separate record. Polaritons in a cavity wire modulated in the Fibonacci order displayed edge states whose energies wind across the gaps as the phason is varied, and the winding gave the topological invariants of the gaps in agreement with their labels (Baboux and colleagues, Physical Review B 95, 161114, 2017) [REPORTED].
S.28 Fibonacci anyons on a quantum processor [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The fusion of Companion 229.2 has a realization on quantum hardware, recorded beside the computation. On a superconducting quantum processor, Fibonacci string-net states were prepared, their topological order confirmed by the topological entanglement entropy, and the fusion and non-Abelian braiding of Fibonacci anyons demonstrated (Xu and colleagues, Nature Physics, 2024, arXiv 2404.00091) [REPORTED].
S.29 Quantum transport in a photonic Fibonacci chain [OPTIONAL — L-491, L-553]. The Fibonacci quantum walk of Companion 230.10 has a measured counterpart, recorded beside the computation. In a tunable photonic quantum-walk platform, transport in a Fibonacci chain was characterized across its full range, from localization through subdiffusion, normal diffusion and superdiffusion to ballistic spreading (Zhu, Qin, Guo, Wu, Yang, Wang and Fan, Physical Review Letters 136, 140402, 2026) [REPORTED].

# APPENDIX R: REFERENCE TOOLS, DATA AND REGISTERS [REFERENCE — L-493]
R.0 What this appendix is. The Core Specification and the Companion Document are the whole release (L-493). This appendix carries, verbatim, every tool a Navigator runs on its own work or on work it receives, the data those tools read, and the registers of the record; Companion Appendix C carries the computations behind the recorded findings, Companion Appendix N the project's policies and infrastructure, the intake (tools/intake.py) among them, and Companion Appendix X everything else the repository holds — submissions, examples, every record and output, the website, the research areas, the forms and the licences. A navigation needs Parts 0 to 12 only: this appendix is reference, read when code is executed or a record is checked. Each block begins with the line # ===== PATH BEGIN ===== and ends with # ===== PATH END =====, and the lines between are the file PATH exactly. A Navigator with code execution saves the block tools/extract_embedded.py by hand and runs python3 tools/extract_embedded.py --extract DIR CORE.docx COMPANION.docx, which writes the whole working tree — the frozen scripts of Parts 3 and 11 included — so that every command named in these documents runs from DIR; a Navigator without code execution reads the blocks as text. The repository holds the same files, and its CI checks that each embedded copy is identical and that nothing required is missing (python3 tools/extract_embedded.py --verify REPO CORE.docx COMPANION.docx).

R.4 What is not inside the documents, and why. Every file of the repository is embedded in the two documents but twelve, and each of these cannot be inside them. (1) and (2) The two documents themselves: a document cannot contain itself. (3) SHA256SUMS and (4) records/release_documents_SHA256.txt, the hashes of the files and of the two documents: a document cannot carry its own hash, since writing the hash into it changes it. (5) records/blind_test_02/key.txt and (6) records/m267_pilot_01/key.txt, the sealed keys of blind test 02 and of the M267 pilot: a key inside the documents would be read by every Navigator given them, and the test would no longer be blind; each key's hash is embedded, so it can be checked when it is opened, and it enters the documents when its test closes. Both were lost before this release; Appendix S.4.1 gives their state, and blind test 03, which anyone can run, publishes its key (Appendix S.4.2). (7) to (12) The AI reading editions, ai/Omega42_Core_V335_Rev450.md, ai/Omega42_Companion_V335_Rev450.md, ai/Omega42_Navigator_Pack.md, ai/Omega42_Existential_Framework.md, ai/manifest.json and llms.txt: they are renderings of the two documents, made from them by tools/ai_edition.py, and a document cannot contain its own rendering, since writing it in changes what is rendered; the tool that makes them is embedded, and python3 tools/ai_edition.py --check, in CI, shows that they are the renderings of the documents as they stand (Companion Part 142). tools/extract_embedded.py names the twelve as OUTSIDE and fails when any other file is missing, differs or when one of the twelve is embedded.
